You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** *Counselors at Law* One Vanderbilt Avenue, 44th Floor New York, New York 10017

Telephone: (212) 814-6000 Facsimile: (212) 814-6001 www.calderwoodharkness.com

October 9, 2023

**VIA EMAIL AND HAND DELIVERY**

Ardent Capital Management LLC 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, New York 10022

> Attention: Marcus Aldridge, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
>
> Priya Narayanan, Co-Founder & Managing Partner

Dear Mr. Aldridge and Ms. Narayanan:

We are pleased to confirm the engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness,\" the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") by Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"ManCo\" or the \"Client\") to serve as legal counsel in connection with the matters described herein. This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions upon which we will provide legal services to the Client in connection with this engagement.

**[1. Purpose and Engagement]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter confirms that Calderwood & Harkness has been engaged by the ManCo to serve as legal counsel in connection with a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$2.8 billion in total commitments. The ManCo is a Delaware limited liability company and a registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") under CRD #298417. The Fund\'s sole general partner is Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company.

The engagement encompasses the formation of new holding entities, the negotiation of separation arrangements with departing principals, the realignment of carried interest and management fee economics among continuing and next-generation principals, the solicitation of necessary limited partner consents, compliance with existing side-letter obligations, and related tax structuring. The scope of the representation, the personnel assigned to the engagement, the fee arrangement, and other terms and conditions governing this engagement are set forth in the sections that follow.

**[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

The engagement will comprise the following principal workstreams, each of which is described in greater detail below. We understand that the scope of the engagement may evolve as the restructuring progresses; any material expansion of the scope described herein will be discussed with the Client in advance.

**2.1 Entity Restructuring**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the restructuring of the organizational hierarchy of the Ardent Capital platform, including:

\(a\) Advising on the formation of a new Delaware limited liability company, to be named Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\"), which will serve as a parent holding company for both the General Partner and the ManCo, thereby consolidating the principals\' economic interests and governance rights in a single vehicle at the top of the organizational structure.

\(b\) Advising on the formation of an intermediate entity, Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\"), as a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo and the sole member of the General Partner. GP Intermediate will serve as an interposing entity between HoldCo and the General Partner, facilitating the allocation of carried interest economics and providing structural flexibility for the admission of future principals and the potential establishment of successor funds.

\(c\) Drafting and negotiating limited liability company agreements for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including provisions governing capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, distribution waterfalls, governance (including voting and consent requirements), transfer restrictions, withdrawal and removal mechanics, non-compete and non-solicitation covenants, and such other provisions as may be appropriate.

\(d\) Preparing amended and restated limited liability company agreements for the General Partner and the ManCo to reflect the new holding-company structure, including modifications to membership interest provisions, management and officer provisions, and capital account and allocation provisions necessitated by the interposition of HoldCo and GP Intermediate.

\(e\) Preparing and filing Certificates of Formation with the Delaware Secretary of State for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, together with any ancillary filings or registrations required in connection with the formation and qualification of such entities.

\(f\) Preparing Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund (the \"LPA\") to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner, including any required modifications to the definitions, representations, and governance provisions of the LPA necessitated by the interposition of GP Intermediate and HoldCo above the General Partner.

**2.2 Economics Realignment**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the reallocation and documentation of the economic arrangements among the principals of the Fund, including:

\(a\) Advising on the reallocation of carried interest percentages and management fee profit-share allocations among the remaining and next-generation principals, taking into account the departure of the principals described in Section 2.3 below, the contributions of continuing principals, and the Firm\'s understanding of the Client\'s objectives with respect to the incentivization and retention of key personnel.

\(b\) Drafting an amended and restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement reflecting the revised carried interest percentages applicable to each principal, including vesting schedules, forfeiture and clawback provisions, and mechanics for the allocation of carried interest among HoldCo members through the GP Intermediate and General Partner chain.

\(c\) Drafting a Management Fee Sharing and Profit Allocation Agreement at the HoldCo level, setting forth the allocation of management fee revenue among HoldCo members, including base compensation allocations, discretionary bonus pools, and distribution priorities.

\(d\) Revising the co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal group and to address any changes in co-investment rights and priorities resulting from the restructuring.

**2.3 Departing Principal Separation**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the negotiation and documentation of separation arrangements for two departing principals:

\(a\) **David Kellner** (Senior Partner), who is retiring from the Ardent Capital platform; and

\(b\) **Joanna Trask** (Partner), who is departing voluntarily.

In connection with each departing principal, the Firm will:

> \(i\) Draft comprehensive separation and release agreements, addressing, among other things, the departing principal\'s resignation from all positions with the ManCo, the General Partner, HoldCo (if applicable), and all affiliated entities; mutual releases of claims; confidentiality, non-disparagement, non-solicitation, and (as applicable) non-competition covenants; cooperation obligations; and any ongoing compensation or benefits arrangements.
>
> \(ii\) Draft carry retention and clawback side letters, specifying the portion of carried interest to be retained by each departing principal with respect to investments made during his or her tenure, the clawback obligations applicable thereto, and the mechanics for the calculation and payment of any retained carry distributions.
>
> \(iii\) As applicable, draft a senior advisor agreement in favor of Mr. Kellner, setting forth the terms of any ongoing advisory role, including the scope of services, compensation, expense reimbursement, and termination provisions.
>
> \(iv\) Coordinate, as necessary and appropriate, with Whitford & Chase LLP, counsel to the departing principals, led by Richard Beaulieu, Esq., in connection with the negotiation and finalization of all separation documentation.

**2.4 LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on all limited partner notification, consent, and compliance matters arising from the restructuring, including:

\(a\) Preparing materials for notification to, and solicitation of consent from, the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, including a detailed memorandum describing the restructuring and its implications for the Fund and its limited partners.

**Date of Conflicts Search.** The initial conflicts search was run on March 31, 2025. A supplemental search was run on April 1, 2025, to capture any matters or parties entered into the Firm\'s systems between the close of business on March 31 and the morning of April 1, 2025.

**Systems Searched.** Both searches were conducted using Calderwood & Harkness LLP\'s proprietary conflicts database (the \"C&H Conflicts System\"), which covers all current and former clients, adverse parties, related entities, and key personnel across all of the Firm\'s domestic and international offices. The C&H Conflicts System is maintained by the Firm\'s Conflicts Department and is updated in real time as new matters are opened, new parties are identified, and existing matters are closed. The search was conducted against all active, inactive, and archived matter records, as well as the Firm\'s lateral hire conflicts records and the personal conflict disclosure records of all partners and counsel in the Funds & Asset Management practice group.

He serves in an equivalent capacity for all affiliated Ardent Capital entities.

Mr. Aldridge is designated as a \"Key Person\" under Section 5.2 of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Ardent Capital Partners III LP. In this role, Mr. Aldridge is required to devote substantially all of his business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund, and any cessation of his active involvement in the Fund\'s investment activities would constitute a Key Person Event under the LPA, which would trigger a suspension of the investment period.

In connection with the restructuring of the Ardent Capital platform, Mr. Aldridge serves as a Managing Member of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC, in which he holds a 42% membership interest. === documents/matters/1001-00002/Structuring & Analysis/restructuring-options-memo.docx ===

The Fund provides for a carried interest of 20% of net profits, subject to an 8% preferred return and a full catch-up allocation to the General Partner. The carried interest is allocated among the GP\'s members in proportion to their respective membership interests in the GP.

The Fund\'s Limited Partnership Agreement (the \"LPA\") provides for a 100% joint and several clawback obligation among the GP membactively. In particular, the presentation should emphasize the promotion of Marchetti and Okonkwo as evidence of the platform\'s depth of talent and its commitment to next-generation leadership development.

**3. Section 8.3 --- Transfer of GP Interest**

Section 8.3 of the LPA governs transfers of the General Partner\'s interest in the Fund. The interposition of GP Intermediate as the sole member of the GP --- which effectively changes the ownership of the GP from five individual principals to a single-entity member (GP Intermediate, itself wholly owned by HoldCo) --- constitutes a transfer of GP interest for purposes of Section 8.3. This transfer is permissible under Section 8.3 with LPAC consent.

Importantly, the ultimate beneficial owners of the GP remain the same individuals --- the principals of the Ardent platform --- who hold their interests through the HoldCo structure rather than directly. This is a structural reorganization of the ownership chain, not a change of control. The LPAC consent solicitation should emphasize this point and make clear that the restructuring does not alter the identity of the individuals responsible for the management of the Fund.

**4. Section 9.7 --- Removal of GP**

Section 9.7 of the LPA provides for the removal of the General Partner under specified circumstances, including a supermajority vote of the limited partners following certain triggering events. The restructuring contemplated by Option B does not involve the removal of the GP. Ardent Capital GP III LLC remains as the sole general partner of the Fund throughout the restructuring and at all times thereafter. Only the ownership of the GP changes --- from direct individual membership to indirect ownership through GP Intermediate and HoldCo. Accordingly, Section 9.7 is not implicated by the restructuring.

**5. Side-Letter Compliance**

A comprehensive side-letter compliance analysis is required in connection with the restructuring. Based on our preliminary review, the relevant side-letter provisions can be categorized as follows:

**Material-change consent provisions (4 side letters).** The side letters with Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System, Pinnacle Insurance Group, Crestwood Endowment Partners, and Haverford Capital Partners each require prior written notice and, in certain cases, affirmative consent for any \"material change in the management structure\" of the Fund. The restructuring will constitute a material change for purposes of these provisions, and prior written notice and (where required) affirmative consent must be obtained from each of these LPs before the restructuring is executed. We recommend that these notices be sent concurrently with the LPAC consent solicitation and that follow-up communications be coordinated with the LPAC presentation.

=== documents/matters/1001-00002/Structuring & Analysis/section-704-analysis-memo.docx ===

**A. Pre-Restructuring Organizational Structure**

**The Fund.** Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\") is a Delaware limited partnership formed in 2019 for the purpose of making private equity investments in middle-market companies across the technology, healthcare, and business services sectors. The Fund has aggregate capital commitments of \$2,800,000,000 from forty-seven limited partners, consisting of institutional investors including public and private pension funds, endowments, sovereign wealth funds, insurance companies, and family offices. As of the date of this memorandum, the Fund has called approximately 70% of committed capital, or approximately \$1,960,000,000, and has invested approximately \$1,880,000,000 across eleven active portfolio companies. The Fund\'s investment period runs through June 30, 2025, and the Fund\'s stated term expires on December 31, 2029, subject to two one-year extensions at the discretion of the GP (with Advisory Committee approval for the second extension). The Fund is subject to an 8% compounding preferred return hurdle and a 100% GP catch-up, after which the GP is entitled to a 20% carried interest.

**The GP.** Ardent Capital GP III LLC is a Delaware limited liability company that serves as the sole general partner of the Fund. The GP has made a 1.5% general partner commitment to the Fund in the amount of \$42,000,000. As of the date of this memorandum, the GP has funded approximately 70% of its commitment, or \$29,400,000. The GP\'s membership interests are held directly by the five senior principals in the following percentages: Marcus Aldridge (35%), Priya Narayanan (30%), David Kellner (15%), Joanna Trask (12%), and Robert Hsiao (8%). The GP is classified as a partnership for federal income tax purposes under the default classification rules of Treasury Regulations Section 301.7701-3. The GP is the entity entitled to receive the 20% carried interest from the Fund, which it distributes to its members in accordance with their respective membership percentages.

--

In the Ardent Capital Restructuring, the shift from a 35/30/15/12/8 ownership structure to a 42/36/14/4/4 structure reflects the genuine commercial bargaining associated with the departure of two senior principals and the promotion of two junior professionals. The reallocation of economics is driven by succession planning, talent retention, and governance realignment --- not by a desire to achieve tax benefits. The economics of each member\'s interest (share of carried interest, management fee profit share, GP capital returns, and exposure to clawback and indemnification obligations) are all affected by the reallocation, and the dollar amounts to be received by each partner will differ materially from what they would have received under the prior structure.

We have considered whether the allocation of built-in gain from the contributed property to the contributing partners (as required by Section 704(c)) could be viewed as a \"shifting allocation\" that benefits the non-contributing partners (Marchetti and Okonkwo). However, the Section 704(c) allocation is mandated by statute and regulation and is specifically designed to prevent the shifting of pre-contribution gain. Compliance with Section 704(c) is not evidence of an abusive shifting allocation; to the contrary, it is evidence that the partnership is properly implementing the requirements of the Code. Accordingly, we conclude that the allocations in the HoldCo LLC Agreement should satisfy the substantiality requirement.

**[V. SECTION 704(c) ANALYSIS --- BUILT-IN GAIN AND LOSS ALLOCATION]{.underline}**

--

> \"An allocation method (or combination of methods) is not reasonable if the contribution of property (or event that results in reverse section 704(c) allocations) and the corresponding allocation of tax items with respect to the property are made with a view to shifting the tax consequences of built-in gain or loss among the partners in a manner that substantially reduces the present value of the partners\' aggregate tax liability.\"

We have considered whether the Restructuring could be viewed as having been designed, in whole or in part, to shift the tax consequences of built-in gain from the contributing partners (Aldridge, Narayanan, and Hsiao) to the non-contributing members (Marchetti and Okonkwo) in a manner that would reduce aggregate tax liability. We conclude that the anti-abuse rule should not apply for the following reasons:

First, the Restructuring is driven by legitimate, non-tax business purposes. The primary motivations for the Restructuring are succession planning (the departure of Kellner and Trask and the promotion of Marchetti and Okonkwo), governance consolidation (centralizing ownership through a single holding company), and liability management (interposition of GP Intermediate to insulate HoldCo from Fund-level liabilities). These are genuine commercial objectives that would exist regardless of any tax considerations.

--

**C. Section 704(c)(1)(B) --- Distribution of Contributed Property within 7 Years**

Section 704(c)(1)(B) of the Code provides that if a contributing partner contributes property with built-in gain to a partnership, and the partnership distributes that property to another partner within seven years of the contribution, the contributing partner must recognize the pre-contribution built-in gain at the time of the distribution (to the extent not already recognized). This provision is designed to prevent partners from using partnerships to circumvent the contribution rules --- contributing appreciated property to a partnership and then engineering a distribution of that property to another partner to shift the gain.

In the Ardent Capital Restructuring, the contributed properties are the GP and ManCo membership interests. If, within seven years of the contribution, HoldCo were to distribute the GP interest (or the ManCo interest) to a HoldCo member other than the contributing partner who originally contributed that interest (e.g., if HoldCo distributed the GP interest to Marchetti or Okonkwo), the contributing partners (Aldridge, Narayanan, and Hsiao) would be required to recognize their respective shares of the pre-contribution built-in gain under Section 704(c)(1)(B).

--

**Transitional Year (2024).** The 2024 taxable year will be a transitional year requiring split-period reporting. Kellner and Trask will receive K-1s from the GP and ManCo reflecting their respective shares of income through their departure dates (March 31, 2024 for Kellner and April 15, 2024 for Trask). The remaining partners will receive K-1s reflecting their income for the full year, with allocations adjusted to reflect the pre-Restructuring ownership (through the Restructuring effective date) and the post-Restructuring ownership (from the Restructuring effective date through December 31, 2024). The GP and ManCo will need to perform an interim closing of the books as of the Restructuring effective date to properly allocate income between the pre- and post-Restructuring periods.

**EINs for New Entities.** HoldCo (EIN 93-1847225) and GP Intermediate (EIN 93-1847231) will need to file informational returns (Form 1065 for HoldCo; Form 8832 entity classification election or disregarded entity information, as applicable, for GP Intermediate) beginning with the 2024 tax year. The EIN applications have been submitted and the EINs have been assigned.

**[VIII. QUANTITATIVE ILLUSTRATION --- BUILT-IN GAIN LAYERS]{.underline}**

**[II. Background and Factual Assumptions]{.underline}**

The following factual background and assumptions are based on information provided by the client and our review of the governing documents of the Fund, the GP, and the ManCo, including the Fund\'s Second Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership dated as of April 15, 2019 (the \"LPA\"), the GP\'s Amended and Restated Limited Liability Company Agreement dated as of January 18, 2019 (the \"GP LLC Agreement\"), and the ManCo\'s Amended and Restated Limited Liability Company Agreement dated as of January 18, 2019 (the \"ManCo LLC Agreement\"). We have also reviewed draft term sheets for the proposed restructuring provided by Marcus Aldridge on behalf of the principals.

**[A. Existing Structure]{.underline}**

--

The Fund\'s most recent quarterly valuation as of September 30, 2023 reflects an aggregate gross multiple of invested capital (\"MOIC\") of 1.42x, a net internal rate of return (\"IRR\") of 14.7%, and aggregate unrealized value of approximately \$2.33 billion. These figures are relevant to the determination of built-in gain in the contributed interests, as discussed in Sections IV and V below.

The Fund\'s term expires on December 31, 2029, subject to two one-year extensions at the discretion of the GP. The investment period under the LPA ends on June 30, 2025, after which the GP may not make new investments but may make follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies and fund capital calls for expenses and reserves.

The GP --- Ardent Capital GP III LLC (EIN 84-3291063) --- is a Delaware limited liability company. Under the current GP LLC Agreement, the five senior principals of the firm hold direct membership interests in the GP. The GP serves as the sole general partner of the Fund and is responsible for the management and control of the Fund\'s business and affairs.

--

**Carried Interest.** The Fund provides for carried interest of 20% of net profits (after return of contributed capital and payment of expenses), subject to an 8% per annum preferred return to the limited partners and a 100% GP catch-up until the GP has received 20% of cumulative net profits. Carried interest is allocated among the principals in the same percentages as their membership interests in the GP. As of September 30, 2023, the Fund has accrued carried interest of approximately \$87.6 million, which has not yet been distributed. The accrued carried interest is attributable to unrealized appreciation in the Fund\'s portfolio companies and is subject to change based on subsequent valuations.

The Fund\'s LPA provides for a 100% joint and several clawback obligation among the GP members, with an individual escrow requirement of 30% of all carried interest distributions. Each principal\'s escrow balance is proportionate to their share of distributed carry.

**Management Fees.** The ManCo charges the Fund a management fee equal to 1.75% of committed capital during the investment period, yielding annual management fee revenue of approximately \$49 million (\$2.8 billion × 1.75%). After the expiration of the investment period on June 30, 2025, the management fee steps down to 1.50% of invested capital (net of write-offs and realizations). The ManCo\'s profit share --- that is, the portion of management fee revenue distributed to the principals as equity owners --- is approximately 35% of fee revenue, or approximately \$17.15 million per year. The remaining approximately 65% of fee revenue (\$31.85 million) is used to fund the ManCo\'s operating expenses, including employee compensation, rent, technology, travel, and other overhead costs.

--

Section 721(b) provides an exception to the general nonrecognition rule of Section 721(a). Under Section 721(b), the nonrecognition rule does not apply to gain realized on a transfer of property to a partnership that would be treated as an investment company (within the meaning of Section 351) if the partnership were incorporated. Under Section 351(e) and Treasury Regulations Section 1.351-1(c), an investment company is a transferee that, after the transfer, holds more than 80% of its assets in stocks, securities, and certain other investment-type assets, and the transfer results in diversification of the transferors\' interests.

This exception is designed to prevent taxpayers from using the partnership formation rules to achieve a tax-free diversification of investment portfolios. The exception is inapplicable to the proposed restructuring because HoldCo is being formed to hold operating management company interests and a general partner interest in an operating private equity fund, not to pool diversified investment assets. The GP and ManCo interests are interests in operating businesses --- the GP manages the Fund\'s portfolio companies and the ManCo provides investment advisory services --- and are not stocks, securities, or other passive investment assets within the meaning of Section 351(e).

Accordingly, we conclude that Section 721(b) does not apply to the formation of HoldCo.

--

**[IV. Basis and Holding Period Consequences]{.underline}**

The tax-free treatment of the HoldCo formation under Section 721(a) is accompanied by a system of carryover and substituted basis rules designed to preserve the built-in gain or loss in the contributed property for future recognition. These rules are set forth in Sections 722, 723, and 1223 of the Code.

**[A. Basis of Contributed Property --- Section 723]{.underline}**

--

Several factors contribute to the potential book-tax disparity in the contributed interests. First, the Fund\'s accrued carried interest of \$87.6 million as of September 30, 2023 represents a significant component of the GP\'s fair market value that may not be fully reflected in the contributing principals\' tax bases. Second, the Fund\'s unrealized portfolio value of approximately \$2.33 billion, to the extent reflected in the GP\'s interest in the Fund, contributes to the value of the GP interest. Third, the ManCo\'s ongoing management fee revenue stream of approximately \$49 million per year, and the associated going-concern value of the ManCo as a registered investment adviser, may result in a fair market value of the ManCo interests that exceeds their adjusted tax bases.

The Section 704(b) and 704(c) rules are designed to ensure that (i) book allocations of partnership items correspond to the economic deal among the partners, and (ii) tax allocations of built-in gain or loss are properly assigned to the contributing partner who contributed the property with built-in gain or loss, rather than being shifted to non-contributing partners.

**[B. Section 704(b) --- Book Allocations]{.underline}**

--

If Kellner retains a continuing profits interest, his retirement does not trigger a complete liquidation of his partnership interest under Section 736. Instead, his retirement constitutes a partial liquidation --- his capital interest and his share of management fee economics are liquidated, while his profits interest (carry) continues. The partial liquidation of his capital interest is governed by Section 736, but the continuing profits interest remains subject to the ordinary partnership allocation and distribution rules of Subchapter K.

The carry escrow of \$3,942,000 (30% of \$13.14 million) remains in place for three years post-retirement, as required by the Fund\'s LPA. Amounts held in escrow are generally not treated as distributed to the partner until actually or constructively received. The escrow does not change Kellner\'s basis in his partnership interest until the escrowed amounts are released. Upon release, the amounts are treated as partnership distributions under Section 731.

**[D. Clawback Obligation]{.underline}**

Kellner\'s clawback obligation continues for three years following his retirement. Under the Fund\'s LPA, Kellner is jointly and severally liable with the other GP members for any clawback obligation owed to the limited partners. The clawback obligation is a contingent liability that does not create current income or deduction for any party. The obligation is only triggered if the Fund\'s aggregate returns decline below the level at which the GP would be entitled to the carried interest previously distributed.

Upon any actual clawback payment by Kellner, the payment would be treated as a contribution back to the partnership, increasing Kellner\'s outside basis in his partnership interest. If Kellner has previously recognized gain on carry distributions, the clawback payment may give rise to a loss or a refund claim, subject to the applicable statute of limitations and the specific provisions of the partnership agreement governing clawback mechanics.

--

Trask will retain 60% of her vested carried interest, valued at \$6,307,200. The analysis of Trask\'s retained carry parallels the analysis of Kellner\'s retained carry in Section VI.C above. Trask retains a continuing profits interest in the GP/Fund for her retained carry, and she is not treated as fully liquidating her partnership interest. Her departure constitutes a partial liquidation of her capital interest and management fee economics, with a continuing profits interest for the retained carry.

**Carry Escrow Adjustment.** Trask\'s carry escrow will be adjusted to reflect her reduced retained carry. Under the Fund\'s LPA, the escrow requirement is 30% of carried interest distributions. Trask\'s adjusted escrow obligation is \$1,892,160 (30% of \$6,307,200). Trask\'s existing escrow balance is \$3,150,000 (reflecting 30% of her total vested carry of \$10,512,000, assuming all accrued carry has been escrowed). The excess of the existing escrow balance over the adjusted requirement is \$1,257,840 (\$3,150,000 minus \$1,892,160).

The release of the excess escrow amount of \$1,257,840 constitutes a distribution to Trask from the partnership. Under IRC Section 731(a)(1), gain is not recognized on a partnership distribution to the extent the distribution does not exceed the partner\'s outside basis in the partnership interest. If the distribution of \$1,257,840 does not exceed Trask\'s outside basis, no gain is recognized. If the distribution exceeds her outside basis, the excess is recognized as gain (generally capital gain under Section 731(a)(1)). A determination of Trask\'s outside basis as of the distribution date will be necessary to evaluate this issue.

--

The proposed restructuring involves the formation of two new entities, each of which requires a separate federal employer identification number and a determination of its tax classification:

**Ardent Capital Holdings LLC.** HoldCo has been assigned EIN 93-1847225. HoldCo will be organized as a Delaware limited liability company with multiple members (Aldridge, Narayanan, Hsiao, Marchetti, and Okonkwo). Under Treasury Regulations Section 301.7701-3(b)(1)(i), a domestic eligible entity with two or more members is classified as a partnership for federal income tax purposes unless it elects to be classified as an association taxable as a corporation. HoldCo will not make such an election and will therefore be classified as a partnership. As a partnership, HoldCo will not be subject to entity-level federal income tax. All items of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit will flow through to the HoldCo members on their respective Schedule K-1s. HoldCo will be required to file Form 1065 (U.S. Return of Partnership Income) annually.

**Ardent GP Intermediate LLC.** GP Intermediate has been assigned EIN 93-1847231. GP Intermediate will be organized as a Delaware limited liability company with a single member (HoldCo). Under Treasury Regulations Section 301.7701-3(b)(1)(ii), a domestic eligible entity with a single owner is classified as a disregarded entity for federal income tax purposes unless it elects to be classified as an association taxable as a corporation. GP Intermediate will not make such an election and will therefore be treated as a disregarded entity. As a disregarded entity, GP Intermediate will not file a separate tax return. All items of GP Intermediate will be treated as items of HoldCo for federal income tax purposes, and the GP interest held by GP Intermediate will be treated as owned directly by HoldCo.

**Existing Entities.** The existing entities --- the Fund (EIN 84-3291057), the GP (EIN 84-3291063), and the ManCo (EIN 84-3291070) --- retain their existing EINs. However, the GP\'s tax classification will change as a result of the restructuring. Prior to the restructuring, the GP is a multi-member LLC (with five individual members) classified as a partnership. Following the restructuring, the GP will be a single-member LLC (sole member: GP Intermediate, which is itself a disregarded entity owned by HoldCo). A single-member LLC is classified as a disregarded entity under Treasury Regulations Section 301.7701-3(b)(1)(ii). Accordingly, the GP will transition from filing its own partnership return (Form 1065) to being a disregarded entity, with all GP-level items flowing through to HoldCo.

--

7\. **Section 752 Analysis.** A complete analysis of the impact of the GP commitment reallocations must be prepared. The combined unfunded commitments of Kellner (\$1,890,000) and Trask (\$1,512,000), totaling \$3,402,000, will be assumed by the remaining HoldCo members. The Section 752 implications of this reallocation --- including the potential deemed distributions to Kellner and Trask and the resulting impact on their outside basis --- require detailed analysis that will be provided under separate cover.

8\. **Timing of Execution.** All restructuring documents --- including the HoldCo LLC Agreement, the GP Intermediate LLC Agreement, the contribution and assignment agreements, the Trask separation agreement, and the Kellner Senior Advisor Agreement --- should be executed prior to Kellner\'s retirement date of March 31, 2024, and Trask\'s departure date of April 15, 2024, to ensure proper tax treatment of all restructuring transactions. We recommend targeting execution of all documents by no later than March 15, 2024, to allow for administrative processing and filing.

**HARROWGATE PRIVATE EQUITY FUND V LP**

This Agreement of Limited Partnership (this **\"Agreement\"**) of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the **\"Partnership\"** or the **\"Fund\"**), is entered into as of the date of the First Close (as defined below) by and among Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as the general partner (the **\"General Partner\"** or **\"GP\"**), and each Person who is admitted as a limited partner of the Partnership (each, a **\"Limited Partner\"** or **\"LP\"** and, collectively, the **\"Limited Partners\"**), in each case in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth herein. The General Partner and the Limited Partners are sometimes referred to herein individually as a **\"Partner\"** and collectively as the **\"Partners.\"**

**RECITALS**

--

**WHEREAS**, the Sponsor has sponsored and managed four predecessor private equity funds (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund I LP through Harrowgate Private Equity Fund IV LP) and manages approximately \$5.8 billion in aggregate assets under management as of the date hereof;

**WHEREAS**, each Limited Partner desires to make a capital commitment to the Partnership on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement and in the Subscription Agreement executed by such Limited Partner; and

**WHEREAS**, the Partners desire to set forth their respective rights, obligations, and duties with respect to the Partnership.

--

**\"Benefit Plan Investor\"** means a \"benefit plan investor\" as defined in 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101(f)(2), as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA, including (a) any \"employee benefit plan\" as defined in Section 3(3) of ERISA that is subject to Part 4 of Subtitle B of Title I of ERISA, (b) any \"plan\" as defined in Section 4975(e)(1) of the Code that is subject to Section 4975 of the Code, and (c) any entity whose underlying assets include \"plan assets\" by reason of a plan\'s investment in such entity.

**\"Blocker Entity\"** means HGF V blocker Corp., a Delaware C corporation formed for the benefit of certain tax-exempt or non-U.S. Limited Partners to mitigate UBTI or effectively connected income concerns, as the General Partner may determine to be appropriate in connection with the Fund\'s investment program.

**\"Bridge Financing\"** means any short-term Fund-level borrowing (whether under the Subscription Credit Facility or otherwise) used to fund Portfolio Investments or other Partnership obligations in advance of or in lieu of issuing Capital Calls, which borrowing shall not remain outstanding for more than one hundred eighty (180) consecutive days from the date of the applicable borrowing.

--

**\"Distribution\"** means any distribution of cash, securities, or other property by the Partnership to one or more Partners, whether as a return of capital, a share of income or gain, or otherwise, as determined by the General Partner in accordance with this Agreement.

**\"Early Close discount\"** means the ten (10) basis point reduction in the Management Fee rate applicable to Limited Partners admitted to the Partnership at the First Close, as described in Section 7.1(c) of this Agreement (resulting in a Management Fee rate of 1.65% per annum on Capital Commitments during the Investment Period, in lieu of 1.75%).

**\"ERISA\"** means the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto, together with all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

--

**\"Final Close\"** means the last date on which Limited Partners may be admitted to the Partnership and Capital Commitments accepted, which date shall be no later than the Final Close Deadline.

**\"Final Close Deadline\"** means February 15, 2027, being eighteen (18) months after the target date of the First Close.

**\"First Close\"** means the initial closing of Capital Commitments to the Partnership, targeted for August 15, 2025, at which the General Partner shall have accepted Capital Commitments aggregating at least Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$750,000,000) (or such lesser amount as the General Partner may determine in its sole discretion).

**\"Fiscal Year\"** means the calendar year commencing on January 1 and ending on December 31 of each year; *provided*, that the first Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall commence on the date of the First Close and shall end on December 31 of such calendar year, and the final Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall end on the date of the final distribution of all Partnership assets and cancellation of the Certificate of Limited Partnership.

**\"For-Cause Removal\"** means the removal of the General Partner for Cause by a vote of a majority in interest of the Limited Partners (excluding GP-affiliated Capital Commitments) in accordance with Section 12.6(b).

--

**\"Included Investors\"** means those Limited Partners that are (a) investment-grade institutional investors (as determined by the lender under the Subscription Credit Facility), (b) government plan investors, or (c) such other investors as may be included in the borrowing base under the Subscription Credit Facility, in each case whose unfunded Capital Commitments are pledged to secure such facility.

**\"Independent Auditor\"** means Caldwell, Fitch & Hartley LLP, or such other independent certified public accounting firm of national or regional standing as the General Partner may select from time to time, subject to LPAC approval for any change in the Independent Auditor.

**\"Investment Company Act\"** means the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto, together with all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

--

**\"Key Person Event\"** means the occurrence of either Key Person ceasing to devote substantially all of his or her business time and professional efforts to the investment activities of the Fund and its Parallel Funds (excluding reasonable time devoted to (i) management and wind-down of predecessor funds (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund I LP through Harrowgate Private Equity Fund IV LP), (ii) civic, charitable, and educational activities, and (iii) personal investment activities that do not conflict with or detract from the Fund\'s investment activities), whether due to death, permanent disability, voluntary departure, termination, or otherwise, as more fully described in Article X.

**\"Large LP discount\"** means the additional five (5) basis point reduction in the Management Fee rate applicable to Limited Partners committing One Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$150,000,000) or more to the Partnership, as described in Section 7.1(c) of this Agreement (resulting in a cumulative Management Fee rate of 1.60% per annum during the Investment Period for a First Close Limited Partner committing \$150,000,000 or more).

**\"Limited Partner\"** or **\"LP\"** means each Person admitted to the Partnership as a limited partner in accordance with Article III of this Agreement and the Act, and **\"Limited Partners\"** means all such Persons collectively. For the avoidance of doubt, the term \"Limited Partner\" does not include the General Partner, except to the extent the General Partner holds an interest in the Partnership in its capacity as a limited partner (if applicable).

**\"Limited Partner Advisory Committee\"** or **\"LPAC\"** means the advisory committee of Limited Partner representatives established and maintained by the General Partner in accordance with Article XI of this Agreement.

**\"Management Fee\"** means the fee payable by the Partnership to the General Partner or its designee in consideration for the management and advisory services provided by the General Partner and its Associates to the Partnership, as set forth in Section 7.1 of this Agreement.

--

**\"Sponsor\"** means Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, the sole member of the General Partner and the management company responsible for the investment advisory and management services provided to the Fund and its parallel vehicles.

**\"Subscription Agreement\"** means the subscription agreement and related documents executed by each Limited Partner in connection with such Limited Partner\'s commitment to the Partnership, in the form attached hereto as Exhibit D (or as otherwise prescribed by the General Partner), together with all exhibits, schedules, questionnaires, and certifications attached thereto.

**\"Subscription Credit Facility\"** means any revolving credit facility, letter of credit facility, or similar borrowing arrangement established by the Partnership (or a parallel vehicle) that is secured, in whole or in part, by the unfunded Capital Commitments of the Partners, as more fully described in Section 4.8 of this Agreement.

**\"Subscription Facility Limit\"** means an amount equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of the aggregate unfunded Capital Commitments of all Partners at the time of determination, being the maximum aggregate principal amount of borrowings permitted to be outstanding under the Subscription Credit Facility at any given time, as further described in Section 4.8.

**\"Subsequent Close\"** means any closing of Capital Commitments to the Partnership occurring after the First Close and on or prior to the Final Close Deadline, at which additional Limited Partners may be admitted to the Partnership and/or existing Limited Partners may increase their Capital Commitments, in accordance with Section 3.4 of this Agreement.

**\"Transaction Fees\"** means all transaction fees, monitoring fees, directors\' fees, advisory fees, consulting fees, break-up fees, topping fees, and similar fees and compensation received by the General Partner, the Sponsor, or any of their respective Affiliates from or in connection with Portfolio Companies or prospective Portfolio Companies (net of any unreimbursed out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection therewith).

--

**[Section 2.1 --- Formation]{.underline}**

The Partnership has been formed as a limited partnership under and pursuant to the Act by the filing (or the contemplated filing on or prior to the date of the First Close) of a Certificate of Limited Partnership with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware. The Certificate of Limited Partnership identifies Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC as the sole general partner of the Partnership. The registered office of the Partnership in the State of Delaware is located at 400 South Ashbury Asset Advisors, Suite 3000, Wilmington, Delaware 19801, in care of Calderwood & Harkness LLP, which serves as the registered agent of the Partnership for service of process in the State of Delaware. The General Partner shall cause such amendments to the Certificate of Limited Partnership and such other filings and recordings as may be required or appropriate under the Act and the laws of any other jurisdiction in which the Partnership conducts business.

**[Section 2.2 --- Name]{.underline}**

--

\(b\) The General Partner may, in its sole discretion, extend the Fund Term for up to two (2) consecutive periods of one (1) year each by providing written notice to the Limited Partners at least ninety (90) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Fund Term (each, a **\"GP Extension\"**).

\(c\) Following the expiration of any GP Extension, the Fund Term may be further extended for one (1) additional period of one (1) year with the prior approval of the LPAC (the **\"LPAC Extension\"**). The General Partner shall request such LPAC approval in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the expiration of the last GP Extension.

\(d\) During any extension period, the General Partner shall focus primarily on the orderly realization and disposition of remaining Portfolio Investments and the distribution of proceeds to the Partners. No new Portfolio Investments shall be made during any extension period (other than follow-on investments in existing Portfolio Companies that are necessary to protect or enhance the value of such investments).

--

**[Section 2.8 --- Fiscal Year]{.underline}**

The Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall be the calendar year, commencing on January 1 and ending on December 31 of each year; *provided*, that the first Fiscal Year shall commence on the date of the First Close and end on December 31 of such calendar year, and the last Fiscal Year shall end on the date upon which all assets of the Partnership have been distributed and the Certificate of Limited Partnership has been cancelled.

**[ARTICLE III --- PARTNERS; ADMISSIONS]{.underline}**

**[Section 3.1 --- General Partner]{.underline}**

\(a\) Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, the sole member of which is Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, is hereby admitted as the sole general partner of the Partnership upon its execution of this Agreement. The General Partner shall serve as the sole general partner of the Partnership for the duration of the Fund Term, subject to the provisions of Sections 12.6 and 12.7.

\(b\) The GP Commitment shall be equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of Aggregate Commitments, which at the hard cap of Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000) equals Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000). The GP Commitment shall be funded by the General Partner (or by one or more Affiliates of the General Partner on its behalf, including by Associates through co-investment or other arrangements) pari passu with Capital Calls issued to the Limited Partners. The GP Commitment shall be subject to the same terms and conditions as the Capital Commitments of the Limited Partners, except that (i) no Management Fee shall be charged with respect to the GP Commitment and (ii) the General Partner\'s distributive share of income and loss shall be determined in accordance with the Carried Interest provisions set forth herein.

--

**[Section 3.2 --- Limited Partners]{.underline}**

\(a\) Each Limited Partner shall be admitted to the Partnership upon (i) the execution and delivery by such Limited Partner of a Subscription Agreement and the joinder or counterpart signature page to this Agreement, (ii) the acceptance of such Limited Partner\'s Capital Commitment by the General Partner, and (iii) the occurrence of the applicable Closing (as defined below) at which such Limited Partner is admitted.

\(b\) Each Limited Partner represents and warrants, as of the date of its admission and as of the date of each Capital Call, that it is (i) a \"qualified purchaser\" as defined in Section 2(a)(51)(A) of the Investment Company Act and (ii) an \"accredited investor\" as defined in Rule 501(a) of Regulation D promulgated under the Securities Act.

--

\(d\) Each Limited Partner acknowledges and agrees that its Partnership Interest has not been registered under the Securities Act or the securities laws of any state and may not be transferred except in compliance with this Agreement and applicable securities laws.

**[Section 3.3 --- First Close]{.underline}**

\(a\) The First Close of Capital Commitments to the Partnership is targeted to occur on August 15, 2025 (the **\"First Close\"**), at which time the General Partner shall accept Capital Commitments from one or more Limited Partners.

\(b\) The First Close shall not occur unless the aggregate Capital Commitments accepted at the First Close (including the GP Commitment) equal or exceed Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$750,000,000); *provided*, that the General Partner may, in its sole discretion, waive or reduce such minimum and proceed with the First Close at a lower aggregate commitment level if the General Partner determines that doing so is in the best interests of the Partnership.

\(c\) Upon the occurrence of the First Close, the Partnership shall commence its operations and the General Partner shall be authorized to make Capital Calls and to begin the investment program described in Article V.

**[Section 3.4 --- Subsequent Closes]{.underline}**

\(a\) Following the First Close, the General Partner may hold one or more Subsequent Closes at such times as the General Partner may determine, at which additional Limited Partners may be admitted to the Partnership and/or existing Limited Partners may increase their Capital Commitments. Subsequent Closes may occur on a rolling basis through the Final Close Deadline of February 15, 2027 (being eighteen (18) months after the target date of the First Close).

\(b\) Each Limited Partner admitted at a Subsequent Close shall be required to make a catch-up capital contribution equal to such Limited Partner\'s pro rata share of all Capital Calls that were funded by the existing Partners prior to such Subsequent Close, together with interest thereon at the rate of eight percent (8%) per annum, compounded annually, from the date of the First Close (or, in the case of Capital Calls funded after the First Close, from the respective funding dates thereof) through the date of such Subsequent Close. The catch-up capital contribution shall be funded on the date of such Subsequent Close (or on such other date as the General Partner may specify in the Capital Call notice).

\(c\) The interest component of the catch-up contribution shall be distributed to the Partners who funded Capital Calls prior to such Subsequent Close, pro rata in proportion to their respective funded Capital Contributions, and shall not constitute a return of capital for purposes of the distribution waterfall.

\(d\) Upon admission at a Subsequent Close, each Limited Partner shall be treated, for purposes of the distribution waterfall, allocations, and all other economic provisions of this Agreement, as if such Limited Partner had been admitted at the First Close.

**[Section 3.5 --- Minimum LP Commitment]{.underline}**

--

\(f\) The General Partner shall notify all Limited Partners in writing within ten (10) Business Days following the initial closing of any Subscription Credit Facility, and shall provide quarterly reports to all Limited Partners setting forth the aggregate outstanding borrowings, available capacity, and weighted average interest rate under all Subscription Credit Facilities.

\(g\) The General Partner shall not amend, modify, or supplement any Subscription Credit Facility agreement in a manner that would increase the maximum aggregate borrowing capacity above the Subscription Facility Limit without the prior approval of the LPAC.

**[Section 4.9 --- Default]{.underline}**

--

\(a\) **Concentration Limit.** No single Portfolio Investment shall exceed twenty percent (20%) of Aggregate Commitments at the time of the initial commitment by the Partnership to such investment (the **\"Concentration Limit\"**), which at the hard cap of Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000) equals a maximum of Four Hundred Million Dollars (\$400,000,000). For purposes of this Section 5.3(a), the amount of a Portfolio Investment shall include the aggregate equity committed by the Partnership to such investment (including any committed but unfunded follow-on amounts), but shall exclude any co-investment amounts funded through Excluded Co-Investments.

\(b\) **Geographic Focus.** The Fund\'s investment program shall be focused primarily on companies headquartered or principally operating in North America (the United States and Canada). Investments in companies headquartered outside North America shall be permitted on an opportunistic basis, provided that such investments do not, in the aggregate, exceed \[twenty percent (20%)\] of Aggregate Commitments without LPAC consent.

\(c\) **Sector Focus.** The Fund\'s investment program shall focus on companies operating in the industrials, business services, healthcare services, and technology-enabled services sectors. Investments in other sectors may be made opportunistically, subject to the General Partner\'s fiduciary obligations and the overall investment strategy of the Fund.

\(d\) **Hostile Acquisitions.** The Partnership shall not pursue or consummate any \"hostile\" acquisition (i.e., an acquisition opposed by the target company\'s board of directors or management) or any unsolicited tender offer without the prior consent of the LPAC.

\(e\) **Affiliate Transactions.** The Partnership shall not make any investment in, or enter into any transaction with, the Sponsor, any Affiliate of the Sponsor, or any portfolio company of a predecessor Harrowgate fund without (i) the prior consent of the LPAC and (ii) the affirmative vote of a majority in interest of the Limited Partners (excluding GP-affiliated Capital Commitments).

\(f\) **Public Securities.** The Partnership\'s investments in publicly traded securities shall be limited to (i) take-private transactions (i.e., acquisitions of publicly traded companies with the intention of delisting and taking private) and (ii) incidental public positions arising from the initial public offering of a Portfolio Company or the receipt of publicly traded securities in connection with the disposition of a Portfolio Investment. The Partnership shall not engage in trading of publicly listed securities as a primary investment strategy.

--

**(a) Management Fee During the Investment Period**

During the Investment Period, the Partnership shall pay to the General Partner (or its designee, which may be the Sponsor or an Affiliate thereof) a Management Fee at the rate of one and three-quarters percent (1.75%) per annum, calculated on each Limited Partner\'s Capital Commitment (at the hard cap of Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000) of Aggregate Commitments, the aggregate annual Management Fee would be approximately Thirty-Five Million Dollars (\$35,000,000), subject to adjustment for fee discounts described below). The Management Fee during the Investment Period shall be payable semi-annually in advance on each January 1 and July 1 (or quarterly in advance on each January 1, April 1, July 1, and October 1, at the General Partner\'s election), commencing on the date of the First Close, and shall be pro rated for any partial period.

**(b) Management Fee Post-Investment Period**

--

**(c) Fee discounts**

> \(i\) **Early Close discount.** Limited Partners admitted to the Partnership at the First Close shall receive a discount of ten (10) basis points on the Management Fee rate during the Investment Period, resulting in a Management Fee rate of one and sixty-five hundredths percent (1.65%) per annum on Capital Commitments during the Investment Period (in lieu of 1.75%).
>
> \(ii\) **Large LP discount.** Limited Partners committing One Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$150,000,000) or more to the Partnership shall receive an additional discount of five (5) basis points on the Management Fee rate during the Investment Period. For a Limited Partner admitted at the First Close with a Capital Commitment of \$150,000,000 or more, the cumulative Management Fee rate during the Investment Period shall be one and sixty hundredths percent (1.60%) per annum on Capital Commitments.
>
> \(iii\) Fee discounts described in this Section 7.1(c) may be documented in Side Letters between the General Partner and the relevant Limited Partners, and shall be subject to the MFN provisions of Section 15.14.

--

\(b\) Transaction Fee offsets shall be applied against the Management Fee payable in the next succeeding semi-annual (or quarterly, as applicable) period following receipt of such Transaction Fees. If the aggregate Transaction Fee offset in any period exceeds the Management Fee payable in such period, the excess shall be carried forward and applied against the Management Fee payable in subsequent periods until fully applied.

\(c\) The General Partner shall provide the Limited Partners with a written summary of all Transaction Fees received and offsets applied on at least an annual basis, and upon request by the LPAC.

**[Section 7.3 --- Organizational Expenses]{.underline}**

--

\(f\) Premiums for directors\' and officers\' liability insurance, errors and omissions insurance, and other insurance policies maintained for the benefit of the Partnership, the General Partner, or their respective officers and directors;

\(g\) Costs associated with LPAC meetings, including travel, venue, and related expenses;

\(h\) Regulatory filing fees, blue sky fees, and other fees required by governmental authorities;

--

\(b\) The General Partner may, in its sole discretion, make interim distributions at any time, including distributions of proceeds from refinancings, recapitalizations, or dividend recapitalizations of Portfolio Companies.

\(c\) Distributions shall generally be made in cash. In-kind distributions of securities or other property shall be permitted only with the prior consent of the LPAC (or, in the case of distributions made in connection with the liquidation and winding up of the Partnership, without LPAC consent), subject to Section 8.5.

\(d\) All Distributions shall be made to the Partners in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 8.2.

--

\(a\) In-kind Distributions of securities or other property shall be valued at fair market value as of the date of Distribution, as determined by the General Partner in good faith (and, in the case of publicly traded securities, based on the closing market price as of such date or the volume-weighted average price over a recent trading period as determined by the General Partner).

\(b\) In-kind Distributions shall require the prior consent of the LPAC, except in connection with the liquidation and winding up of the Partnership pursuant to Article XIII.

\(c\) In the case of in-kind Distributions, the General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to distribute securities or other property that are freely transferable and not subject to contractual or regulatory restrictions on resale; *provided*, that if the distributed securities are subject to a lock-up period or other transfer restriction, the General Partner shall so notify the receiving Partners.

--

**[Section 9.2 --- Personal Guarantees]{.underline}**

\(a\) The Clawback obligation set forth in Section 9.1 shall be guaranteed by the following principals of Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, each of whom shall execute a personal guarantee in form and substance reasonably acceptable to the LPAC: (i) Marcus J. Harrowgate; (ii) Diana R. Castellano; and (iii) Jonathan P. Birch (each, a **\"Clawback Guarantor\"** and, collectively, the **\"Clawback Guarantors\"**), as set forth in Schedule C.

\(b\) The guarantee of each Clawback Guarantor shall be on a several (and not joint) basis, in proportion to such Clawback Guarantor\'s respective allocation and receipt of Carried Interest.

--

\(a\) The General Partner shall cause the Independent Auditor to perform an interim clawback test as of the end of each Fiscal Year following the end of the Investment Period. Each such interim test shall determine whether, based on the Partnership\'s cumulative realized and unrealized results as of the applicable testing date, the General Partner has received cumulative Carried Interest Distributions in excess of the amount to which it would be entitled under the distribution waterfall.

\(b\) The results of each interim clawback test shall be provided to the LPAC within ninety (90) days following the end of the applicable Fiscal Year, together with a report from the Independent Auditor setting forth the methodology and assumptions used in such test.

\(c\) If an interim clawback test reveals that the General Partner has received excess Carried Interest, the General Partner and the LPAC shall consult in good faith regarding the appropriate treatment of such excess, which may include (i) the establishment of an escrow or holdback from future Carried Interest Distributions, (ii) the voluntary return of all or a portion of the excess by the General Partner, or (iii) such other arrangement as the General Partner and the LPAC may agree.

**[ARTICLE X --- KEY PERSON]{.underline}**

--

Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event:

\(a\) The Investment Period shall be automatically suspended, effective as of the date of the Key Person Event;

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide written notice to all Limited Partners within five (5) Business Days of the occurrence of the Key Person Event, specifying the identity of the affected Key Person and the circumstances giving rise to the Key Person Event;

--

\(c\) The General Partner shall provide prompt written notice to all Limited Partners of any cure or reinstatement of the Investment Period (or, alternatively, of the permanent termination of the Investment Period due to an uncured Key Person Event).
