**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

This First Amendment (this \"Amendment\") to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Partnership\" or \"Fund V\"), is entered into as of \[●\], 2025 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as general partner of the Partnership (the \"General Partner\" or \"Solara GP\"), and the limited partners of the Partnership (collectively, the \"Limited Partners\" and, together with the General Partner, the \"Partners\").

The Partnership was formed under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. § 17-101 *et seq.* (the \"DRULPA\"), and the Certificate of Limited Partnership of the Partnership was filed with the Office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on or about September 30, 2023, the date of final close of the Partnership. The Employer Identification Number of the Partnership is 88-3467219. The Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Partnership was entered into as of September 30, 2023, the date of the final close of the Partnership (as in effect immediately prior to this Amendment, the \"Partnership Agreement\").

The principal office of the Partnership is located at 1200 Market Street, Suite 3400, Wilmington, Delaware 19801. The registered agent of the Partnership in the State of Delaware is Capitol Registered Agents Inc., 850 New Burton Road, Suite 201, Dover, Delaware 19904.

The General Partner, Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC, is a Delaware limited liability company, Employer Identification Number 82-4917365, managed by Viktor Raines in his capacity as Managing Partner and Founder. The General Partner is also the general partner of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (\"SDILP\"), a Delaware limited partnership (Employer Identification Number 82-4917366), the parent sponsor entity of the Solara fund platform, which had approximately \$14.7 billion in assets under management as of March 31, 2025.
--
The parties to this Amendment enter into this Amendment on the basis of the following background recitals:

**WHEREAS**, the Partnership is a Delaware limited partnership organized for the purpose of making private equity investments in digital infrastructure, including data centers, fiber-optic networks, and edge computing facilities, and enterprise software-as-a-service (\"SaaS\") platforms, in accordance with the investment objectives, strategies, and restrictions set forth in the Partnership Agreement;

**WHEREAS**, Fund V achieved its final close on September 30, 2023, with total capital commitments of \$5,600,000,000 (vintage year 202 partners to the appropriate feeder vehicles (Step 5).

\"**Reorganization Documents**\" means, collectively, all agreements, instruments, certificates, consents, elections, filings, and other documents to be executed, delivered, and filed in connection with the Reorganization, including, without limitation, the limited partnership agreement of the Consolidated Master Fund, the operating agreement of the Master Fund GP, the limited partnership agreements of the International Feeder and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, contribution agreements, assignment and assumption agreements, Form 8832 entity classification elections, the PLR Request, lender consent letters, insurance endorsements, and any other documents reasonably necessary to consummate the Reorganization.

\"**Step 4 Contributions**\" means the contributions by Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Lux of their respective portfolio company assets to the Consolidated Master Fund in exchange for limited partnership interests therein, as described in Step 4 of the Reorganization.

\"**Step 5 Dissolutions**\" means the dissolutions of the Legacy Offshore Vehicles and the distribution of their respective partnership interests in the Consolidated Master Fund to their existing limited partners, as described in Step 5 of the Reorganization.

\"**Tax-Exempt Feeder**\" means Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP, a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to be formed in connection with the Reorganization in accordance with the terms hereof, which will serve as a feeder vehicle for U.S. tax-exempt investors (including pension funds, endowments, and other organizations described in IRC § 501(c)(3)) investing indirectly into the Consolidated Master Fund.

**Section 1.2 --- Interpretation**

\(a\) All references in this Amendment to the \"Partnership Agreement\" shall mean the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP, dated as of September 30, 2023, as amended by this Amendment, and as may be further amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time in accordance with its terms and the terms of this Amendment.

\(b\) In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the terms and provisions of this Amendment and the terms and provisions of the Partnership Agreement (as in effect immediately prior to the effectiveness of this Amendment), the terms and provisions of this Amendment shall control and prevail.

\(c\) References in this Amendment to \"Sections,\" \"Articles,\" and \"Exhibits\" are, unless otherwise specified, references to Sections, Articles, and Exhibits of this Amendment. References to \"Sections\" of the Partnership Agreement are, where the context so requires, references to the Sections of the Partnership Agreement as amended by this Amendment.

\(d\) The terms \"include,\" \"includes,\" and \"including\" shall be deemed to be followed by the words \"without limitation.\" The terms \"hereof,\" \"herein,\" \"hereby,\" and \"hereunder\" refer to this Amendment as a whole. The term \"or\" is not exclusive. Words in the singular include the plural and vice versa.
--
**Section 2.1 --- Consent to the Reorganization**

The Limited Partners hereby consent to the Reorganization as described in the Recitals to this Amendment, including, without limitation, the following actions:

> \(a\) The contribution by Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Lux of all of their respective portfolio company assets to the Consolidated Master Fund in exchange for limited partnership interests therein, as contemplated by Step 4 of the Reorganization (target effective date: November 1, 2025);
>
> \(b\) The dissolution of Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Lux and the distribution of their respective partnership interests in the Consolidated Master Fund to their respective limited partners, as contemplated by Step 5 of the Reorganization (target effective date: December 1, 2025);
>
> \(c\) The migration of non-U.S. limited partners from Fund V-A Cayman into the International Feeder and the migration of U.S. tax-exempt limited partners from Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Lux into the Tax-Exempt Feeder, in each case in connection with the Step 5 Dissolutions; and
>
> \(d\) The establishment of the post-Reorganization structure whereby Fund V LP will co-invest directly alongside the Consolidated Master Fund on a proportionate basis, rather than alongside separate parallel offshore vehicles, in a manner designed to preserve the economic rights, investment exposure, and proportionate sharing of gains, losses, and distributions applicable to the Limited Partners.

The consent of the Limited Partners provided pursuant to this Section 2.1 is granted with the understanding that the Reorganization is subject to the conditions precedent set forth in Article V of this Amendment and that the General Partner retains the authority to modify the timing and structure of the Reorganization steps as provided in Section 2.4.

**Section 2.2 --- Authorization of the General Partner**
--
The General Partner is hereby authorized, empowered, and directed, on behalf of the Partnership and the Limited Partners, to take the following actions in connection with the Reorganization:

> \(a\) **Formation of New Entities.** Cause the formation of the Consolidated Master Fund, the Master Fund GP, the International Feeder, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, including (i) the preparation and filing of certificates of formation and certificates of limited partnership with the Office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware for the Consolidated Master Fund and the Master Fund GP, (ii) coordination with Meridian Offshore Legal (Fiona McAllister, Partner) for the formation and registration of the International Feeder and the Tax-Exempt Feeder as Cayman Islands exempted limited partnerships with the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority, and (iii) engagement of Harborstone Corporate Services Ltd. as registered office provider for the Cayman feeder entities;
>
> \(b\) **Negotiation and Execution of Reorganization Documents.** Negotiate, execute, and deliver the limited partnership agreement of the Consolidated Master Fund, the operating agreement of the Master Fund GP, the limited partnership agreements of the International Feeder and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, and all other Reorganization Documents, on such terms and conditions as the General Partner determines in its reasonable discretion to be in the best interests of the Partnership and the Limited Partners;
>
> \(c\) **Entity Classification Elections.** File Internal Revenue Service Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) for the Consolidated Master Fund, the International Feeder, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, in each case electing classification as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes under Treasury Regulations § 301.7701-3, and take all actions necessary to ensure the timely filing and effectiveness of such elections;
>
> \(d\) **Coordination with Tax Counsel.** Coordinate with Calderwood & Harkness LLP (Leonard Cross, Responsible Partner; Sylvia Hartwell, Billing Partner; Robert Jansen, Lead Associate; Garrett Simmons, Working Associate), 1900 K Street NW, Suite 1100, Washington, DC 20006, in the preparation, review, finalization, and submission of the PLR Request to the Internal Revenue Service, including the preparation of all supporting exhibits, financial data compilations, tax analysis memoranda, and organizational charts required by the PLR Request;
>
> \(e\) **Powers of Attorney.** File Internal Revenue Service Form 2848 (Power of Attorney and Declaration of Representative) designating Leonard Cross and Sylvia Hartwell of Calderwood & Harkness LLP as authorized representatives of the Partnership, the General Partner, and each of the Legacy Offshore Vehicles before the Internal Revenue Service in connection with the PLR Request and all related matters;
>
> \(f\) **Penalties of Perjury Declaration.** Execute and deliver the penalties of perjury declaration required to accompany the PLR Request, with Viktor Raines, in his capacity as Managing Partner of Solara GP, serving as the authorized signatory for such declaration on behalf of the Partnership and the General Partner;
>
> \(g\) **Asset Contributions and Reorganization Steps.** Cause the contribution of Fund V parallel vehicle portfolio company assets to the Consolidated Master Fund and take all actions necessary or advisable to consummate Steps 4 and 5 of the Reorganization, including the execution of contribution agreements, assignment and assumption agreements, and instruments of transfer;
>
> \(h\) **Luxembourg Dissolution Coordination.** Coordinate with Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l. (Marc Gérard, Managing Partner), Luxembourg counsel, regarding the dissolution of Fund V-B Lux (RCS B 271056), including the preparation and filing of all dissolution documents with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, notification to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (\"CSSF\"), and obtaining Luxembourg tax clearance certificates as required under applicable Luxembourg law;
>
> \(i\) **Cayman Deregistration.** Coordinate with Meridian Offshore Legal regarding the deregistration of Fund V-A Cayman with the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (CIMA registration MF-89103), including the preparation and filing of all deregistration applications and the satisfaction of all applicable Cayman Islands regulatory requirements;
>
> \(j\) **Lender Consents.** Execute amendments, consents, and waivers under existing credit facilities as necessary to permit the consummation of the Reorganization, including obtaining consent from Ashford National Bank, N.A. (Thomas Greenleaf, Managing Director, Fund Finance) and Sentinel Capital Markets LLC (Laura Pak, Vice President) under the Partnership\'s \$1,500,000,000 Fund V subscription revolving credit facility, and negotiate such modifications to the credit facility documentation as may be required to reflect the post-Reorganization structure;
>
> \(k\) **Insurance.** Notify Hawkstone Specialty Insurance Co. (Neil Braddock, Senior Underwriter) of the Reorganization and request endorsement of the Partnership\'s directors\' and officers\' liability insurance and errors and omissions liability insurance policies (aggregate limit of \$50,000,000) to provide coverage for the officers, directors, managers, and employees of the newly formed entities in connection with the Reorganization;
>
> \(l\) **Fund Administration.** Notify Clarendon Fund Services Ltd. (Rachel Okonkwo, Client Relationship Director) regarding the transition of fund administration services to accommodate the post-Reorganization structure, including the establishment of new accounts, books, and records for the Consolidated Master Fund and the feeder entities;
--
> \(m\) **Fair Market Value Appraisals.** Engage Redstone Advisory Group LLC (Marco DeLuca, Managing Director) to prepare independent fair market value appraisals of the portfolio company interests being transferred from the Legacy Offshore Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, such appraisals to be prepared in accordance with generally accepted valuation methodologies and to be used as support for the tax positions taken in the PLR Request and the Partnership\'s tax returns;
>
> \(n\) **Accounting and Tax Compliance Support.** Coordinate with Caldwell Pierce & Co. LLP (Helen Okamoto, Partner, Financial Services Tax), the Partnership\'s independent accounting firm and tax compliance provider, for the preparation and compilation of financial data, historical tax return information, and Schedule K-1 data needed for the Reorganization, the PLR Request, and the post-Reorganization tax reporting; and
>
> \(o\) **General Authority.** Take all other actions as may be reasonably necessary, appropriate, or desirable to consummate the Reorganization, including the execution and delivery of any additional agreements, instruments, certificates, consents, and filings, and the engagement of additional advisors, service providers, and professionals as the General Partner may determine in its reasonable discretion to be necessary or advisable.

**Section 2.3 --- Tax Treatment**

The Partnership and the General Partner intend that the Reorganization be treated for U.S. federal income tax purposes as follows, and the General Partner is authorized to take all actions and make all elections consistent with the following intended tax treatment:

> \(a\) **Tax-Free Contributions Under IRC § 721(a).** The Step 4 Contributions constitute tax-free contributions of property to the Consolidated Master Fund in exchange for partnership interests under IRC § 721(a), and no gain or loss shall be recognized by Fund V-A Cayman, Fund V-B Lux, or any of their respective partners as a result of such contributions.
>
> \(b\) **Carryover Basis and Holding Period Tacking.** The Consolidated Master Fund\'s basis in the portfolio company assets received in the Step 4 Contributions shall be determined under IRC § 723, which provides for a carryover basis equal to the adjusted tax basis of such assets in the hands of the contributing partnerships immediately prior to the contribution. The Consolidated Master Fund\'s holding period in such assets shall include the holding period of the contributing partnerships under IRC § 1223(2).
>
> \(c\) **Not an Investment Company.** The Consolidated Master Fund is not an \"investment company\" within the meaning of IRC § 721(b) and Treasury Regulations § 1.351-1(c)(1)(ii), as the portfolio of the Consolidated Master Fund consists of interests in operating companies engaged in digital infrastructure (data centers, fiber-optic networks, edge computing) and enterprise SaaS businesses, and the Consolidated Master Fund does not hold a diversified portfolio of stocks, securities, or other investment assets of the type described in IRC § 351(e)(1).
--
> \(f\) **IRC § 704(c) Built-In Gain Tracking.** Built-in gain and loss accounts under IRC § 704(c) applicable to the portfolio company assets held by the Legacy Offshore Vehicles shall carry over to the Consolidated Master Fund and shall be maintained and tracked by the Consolidated Master Fund using the remedial allocation method described in Treasury Regulations § 1.704-3(d), which is the same method that has been used by the Legacy Offshore Vehicles and the Partnership.
>
> \(g\) **IRC § 752 Liability Shifts.** Shifts in partner-level shares of the aggregate \$1,340,000,000 in liabilities that will be assumed by or transferred to the Consolidated Master Fund in connection with the Reorganization shall be netted under Treasury Regulations § 1.752-1(f) and are not expected to result in the recognition of gain by any partner, as the increases and decreases in each partner\'s share of partnership liabilities occurring as part of the Reorganization are treated as occurring simultaneously rather than sequentially.
>
> \(h\) **No IRC § 1446 Withholding.** No withholding under IRC § 1446(a) is required with respect to the Step 4 Contributions or the Step 5 distributions, as the Step 4 Contributions are tax-free contributions that do not give rise to effectively connected taxable income allocable to foreign partners, and the Step 5 distributions are tax-free distributions under IRC § 731(a).
>
> \(i\) **PLR Request Authorization.** The General Partner is authorized to seek confirmation of the foregoing intended tax treatment through the PLR Request to the IRS Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries), and to take all actions reasonably necessary to prosecute and advance the PLR Request to a favorable conclusion.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Fund V parallel vehicle portfolio assets being contributed to the Consolidated Master Fund in the Step 4 Contributions include interests in 12 portfolio companies, with specific reference to the following key holdings: (i) Veridian Edge Computing Corp. (fair market value of approximately \$1,120,000,000; adjusted tax basis of approximately \$780,000,000; built-in gain of approximately \$340,000,000); and (ii) Helix SaaS Holdings Ltd. (fair market value of approximately \$445,000,000; adjusted tax basis of approximately \$310,000,000; built-in gain of approximately \$135,000,000). The complete schedule of portfolio company interests, including fair market values, adjusted tax bases, and built-in gains, will be set forth in the contribution agreements and the exhibits to the PLR Request.

**Section 2.4 --- Scope of Authorization**

The authorization granted to the General Partner pursuant to this Article II extends to actions taken prior to, on, or after the Effective Date in furtherance of the Reorganization. Any actions taken by the General Partner prior to the Effective Date that were within the scope of the authorization granted by this Article II are hereby ratified and confirmed.

The General Partner may modify the timing of the Reorganization steps described in the Recitals, provided that the target effective date for the Step 5 Dissolutions remains on or about December 1, 2025, or such other date as the General Partner determines in its reasonable discretion, taking into account the progress of the PLR Request, the receipt of lender consents, the availability of regulatory approvals, and other relevant factors. The General Partner shall provide the LPAC with reasonable advance notice of any material changes to the Reorganization timeline.

The General Partner may adjust the structure of the Reorganization as reasonably necessary to address feedback received from the IRS during the pre-submission conference (which has been requested for July 22, 2025) or in response to the PLR Request, or to address changes in applicable tax law, regulation, or administrative guidance, provided that such adjustments do not materially adversely affect the economic rights, investment exposure, or tax position of the Limited Partners. If any structural adjustment is required that would, in the General Partner\'s reasonable judgment, materially adversely affect the Limited Partners, the General Partner shall seek LPAC consent prior to implementing such adjustment.

**[ARTICLE III --- AMENDMENTS TO THE PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Amendment to Investment Provisions**

The Partnership Agreement is hereby amended to permit the Partnership\'s portfolio company assets that are held through Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Lux (i.e., the portfolio company interests held indirectly by the Partnership through the Legacy Offshore Vehicles as part of the parallel fund structure) to be contributed to the Consolidated Master Fund as part of the Reorganization. For the avoidance of doubt, this amendment authorizes the transfer of such assets out of the Legacy Offshore Vehicles and into the Consolidated Master Fund, notwithstanding any investment restrictions, transfer limitations, or other provisions in the Partnership Agreement that might otherwise be interpreted to restrict or prohibit such transfers.

Following the consummation of the Reorganization, the Partnership (Fund V LP) will co-invest alongside the Consolidated Master Fund on a proportionate basis, rather than alongside separate parallel offshore vehicles. All new investments and follow-on investments of the Partnership shall be made in accordance with this co-investment arrangement, with Fund V LP investing directly and the feeder vehicles investing indirectly through the Consolidated Master Fund.

The existing investment restrictions, concentration limits, sector allocation guidelines, and diversification requirements set forth in the Partnership Agreement shall continue to apply to the Partnership\'s investments, and for purposes of measuring compliance with such restrictions and limits, the Partnership\'s investments shall be calculated on an aggregated basis that includes both the Partnership\'s direct investments and the Partnership\'s proportionate share of the Consolidated Master Fund\'s investments. The General Partner shall ensure that the limited partnership agreement of the Consolidated Master Fund contains investment restrictions that are consistent with, and no less restrictive than, the investment restrictions set forth in the Partnership Agreement.

**Section 3.2 --- Amendment to Parallel Fund Provisions**

All provisions in the Partnership Agreement relating to the parallel fund structure, specifically those provisions governing the establishment, maintenance, and operation of parallel fund vehicles alongside Fund V LP, and the relationship between Fund V LP and the Legacy Offshore Vehicles, are hereby amended to reflect the post-Reorganization structure.

Following the consummation of the Reorganization, all references to \"Parallel Funds,\" \"Parallel Vehicles,\" or similar terms in the Partnership Agreement shall be deemed to refer to the Consolidated Master Fund, the International Feeder, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, and not to the Legacy Offshore Vehicles (which will have been dissolved pursuant to Step 5 of the Reorganization).

The aggregate investments convention pursuant to which investment opportunities are allocated on a proportionate basis across Fund V LP and its parallel vehicles shall be maintained through the Consolidated Master Fund structure. The General Partner shall ensure that the limited partnership agreement of the Consolidated Master Fund and the limited partnership agreements of the feeder vehicles contain provisions that are consistent with the aggregate investments convention and the principles of proportionate allocation applicable under the Partnership Agreement.

**Section 3.3 --- Amendment to Allocation and Distribution Provisions**

The allocation and distribution provisions of the Partnership Agreement, including the provisions governing the allocation of net income, net loss, capital gains, and capital losses among the Partners, and the provisions governing the distribution of proceeds and other amounts to the Partners, are hereby amended to the extent necessary to accommodate the following:

> \(a\) The Consolidated Master Fund structure as a co-investment vehicle alongside Fund V LP, such that the allocation and distribution provisions of the Partnership Agreement operate in a manner that is economically equivalent to the allocations and distributions that would have been made under the prior parallel fund structure;
>
> \(b\) The continuation of IRC § 704(c) built-in gain and loss tracking for the contributed properties using the remedial allocation method under Treasury Regulations § 1.704-3(d), including the maintenance of § 704(c) accounts at the Consolidated Master Fund level and the flow-through of § 704(c) allocations to the Partners through the feeder structures; and
>
> \(c\) Adjustments to IRC § 752 liability allocations resulting from the Reorganization, including the reallocation of liability shares among the Partners to reflect the post-Reorganization structure.
--
**Section 3.4 --- Amendment to Transfer and Withdrawal Provisions**

The transfer restrictions and withdrawal provisions in the Partnership Agreement are hereby amended to permit the limited partner migration contemplated in Step 5 of the Reorganization without requiring the individual transfer consent procedures that would otherwise apply under the Partnership Agreement. Specifically:

> \(a\) The migration of non-U.S. limited partners from Fund V-A Cayman to the International Feeder shall not be treated as a \"transfer\" requiring the General Partner\'s consent or the satisfaction of any other transfer conditions under the Partnership Agreement; and
>
> \(b\) The migration of U.S. tax-exempt limited partners from Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Lux to the Tax-Exempt Feeder shall not be treated as a \"transfer\" requiring the General Partner\'s consent or the satisfaction of any other transfer conditions under the Partnership Agreement.

Any admission of a Limited Partner or former limited partner of the Legacy Offshore Vehicles into the International Feeder or the Tax-Exempt Feeder in connection with the Reorganization shall not be treated as a new admission, a transfer, or a secondary transaction requiring consent under the Partnership Agreement. For all purposes of the Partnership Agreement and the Reorganization Documents, such migrations and admissions shall be treated as part of the integrated Reorganization transaction and shall not give rise to any transfer fees, consent fees, or other charges that might otherwise be assessed in connection with transfers or admissions under the Partnership Agreement.

<!-- Slide number: 1 -->
# Solara Digital Infrastructure LP — Cross-Border Fund-Platform Reorganization
Presentation to the LP Advisory Committee
Prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP
CONFIDENTIAL — Attorney-Client Privileged
Date: For LPAC Review — July 15, 2025

<!-- Slide number: 2 -->
# Agenda
I. Executive Summary & Business Rationale
II. Current Fund Platform Structure
III. Proposed Post-Reorganization Structure
IV. Five-Step Transaction Overview
V. Tax Treatment — Summary of Rulings Requested
VI. Key Financial Data
VII. Impact by Investor Category
VIII. Third-Party Consents & Coordination
IX. Timeline & Key Milestones
X. LP Consent Requirements & Next Steps

<!-- Slide number: 3 -->
# I. Executive Summary
Solara Digital Infrastructure LP ($14.7 billion AUM as of March 31, 2025) proposes to consolidate its cross-border fund platform
Four offshore parallel fund vehicles (two Cayman, two Luxembourg) to be reorganized into a single Delaware-domiciled master fund structure with Cayman feeder vehicles
Transaction designed to qualify as tax-free under IRC §§ 721 and 731
Private letter ruling request to be submitted to IRS Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) — target August 15, 2025
Target effective date: December 1, 2025

<!-- Slide number: 4 -->
# Business Rationale for the Reorganization
Operational Cost Reduction: Elimination of approximately $3.8 million in annual duplicative offshore administration, audit, and regulatory fees
OECD Pillar Two GloBE Rules: Forthcoming Pillar Two rules effective for Luxembourg entities from FY 2025 diminish the benefits of the Luxembourg SCSp structures
FATCA/CRS Compliance Simplification: Consolidated reporting reduces complexity and compliance risk across multiple jurisdictions
Governance Simplification: LP-requested streamlining of parallel fund governance, voting, and reporting across multiple vehicles

<!-- Slide number: 5 -->
# II. Current Fund Platform Structure
Fund IV Family (Vintage 2021; 72% deployed):
  — Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP (Delaware) — $4.2B — U.S. taxable investors
  — Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP — $1.85B — Non-U.S. and U.S. tax-exempt investors
  — Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp — €1.15B ($1.24B) — Non-U.S. investors (treaty access)
Fund V Family (Vintage 2023; 38% deployed):
  — Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP (Delaware) — $5.6B — U.S. taxable investors
  — Fund V-A (Cayman) LP — $2.45B — Non-U.S. and U.S. tax-exempt investors
  — Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp — €1.38B ($1.49B) — Non-U.S. investors (treaty access)
Three GP entities: Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (DE), Solara Offshore GP Ltd. (Cayman), Solara Luxembourg Management S.à r.l. (Luxembourg)

<!-- Slide number: 6 -->
# Representative Investor Base
U.S. Tax-Exempt: Pinnacle State Employees' Retirement System ($275M Fund IV / $340M Fund V); Grandview University Endowment ($120M Fund IV / $185M Fund V)
Non-U.S. Sovereign: Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund ($380M Fund IV-A Cayman / $500M Fund V-A Cayman)
Non-U.S. Insurance: Kestrel Pacific Insurance Group (€200M Fund IV-B Lux / €275M Fund V-B Lux)
U.S. Taxable: Argyle Family Office Holdings LLC ($95M Fund IV / $130M Fund V)
Each category has distinct tax sensitivities driving post-reorganization feeder/direct investment channel

<!-- Slide number: 7 -->
# III. Proposed Post-Reorganization Structure
Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP (Delaware) — new master fund consolidating all offshore vehicle assets
  — GP: Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC (Delaware)
Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP — feeder for non-U.S. investors investing into the Master Fund
Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP — feeder for U.S. tax-exempt investors (pensions, endowments) to mitigate UBTI concerns
Fund IV LP and Fund V LP (Delaware) — remain as-is; U.S. taxable investors continue to invest directly alongside the Master Fund
All new entities to elect partnership classification via IRS Form 8832 (check-the-box)

<!-- Slide number: 8 -->
# IV. Five-Step Transaction Overview
Step 1 — Formation of New Entities (Sept. 15, 2025): Form Master Fund GP LLC, Master Fund LP, International Feeder, Tax-Exempt Feeder; file Form 8832 elections
Step 2 — Contribution of Fund IV-A Cayman Assets (Oct. 1, 2025): All portfolio assets (FMV $2.31B; basis $1.62B; BIG $690M) contributed to Master Fund LP
Step 3 — Contribution of Fund IV-B Luxembourg Assets (Oct. 15, 2025): All portfolio assets (FMV $1.16B; basis $844.6M; BIG $311M) contributed to Master Fund LP
Step 4 — Contribution of Fund V Offshore Assets (Nov. 1, 2025): Fund V-A Cayman (FMV $2.89B; BIG $550M) and Fund V-B Lux (FMV $1.39B; BIG $162M) contributed to Master Fund LP
Step 5 — Dissolution & LP Migration (Dec. 1, 2025): Legacy vehicles dissolve; Master Fund LP interests distributed to LPs; non-U.S. LPs roll into International Feeder; U.S. tax-exempt LPs roll into Tax-Exempt Feeder

<!-- Slide number: 9 -->
# Aggregate Financial Summary of the Reorganization
Total FMV of assets transferred to Consolidated Master Fund: $7.75 billion
Total adjusted tax basis: $6.03 billion
Total aggregate built-in gain: $1.72 billion
Aggregate liabilities assumed by Master Fund: $1.34 billion (subject to § 752 analysis)
Total portfolio companies across all funds: 23 (11 in Fund IV vehicles; 12 in Fund V vehicles)
EUR/USD exchange rate applied uniformly: 1.08

<!-- Slide number: 10 -->
# V. Tax Treatment — Overview of Rulings Requested
Ruling 1 (§ 721): Tax-free contributions of portfolio assets to Master Fund LP — no gain/loss recognized
Ruling 2 (§ 721(b)): Master Fund LP does not constitute an 'investment company' (operating company portfolio)
Ruling 3 (§ 367): §§ 367(a)/(b) do not apply — provisions apply only to transfers to/from corporations, not partnerships
Ruling 4 (§ 731): Tax-free distributions of Master Fund LP interests to LPs upon dissolution of legacy vehicles
Ruling 5 (§ 752): Liability shifts do not trigger gain recognition under § 731 after netting analysis
Ruling 6 (§ 704(c)): Built-in gain/loss accounts carry over; remedial allocation method continues
Ruling 7 (§ 1446): No withholding required on contributions or distributions (nonrecognition transactions)
Ruling 8 (Entity Classification): All new entities properly classified as partnerships under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3

<!-- Slide number: 11 -->
# Ruling 1: IRC § 721(a) — Tax-Free Contributions
Each offshore vehicle contributes its entire portfolio to Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP in exchange for a limited partnership interest
Under IRC § 721(a), no gain or loss is recognized by the contributing partnerships or their partners on the contribution of property to a partnership
Carryover basis under IRC § 723 — Master Fund takes the same tax basis as the contributing vehicle
Holding period of contributed assets tacks under IRC § 1223(2)
No cash boot or other consideration beyond partnership interests

<!-- Slide number: 12 -->
# Ruling 2: IRC § 721(b) — Not an Investment Company
IRC § 721(b) denies tax-free treatment if the contribution results in 'diversification' and the partnership is an 'investment company'
Treas. Reg. § 1.351-1(c)(1)(ii) defines 'investment company' by reference to holdings of 'stocks, securities, or other investment assets'
Solara's portfolio consists entirely of operating company interests — digital infrastructure and enterprise SaaS platforms
All 23 portfolio companies are active operating businesses, not passive investment assets
Conclusion: § 721(b) exception does not apply; contributions remain tax-free

<!-- Slide number: 13 -->
# Rulings 3–4: § 367 Inapplicability & § 731 Distributions
Ruling 3 (§ 367): IRC §§ 367(a) and 367(b) by their terms apply only to transfers to or from corporations — the Master Fund LP is a partnership; § 367 does not apply
Ruling 4 (§ 731): Distributions by legacy vehicles of Master Fund LP interests to LPs in Step 5 are tax-free under § 731(a) — no gain recognized because LPs receive only partnership interests, not money
IRC § 731(c) marketable securities exception does not apply — Master Fund LP interests are not 'marketable securities' as they are not actively traded or readily tradable on a secondary market

<!-- Slide number: 14 -->
# Rulings 5–6: Liability Shifts (§ 752) & Built-In Gain Carryover (§ 704(c))
Ruling 5 (§ 752): $1.34B in aggregate liabilities shift from legacy vehicles to Master Fund LP — §§ 752(a)/(b) create deemed contributions and distributions as partner shares change
Netting under Treas. Reg. § 1.752-1(f) and tiered partnership rules applied to demonstrate no net gain recognition under § 731
Ruling 6 (§ 704(c)): $1.72B in built-in gain accounts carry over from legacy vehicles to Master Fund LP
Master Fund LP will continue to use the remedial allocation method under Treas. Reg. § 1.704-3(d) for each contributed property
Ensures historic investors continue to bear their appropriate share of built-in gain on eventual disposition

<!-- Slide number: 15 -->
# Rulings 7–8: Withholding (§ 1446) & Entity Classification
Ruling 7 (§ 1446): No withholding on Steps 2–4 contributions or Step 5 distributions — nonrecognition events generate no effectively connected taxable income
Particularly relevant for non-U.S. investors (Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund, Kestrel Pacific Insurance Group)
Ruling 8 (Entity Classification): Master Fund LP, International Feeder, and Tax-Exempt Feeder each properly classified as partnerships under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3 via check-the-box elections
Form 8832 elections to be filed for each new entity with effective dates coordinated to precede the first contribution step

<!-- Slide number: 16 -->
# VI. Key Financial Data — Portfolio Company Highlights
NovaBright Data Systems Inc. (DE corp) — Data center operator — FMV $890M / Basis $520M / BIG $370M — Fund IV-A Cayman 60%, Fund IV LP 40%
Veridian Edge Computing Corp. (DE corp) — Edge computing infra — FMV $1.12B / Basis $780M / BIG $340M — Fund V-A Cayman 55%, Fund V LP 45%
Thorngate Fiber Networks LP (DE LP) — Fiber-optic networks — FMV $670M / Basis $490M / BIG $180M — Fund IV-A Cayman 100%
Crestline Cloud Solutions LLC (DE LLC, disregarded) — SaaS platform — FMV €340M ($367M) / Basis €195M ($211M) / BIG $156M — Fund IV-B Lux 100%
Helix SaaS Holdings Ltd. (Cayman exempted co.) — SaaS holding — FMV $445M / Basis $310M / BIG $135M — Fund V-A Cayman 100%
Plus 18 additional portfolio companies across Fund IV and Fund V vehicles

<!-- Slide number: 17 -->
# VII. Impact by Investor Category
U.S. Taxable Investors (e.g., Argyle Family Office): No change — remain directly in Fund IV LP and Fund V LP; co-invest alongside Master Fund
U.S. Tax-Exempt Investors (e.g., Pinnacle SERS, Grandview Endowment): Migrate from Cayman parallel vehicles to Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP → Master Fund; UBTI blocker benefits preserved
Non-U.S. Investors — Cayman (e.g., Nordhaven SWF): Migrate from Fund IV-A/V-A Cayman to International Feeder (Cayman) LP → Master Fund; no U.S. withholding on reorganization steps
Non-U.S. Investors — Luxembourg (e.g., Kestrel Pacific): Migrate from Fund IV-B/V-B Lux to International Feeder (Cayman) LP → Master Fund; Luxembourg SCSps dissolved; no Luxembourg capital gains tax expected
All categories: No gain recognition anticipated; built-in gain accounts carry over; tax attributes preserved

<!-- Slide number: 18 -->
# VIII. Third-Party Consents & Coordination
Lender Consents: Ashford National Bank, N.A. — Fund IV subscription facility ($1.1B) and Fund V subscription facility ($1.5B); Sentinel Capital Markets LLC — co-lender/administrative agent on Fund V facility
Insurance: Hawkstone Specialty Insurance Co. — endorsement of $50M D&O/E&O policies to cover new entities
Fund Administrator: Clarendon Fund Services Ltd. — transition of NAV calculation and investor reporting to Master Fund structure
Cayman Counsel: Meridian Offshore Legal (Fiona McAllister) — formation of new Cayman feeders; CIMA deregistration of Fund IV-A (MF-72491) and Fund V-A (MF-89103)
Luxembourg Counsel: Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l. (Marc Gérard) — dissolution of Fund IV-B SCSp (RCS B 248193) and Fund V-B SCSp (RCS B 271056); CSSF notification
Accounting: Caldwell Pierce & Co. LLP — financial data and tax compliance support for PLR submission

<!-- Slide number: 19 -->
# IX. Timeline & Key Milestones
March 14, 2025 — GP board approval of reorganization exploration
April 22, 2025 — LPAC meeting; preliminary consent obtained (78% in interest)
May 12, 2025 — Calderwood & Harkness engagement letter executed
June 16, 2025 — Initial tax analysis memorandum completed
July 1, 2025 — Draft PLR request circulated to Solara
July 15, 2025 — LPAC review of final PLR request
July 22, 2025 — Pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL Branch 1
August 15, 2025 — PLR request submitted to IRS
September 15, 2025 — Formation of new entities; Form 8832 elections filed
October 1, 2025 — Step 2: Fund IV-A Cayman contribution to Master Fund
October 15, 2025 — Step 3: Fund IV-B Luxembourg contribution to Master Fund
November 1, 2025 — Step 4: Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Luxembourg contributions
December 1, 2025 — Step 5: Dissolution of legacy vehicles; LP migration (target effective date)

<!-- Slide number: 20 -->
# X. LP Consent Requirements & Next Steps
Formal LP consent required under LPA amendment provisions for Fund IV and Fund V (and all parallel vehicles)
Preliminary consent of 78% in interest obtained at April 22, 2025 LPAC meeting — formal solicitation to follow
LP Consent Solicitation Letter and Form of LP Consent to be distributed to all LPs
Draft Amendments to Fund IV LPA and Fund V LPA to authorize asset contributions and formation of new entities
LP Tax Impact Summary Letter to be provided to all LPs — each LP encouraged to consult its own tax advisors
LPAC counsel (Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP) reviewing PLR Draft v3.0 — comments due July 15, 2025

<!-- Slide number: 21 -->
# Key Advisors & Contacts
U.S. Tax Counsel: Calderwood & Harkness LLP — Leonard Cross (Responsible Partner), Sylvia Hartwell (Billing Partner), Robert Jansen (Lead Associate), Garrett Simmons (Working Associate)
LPAC Counsel: Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP — Diana Carruthers (Partner)
Nordhaven SWF Independent Tax Counsel: Bramhall & Quelwick LLP — Jason Tremaine (Partner)
Cayman Counsel: Meridian Offshore Legal — Fiona McAllister (Partner)
Luxembourg Counsel: Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l. — Marc Gérard (Managing Partner)

Valuation Advisor: Redstone Advisory Group LLC — Marco DeLuca (Managing Director)

Lender: Ashford National Bank, N.A. — Thomas Greenleaf (MD); Sentinel Capital Markets LLC — Laura Pak (VP)
Solara Contacts: Viktor Raines (Managing Partner), Priya Narasimhan (GC), Stefan Dalmqvist (Head of Tax), Douglas Wexford (CFO), Meredith Tsao (COO)

<!-- Slide number: 22 -->
# Appendix: Key Tax Code Provisions Referenced
IRC § 721(a), (b) — Contribution of property to a partnership; investment company exception
IRC § 723 — Basis of property contributed to a partnership

Dear Ms. Narasimhan:

**[1. Purpose and Acceptance]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (\"Solara\" or \"SDILP\"), a Delaware limited partnership, and its general partner, Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (\"Solara GP\"), a Delaware limited liability company (collectively, the \"Client\"), to provide the legal services described in this engagement letter (this \"Letter\"). We appreciate the confidence that Solara and Solara GP have placed in our Firm, and we look forward to working with your team on this significant and complex matter.

This Letter sets forth the terms and conditions upon which Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services in connection with the matter described herein. By countersigning this Letter in the space provided below, the Client agrees to be bound by the terms and conditions set forth herein. This engagement shall be effective as of the date of the countersignature below. No attorney-client relationship will be deemed to have been established with respect to the matter described herein until this Letter has been signed by an authorized representative of the Client and returned to the Firm.

**[2. Description of the Client]{.underline}**

The client for this engagement is Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (EIN: 82-4917366) and Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (EIN: 82-4917365). For the avoidance of doubt, the \"Client\" as used throughout this Letter refers collectively to SDILP and Solara GP, except where the context clearly requires otherwise.

Solara is a Delaware-based private equity sponsor with approximately \$14.7 billion in assets under management as of March 31, 2025, operating across digital infrastructure and enterprise SaaS verticals. Solara sponsors private equity funds through a series of parallel fund structures established across Delaware, the Cayman Islands, and Luxembourg to accommodate U.S. taxable, U.S. tax-exempt, and non-U.S. investor pools. The fund platform reflects a multi-jurisdictional architecture that is common among institutional-scale private equity sponsors and is central to the reorganization that is the subject of this engagement.

The principal contact persons at Solara for purposes of this engagement are as follows:

> • **Priya Narasimhan**, General Counsel --- primary legal contact and authorized decision-maker for engagement-related matters;
>
> • **Stefan Dalmqvist**, Head of Tax --- primary contact for substantive tax matters, financial data, and coordination with the Client\'s independent auditors and valuation advisors.

The Managing Partner and Founder of Solara is **Viktor Raines**. Mr. Raines will serve as the authorized officer of Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC for purposes of executing any penalties of perjury declarations and other representations required in connection with Internal Revenue Service (\"IRS\") submissions, as described more fully in Section 8 below.

All communications from the Firm regarding this engagement should be directed to Ms. Narasimhan and Mr. Dalmqvist, unless otherwise instructed in writing by the Client.

**[3. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

**3.1 Overview of the Transaction**

Solara is undertaking a cross-border reorganization of its fund platform (the \"Reorganization\"), involving the domestication and merger of several Cayman Islands and Luxembourg fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure. The Reorganization is designed to simplify the Client\'s fund architecture, reduce administrative and operational costs, enhance investor reporting, and achieve certain tax efficiencies in connection with the ongoing management and eventual disposition of portfolio company interests.

The Reorganization involves the following existing fund vehicles (collectively, the \"Legacy Fund Vehicles\"):

> \(i\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$4.2 billion in committed capital (vintage 2021), approximately 72% deployed as of the date hereof;
>
> \(ii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$1.85 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors;
>
> \(iii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.15 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.24 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for certain European institutional investors;
>
> \(iv\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$5.6 billion in committed capital (vintage 2023), approximately 38% deployed as of the date hereof;
>
> \(v\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$2.45 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors; and
>
> \(vi\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.38 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.49 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for certain European institutional investors.

The Reorganization contemplates the formation of the following new entities (collectively, the \"New Fund Vehicles\"):
--
> \(ii\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company to serve as the general partner of the Consolidated Master Fund;
>
> \(iii\) **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for non-U.S. investors; and
>
> \(iv\) **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for U.S. tax-exempt investors.

The Reorganization involves a multi-step transaction that includes, among other things, asset contributions by the four offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the dissolution of the legacy offshore vehicles following such contributions, and the migration of existing limited partners into the appropriate new feeder structure. The target effective date for the completion of the Reorganization is December 1, 2025. The precise sequencing and mechanics of the multi-step transaction will be developed and refined in the course of the engagement, in consultation with the Client and its other advisors.

**3.2 Scope of Legal Services**

Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement is limited to the following specific legal services in connection with the Reorganization:

> \(a\) **Tax Analysis Memoranda.** Preparation of comprehensive tax analysis memoranda addressing the U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Reorganization under, among other provisions, Internal Revenue Code (\"IRC\") §§ 721(a), 721(b), 723, 731(a), 731(c), 704(c), 752, 367(a), 367(b), 1446, and 897, and Treasury Regulations § 301.7701-3. The tax analysis memoranda will address the characterization of each step of the multi-step Reorganization, including the contribution of assets by the offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the treatment of assumed or shifted liabilities, the application of the anti-mixing bowl rules, and the withholding tax implications for non-U.S. limited partners.
>
> \(b\) **Private Letter Ruling Request.** Drafting, revising, and finalizing a private letter ruling request (the \"PLR Request\") to be submitted to the Internal Revenue Service\'s Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (\"CC:INTL\"), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (\"CC:PSI\"). The PLR Request will seek rulings on the specific tax consequences of the Reorganization that are identified in the course of the engagement as requiring advance IRS guidance for purposes of transaction certainty.
>
> \(c\) **Ancillary IRS Procedural Documents.** Preparation and filing of all ancillary IRS procedural documents required in connection with the PLR Request, including IRS Forms 2848 (Powers of Attorney and Declarations of Representative), penalties of perjury declarations, user fee transmittals, and pre-submission and supplemental correspondence with the IRS.
>
> \(d\) **Pre-Submission Conference.** Coordination and participation in a pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL (requested for July 22, 2025) and any follow-up communications arising therefrom. The pre-submission conference is intended to confirm the jurisdictional assignment of the PLR Request, identify any threshold legal issues, and facilitate an efficient review process following formal submission.
>
> \(e\) **Submission of PLR Request.** Submission of the PLR Request to the IRS at the following address: Internal Revenue Service, Attn: CC:INTL, 1111 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20224, together with all required enclosures, exhibits, and transmittal documents.
>
> \(f\) **Post-Submission Monitoring.** Post-submission monitoring of the status of the PLR Request, preparation of responses to IRS information requests and additional questions, and supplemental submissions as necessary through issuance of the private letter ruling or closure of the matter by the IRS. This includes attendance at any conferences or telephone calls requested by the IRS examining branch.
>
> \(g\) **Coordination with Other Advisors.** Coordination with the Client\'s other advisors as described in Section 3.3 below, to the extent necessary for the preparation and prosecution of the PLR Request and associated tax analysis memoranda.
>
> \(h\) **Supporting Documentation.** Preparation of supporting documentation in connection with the Reorganization, including review of and comment on IRS Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) filings for the New Fund Vehicles and any related check-the-box elections.

**3.3 Coordination with Other Advisors**

Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with, but does not assume responsibility for the work of, the following advisors that have been retained by Solara or its affiliates in connection with the Reorganization or related matters. Each of the following advisors has been engaged separately by the Client, and the Firm\'s coordination with such advisors is limited to the exchange of information and consultation necessary for Calderwood & Harkness to perform the services described in Section 3.2:

> \(i\) **Caldwell Pierce & Co. LLP** (400 Renaissance Center, Suite 2500, Detroit, MI 48243; Helen Okamoto, Partner) --- independent accounting firm providing annual audits, tax compliance services, and supporting financial data for the PLR Request, including fund-level financial statements, capital account schedules, and partner allocation computations.
>
> \(ii\) **Redstone Advisory Group LLC** (750 Seventh Avenue, 21st Floor, New York, NY 10019; Marco DeLuca, Managing Director) --- valuation and transfer pricing advisory firm preparing fair market value appraisals of portfolio company interests and other assets to be contributed in connection with the Reorganization. Redstone\'s valuation reports will be included as exhibits to the PLR Request.
>
> \(iii\) **Meridian Offshore Legal** (Caledonia House, 69 Dr. Roy\'s Drive, George Town, Grand Cayman KY1-1103; Fiona McAllister, Partner) --- Cayman Islands counsel advising on the formation of the New Fund Vehicles organized in the Cayman Islands, the dissolution of the Legacy Fund Vehicles organized in the Cayman Islands, and related regulatory matters involving the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (\"CIMA\").
>
> \(iv\) **Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l.** (22, boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg; Marc Gérard, Managing Partner) --- Luxembourg counsel advising on the dissolution of the Luxembourg SCSp vehicles and notification requirements to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (\"CSSF\").
>
> \(v\) **Clarendon Fund Services Ltd.** (Windward 3, Regatta Office Park, West Bay Road, George Town, Grand Cayman KY1-1108; Rachel Okonkwo, Client Relationship Director) --- fund administrator for the offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles, providing net asset value computations, investor registries, and other administrative data relevant to the Reorganization.

Calderwood & Harkness will rely upon the work product of the foregoing advisors to the extent necessary for the preparation of the PLR Request and associated tax analysis memoranda. However, the Firm assumes no responsibility for the accuracy, completeness, or timeliness of work product prepared by any such advisor, and the Firm\'s reliance on such work product will be subject to the Firm\'s independent professional judgment.

**3.4 Matters Excluded from Scope**

For the avoidance of doubt, this engagement does not include the following:

> \(a\) Legal advice on the laws of the Cayman Islands or Luxembourg, including corporate, partnership, regulatory, or tax law of those jurisdictions. Such matters are addressed by Meridian Offshore Legal and Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l., respectively, as described in Section 3.3 above.
>
> \(b\) Ongoing tax compliance for any fund vehicle, including preparation of federal, state, or local tax returns, Schedules K-1, FATCA reporting (including IRS Forms W-8BEN, W-8BEN-E, and W-8IMY), or Common Reporting Standard (\"CRS\") reporting.
>
> \(c\) Post-ruling implementation of the Reorganization, including without limitation the filing of formation documents, execution of contribution agreements, amendment and restatement of limited partnership agreements, or preparation or filing of dissolution documents, except to the extent specifically set forth in Section 3.2 above.
>
> \(d\) Legal advice to, or representation of, any individual limited partner of any Legacy Fund Vehicle or New Fund Vehicle, the LP Advisory Committee of any fund (including the Fund IV LP Advisory Committee and the Fund V LP Advisory Committee), or any counterparty to any transaction involving Solara or its affiliates.
>
> \(e\) State and local tax advice, including analysis of state income, franchise, or other tax consequences of the Reorganization in any U.S. state or local jurisdiction.
>
> \(f\) Investment advice or securities law analysis, including advice under the Securities Act of 1933, the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, the Investment Company Act of 1940, or any state \"blue sky\" laws.

If the Client wishes to expand the scope of this engagement to include any of the foregoing matters or any other matters not described in Section 3.2, the parties will enter into a separate engagement letter or written amendment to this Letter.

**[4. Engagement Team]{.underline}**

The following attorneys of Calderwood & Harkness will serve as the engagement team for this matter:

**Leonard Cross** --- Responsible Partner, Tax. Mr. Cross has twenty-eight (28) years of experience in international tax, partnership tax, and fund formation matters, with particular focus on cross-border restructurings, private letter ruling requests, and IRS controversy matters. Mr. Cross is located in Calderwood & Harkness\'s Washington, D.C. office at 1900 K Street NW, Suite 1100, Washington, DC 20006. He will serve as the primary point of contact for substantive tax matters and all communications with the IRS, including representation at the pre-submission conference and any subsequent IRS conferences or calls.

**Sylvia Hartwell** --- Billing Partner, Tax. Ms. Hartwell has twenty-four (24) years of experience in cross-border restructurings and investment fund taxation, with deep expertise in multi-jurisdictional fund platform redesigns. Ms. Hartwell is located in Calderwood & Harkness\'s New York office at 600 Lexington Avenue, 38th Floor, New York, NY 10022. She will be responsible for billing, budget management, engagement administration, and overall client relationship management. Ms. Hartwell will also contribute to the substantive tax analysis as needed.

**Robert Jansen** --- Lead Associate, Tax. Mr. Jansen has six (6) years of experience in tax law, with a focus on partnership taxation, entity classification, and IRS procedural matters. Mr. Jansen is located in the Firm\'s Washington, D.C. office. He will serve as the lead drafter of the PLR Request and tax analysis memoranda.

**Garrett Simmons** --- Working Associate, Tax. Mr. Simmons has three (3) years of experience in tax law, with a focus on international tax research and financial modeling. Mr. Simmons is located in the Firm\'s New York office. He will provide research support, drafting assistance, and financial modeling in connection with the tax analysis memoranda and the PLR Request.

Calderwood & Harkness may, from time to time, engage additional attorneys or professional staff to assist with the matter as the needs of the engagement require. The Client will be notified of any material change to the staffing plan described above, including the assignment of any additional partner-level attorney to the engagement team. The Firm will endeavor to staff the engagement in a manner that balances efficiency, continuity, and the appropriate level of expertise for each task.

**[5. Fees and Billing]{.underline}**

**5.1 Hourly Rates**

Legal services rendered in connection with this engagement will be billed at a blended hourly rate of **\$1,175.00 per hour** for all engagement team members. The blended rate applies uniformly to all timekeepers assigned to the engagement, including partners, associates, counsel, and any other attorneys who may be assigned to the matter from time to time.

Calderwood & Harkness\'s standard billing rates are subject to annual adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each calendar year. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the blended rate of \$1,175.00 per hour will be maintained for the duration of this engagement and will not be adjusted unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Calderwood & Harkness and the Client.

**5.2 Estimated Fees**

Based on the scope of services described in Section 3, Calderwood & Harkness estimates that total legal fees for this engagement will be in the range of **\$1,800,000 to \$2,400,000**. This estimate reflects the Firm\'s current understanding of the complexity of the Reorganization, the anticipated number of issues to be addressed in the PLR Request, and the expected level of IRS engagement.

This estimate is provided for budgeting purposes only and does not constitute a cap, maximum, fixed fee, or guaranteed price. The matter will be billed on a time-and-materials basis, and the Client will be responsible for actual fees incurred regardless of whether they fall within the estimated range.

**LPAC Procedures.** The LPAC is an advisory body and does not have the authority to bind the Fund or the General Partner except as specifically provided in the LPA. **[XII. TIMELINE AND NEXT STEPS]{.underline}**
=== documents/matters/1004-00002/Structuring & Analysis/side-letter-framework-memo.docx ===

**Transaction and Monitoring Fee Offset.** Transaction fees, monitoring fees, directors\' fees, and similar fees received by CLSO GP or its affiliates from portfolio companies will be offset at a rate of 80% against the management fee payable by the Fund. The 20% retained by CLSO Management is intended to compensate for the incremental cost of providing transaction and monitoring services to portfolio companies.

**Fund Term.** The Fund\'s term will be 10 years from the final close, with two optional one-year extensions. The first extension may be effected at the sole discretion of CLSO GP. The second extension requires the affirmative consent of the LP Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\"). Based on a target final close of May 15, 2027, the initial term would expire on May 15, 2037, with possible extensions to May 15, 2038 (first extension) and May 15, 2039 (second extension, subject to LPAC consent).

**LP Advisory Committee.** The LPAC will consist of a minimum of three and a maximum of seven members, appointed by CLSO GP. If aggregate non-U.S. commitments reach or exceed \$50,000,000, at least one LPAC member must be a representative of a non-U.S. limited partner. The LPAC\'s functions include consent to conflicts of interest, review of valuation methodology, consent to the second one-year fund extension, and such other matters as may be specified in the LPA.

**Key Person.** Both Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta are designated as key persons. A key person event will be triggered if either Principal ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund, resulting in a suspension of the investment period pending reinstatement or termination by the limited partners.

--

**Mechanics.** Upon the final close of the Fund (target: May 15, 2027), CLSO GP will prepare---with the assistance of Calderwood & Harkness LLP---a redacted compendium of all side letter terms granted to all LPs. The compendium will be redacted to remove investor-identifying information (including the name, commitment size, and contact details of each LP) while preserving the substance of each concession in sufficient detail to permit an informed election. Each MFN-eligible LP will receive a copy of the redacted compendium, together with a notice setting forth the election procedures and the deadline for elections. Each MFN-eligible LP will have 30 calendar days from the date of distribution to elect, in writing, to receive any or all of the disclosed concessions. Elected terms will be incorporated into the electing LP\'s side letter by means of a written amendment executed by the LP and CLSO GP.

**Carve-Outs from MFN.** Certain categories of side letter terms should be excluded from the MFN election process, as they are by their nature investor-specific or relate to the particular legal, regulatory, or tax status of the benefited LP. The recommended carve-out categories are discussed in detail in Section V.C below and summarized in Appendix B. By way of overview, the recommended carve-outs include: (a) ERISA-specific provisions (e.g., the Northgate VCOC carve-out); (b) insurance regulatory provisions (e.g., the Pinnacle compliance suite); (c) FOIA and public records protections (e.g., the Ironwood PERS provisions); (d) blocker entity access (investor-specific tax structuring); (e) LPAC seats (allocated based on commitment size and investor profile); (f) co-investment rights at no fee/no carry, to the extent offered only to investors above a specified commitment threshold (recommended: \$75,000,000); and (g) terms that are personal to the investor, such as notice addresses and contact information.

**Co-Investment and MFN.** A threshold question for the framework is whether co-investment rights at no additional management fee and no carried interest should be MFN-eligible or carved out as an anchor-specific concession. Our recommendation is that co-investment rights at no fee/no carry should be carved out of MFN for investors with commitments below \$75,000,000. This preserves the economic incentive for anchor commitments and is consistent with market practice for life-sciences funds of this size. Co-investment opportunities offered on a \"best-efforts\" basis at reduced (but not eliminated) fee and carry terms may remain MFN-eligible, as these represent a lower-value concession and are less likely to create economic imbalance.

--

**Allocation Policy.** Co-investment allocations will be made on a pro rata basis relative to each LP\'s commitment to the Fund, subject to CLSO GP\'s discretion to consider factors including investor suitability for the particular investment, speed of execution and ability to commit capital within the required timeframe, the LP\'s historical participation in co-investment opportunities, and potential conflicts of interest. The allocation policy should be set forth in the LPA and referenced in each side letter that includes co-investment rights.

**I. Advisory Committee (LPAC) Representation**

**LPAC Composition.** As noted in Section II.B, the LPAC will consist of a minimum of three and a maximum of seven members, appointed by CLSO GP. At least one member must be a representative of a non-U.S. LP if aggregate non-U.S. commitments reach \$50,000,000.

**Side Letter Allocation of Seats.** LPAC seats are a governance concession that is typically offered to the largest LPs and to investors whose participation in the LPAC adds value to the Fund\'s governance (e.g., investors with deep sector expertise, investors who represent a particular constituency within the LP base, or investors whose regulatory status makes their input on compliance matters particularly relevant). LPAC seats should be allocated in the side letters of anchor investors. For CLSO Fund I, we recommend guaranteeing one LPAC seat to Ironwood PERS (as the largest anchor investor) in its side letter, and reserving the remaining seats for allocation during the fundraising process based on the composition of the LP base at each closing. Northgate and Pinnacle may request LPAC representation, and CLSO GP should retain flexibility to accommodate such requests if the committee composition allows.

**LPAC Functions.** The LPAC\'s primary functions, as set forth in the LPA, will include: (a) consent to conflicts of interest involving CLSO GP, the Principals, or their affiliates; (b) review of the Fund\'s valuation methodology, including fair value determinations for portfolio investments; (c) consent to the second one-year fund extension (from May 15, 2038 to May 15, 2039, assuming the first extension has been exercised); and (d) such other advisory functions as may be specified in the LPA. The LPAC will operate in an advisory capacity and will not have the power to bind the Fund or CLSO GP, except where specific consent rights are granted.

**J. Indemnification and Exculpation**

--

**MFN Side Letter.** Ironwood PERS will expect full MFN rights, with the broadest possible scope of election. As the largest LP, Ironwood PERS will expect to be the MFN \"benchmark\" investor, meaning that its side letter effectively sets the ceiling of concessions that other investors can elect into (subject to carve-outs for investor-specific regulatory provisions). This is a standard expectation for the largest LP in a fund and is consistent with market practice. We recommend granting full MFN rights to Ironwood PERS, while ensuring that the carve-out categories are clearly delineated to prevent unintended cascade of investor-specific provisions. Specifically, insurance regulatory provisions (applicable to Pinnacle), ERISA/VCOC provisions (applicable to Northgate), and blocker entity access provisions should be carved out of MFN as relating to the specific legal, regulatory, or tax status of the benefited LP.

**Advisory Committee Seat.** Ironwood PERS will expect a guaranteed seat on the LPAC for Helen Tsao or her designee. This is a standard request for the largest LP and is consistent with LPAC governance best practices. Ironwood PERS expects to participate actively in conflict-of-interest reviews, valuation methodology reviews, and extension votes. We recommend granting this concession without qualification, as LPAC participation by the largest LP is both customary and valuable for Fund governance.

**Co-Investment Rights at No Fee / No Carry.** Ironwood PERS will seek the right of first offer on all co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund, with no additional management fee and no carried interest charged on co-invested capital. This is a material concession, as it allows Ironwood PERS to increase its exposure to the Fund\'s best investments at zero incremental cost. We recommend granting this concession, subject to the following limitations: (a) the right of first offer applies only to co-investment opportunities where the Fund\'s desired allocation exceeds the concentration limit (\$112,500,000 / 15% of aggregate commitments) or where CLSO GP otherwise determines in its sole discretion that a co-investment allocation is available; (b) the minimum allocation for Ironwood PERS co-investments will be calculated pro rata based on Ironwood PERS\'s commitment relative to total Fund commitments; and (c) CLSO GP retains discretion over the timing, structure, and terms of each co-investment opportunity, including the right to offer co-investment opportunities through a co-investment vehicle organized and managed by CLSO GP.

--

**3. Analysis and Recommendations.** The \$100,000,000 commitment from Ironwood PERS represents approximately 13.3% of the Fund\'s target size. This is a marquee anchor relationship that provides the Fund with substantial first-close capital, a credible institutional anchor investor for marketing purposes, and a relationship that, if successful, could yield follow-on commitments in future Cobalt Life Sciences vintage vehicles.

From a concessions perspective, the terms sought by Ironwood PERS are well within market norms for anchor investors of this size in life-sciences funds. Co-investment at no fee/no carry is increasingly standard for commitments of \$75,000,000 or more in the life-sciences sector, where deal sizes and concentration limits naturally create co-investment opportunities. The LPAC seat, FOIA protections, and placement agent disclosures are standard governmental plan requirements that impose minimal economic cost on the Fund or other LPs. The annual in-person reporting requirement is a modest operational commitment that builds relationship equity with a key investor.

We recommend granting the full suite of concessions described above to Ironwood PERS. The Ironwood PERS side letter will serve as the Tier 1 template from which other anchor investor side letters are derived, with investor-specific modifications for each anchor.

--
>
> 2\. **blocker Entity Access.** Provisions permitting investment through the blocker Corp or any similar corporate wrapper for UBTI management or statutory accounting purposes. *Justification:* blocker entity access is a tax and regulatory structuring accommodation that is investor-specific and that imposes incremental costs on the electing LP; it is not an economic concession that could be meaningfully elected by an LP without a tax or regulatory need for the blocker structure.
>
> 3\. **LPAC Seats.** Provisions guaranteeing or offering LPAC representation. *Justification:* LPAC seats are governance positions that are allocated based on commitment size, investor profile, and the overall composition of the committee. They are inherently limited in number (maximum seven members) and cannot be made available to all LPs through MFN election.
>
> 4\. **Co-Investment Rights at No Fee / No Carry (Above Threshold).** Co-investment rights at no additional management fee and no carried interest, to the extent such rights are offered only to investors with commitments above a specified commitment threshold (recommended: \$75,000,000). *Justification:* No-fee/no-carry co-investment rights represent a material economic concession that is offered as an incentive for anchor-level commitments. If these rights were MFN-eligible, they would be available to all MFN-eligible LPs (i.e., all LPs at \$25,000,000 or above), which would significantly dilute the value of the anchor commitment incentive and could create an impractical volume of co-investment demand.

> \(c\) **Enhanced Reporting:** Certain enhanced reporting obligations (e.g., clinical trial milestone tracking) may terminate upon the realization or write-off of the relevant portfolio investment.

**[F. Other States]{.underline}**

**New York.** Calderwood & Harkness LLP\'s main office is located in New York, and sagebrush Capital Partners LLC (the placement agent) is also based in New York. However, these entities are advisors to the Fund, not the Fund itself, and their New York presence does not independently create New York nexus for the Fund. Nonetheless, Fund activities conducted in New York --- including LP advisory committee meetings, annual meetings, marketing activities, and other events --- should be monitored to avoid creating New York nexus. New York\'s nexus rules for partnerships are broadly defined, and even limited activities in New York can trigger filing obligations if such activities constitute \"doing business\" in the state.

**Portfolio Company States.** The Fund\'s investment activities in various states will be analyzed on a deal-by-deal basis to determine whether state filing obligations arise. Each state has its own nexus rules for pass-through entities, and the Fund\'s obligation to file in a particular state depends on whether the Fund has income sourced to that state. States with significant biotech clusters --- including Massachusetts, California, New Jersey, Maryland, North Carolina, and Texas --- are the most likely sources of state filing obligations.
