**[IV. BACKGROUND: THE KEY-PERSON EVENT]{.underline}**

--

Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA provides, in relevant part, as follows:

> A \"Key Person Event\" shall be deemed to have occurred if a Key Person designated pursuant to Section 8.04(a) is \"unable to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Partnership for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days,\" absent the prior written notice of such Key Person delivered to the General Partner and each member of the Investor Advisory Committee setting forth the anticipated duration and reason for such absence.

No prior written notice was delivered by Whitmore, as his incapacitation was sudden and unexpected. The incapacitation commenced on June 3, 2024. The seven-consecutive-calendar-day period prescribed by Section 8.04(b) elapsed at 11:59 p.m. (Eastern Time) on June 9, 2024, and accordingly the Key Person Event was deemed triggered as of the close of business on June 10, 2024 (the first business day following the expiration of the seven-day period). The C&H engagement team confirmed this trigger date through a detailed analysis of the A&R LPA\'s definitions and day-count conventions, as set forth in the Key-Person Event Analysis Memorandum delivered to DCM on June 13, 2024.

--

**B. Phase 2: Successor Governance Framework Development (June 17--July 15, 2024)**

Following the delivery of the LP Notification Letter, the C&H engagement team commenced the development of a comprehensive successor governance framework. This workstream involved extensive consultation with Elaine R. Sato and other senior members of DCM\'s investment team, a review of industry best practices for key-person succession in institutional hedge fund structures, and an analysis of the expectations and concerns likely to be raised by the Fund\'s institutional limited partner base and the Investor Advisory Committee.

**Successor Governance Framework Memorandum.** C&H prepared and delivered to DCM a detailed Successor Governance Framework Memorandum setting forth the Firm\'s analysis and recommendations. The principal recommendations were as follows:

> \(a\) **Designation of Joint Successor Key Persons.** C&H recommended the designation of Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons under an amended Section 8.04. The recommendation was based on the complementary expertise and track records of the two individuals, their existing roles within DCM\'s investment process, and the need to demonstrate to the LP base that the Fund\'s multi-strategy mandate could be sustained without reliance on a single individual. The joint designation structure was also designed to address anticipated LP concerns regarding concentration of authority in a sole Key Person --- the very structure that had created the vulnerability exposed by Whitmore\'s incapacitation.
>
> \(b\) **Establishment of a Three-Member Investment Committee.** C&H recommended the creation of a formal Investment Committee under a new Section 8.05 of the A&R LPA. The Investment Committee was to be composed of three members: Sato (as Chair), Huang, and one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee. The inclusion of an IAC-designated independent member was intended to enhance governance credibility and LP confidence, and to provide an institutional check on investment decision-making in the absence of Whitmore.
>
> \(c\) **Revised Key-Person Clause Mechanics.** C&H recommended a revision to the key-person clause to reflect the joint designation structure. Specifically, the loss of one Successor Key Person would trigger a 180-day Replacement Period --- during which the remaining Successor Key Person and the Investment Committee could continue to manage the Fund --- rather than an automatic Investment Period suspension. Only the loss of both Successor Key Persons would trigger the automatic Investment Period suspension and standard cure mechanics previously applicable under Section 8.04. This tiered approach was designed to provide operational continuity while preserving meaningful LP protections.
>

Sato as authorized signatory) and countersigned by the Fund. **[3.4 Co-Investment by GP and HoldCo Members]{.underline}**

Any co-investment made by the General Partner, the ManCo, HoldCo Members, or their respective affiliates alongside the Fund shall be subject to the same terms (including entry price, equity structure, valuation, and governance rights) as the Fund\'s investment in the applicable Portfolio Company, except to the extent that any deviation from such terms is disclosed to and approved by the LPAC in advance of the closing of such co-investment.

GP and HoldCo Member co-investments are in addition to, and shall not reduce or offset, the GP\'s 1.5% general partner commitment to the Fund (approximately \$42,000,000 based on total commitments of approximately \$2.8 billion). The GP\'s general partner commitment shall continue to be funded in accordance with the LPA, and any co-investment by the GP or HoldCo Members shall be funded separately from such commitment.

>
> \(d\) **Same Terms.** All GP and HoldCo Member co-investments shall be made on the same terms as the Fund\'s investment, as described in Section 3.4 of this Policy, unless any deviation is disclosed to and approved by the LPAC.

We note that the Ardent Parties are working toward execution of all restructuring documents --- including the formation documents for Ardent Capital Holdings LLC, the amended and restated GP LLC agreement, and the management company reorganization agreements --- in late February 2024. LPAC notification letters are expected to be sent to the members of the Fund\'s Limited Partner Advisory Committee in early February. As you know, the LPAC of the Fund --- consisting of Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System, Crestwood Endowment Partners, Pinnacle Insurance Group, and Graystone Family Office LLC --- will need to consent to the overall restructuring, including the separation arrangements for Ms. Trask, pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA. Timely resolution of the separation terms is therefore important to the broader restructuring timeline and to the Ardent Parties\' ability to comply with their LP notification and consent obligations.

I am available to discuss any of the foregoing at your convenience. Nicholas Stern is also available for a principal-level discussion with you or your client, should that be helpful in advancing the remaining open items toward resolution.

In addition, the anticipated departures of two principals will trigger the Key Person provisions set forth in Section 5.2 of the LPA, requiring careful analysis and, potentially, a cure or waiver process. Calderwood & Harkness will also conduct a comprehensive review of all existing side-letter commitments entered into with the Fund\'s limited partners to ensure that the Restructuring does not result in any non-compliance with those obligations.

We also note that the Management Company is an SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD #298417). The Restructuring will require amendments to the Management Company\'s Form ADV, including Form ADV Part 2A brochure supplements, to reflect the changes in ownership, control persons, and key personnel. > \(h\) **LPAC Consent Solicitation.** Preparation of LPAC notification and consent solicitation letters, a detailed LPAC presentation memorandum describing the Restructuring and its rationale, and the form of written consent to be executed by LPAC members.
>
> \(i\) **LP Notification.** Drafting of notification letters to all 47 limited partners of the Fund regarding the completed Restructuring, including appropriate disclosure regarding changes in ownership, key personnel, and economics.
>
--
>
> \(ii\) Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan have authorized both firms to share information relevant to their respective scopes, subject to applicable privilege considerations. To the extent that either firm believes that the sharing of particular information may implicate privilege or confidentiality concerns, the matter should be raised with the client promptly so that appropriate safeguards can be put in place.
>
> \(iii\) Upon the closing of the Restructuring, Calderwood & Harkness will provide Pemberton Hale with copies of all executed Restructuring documents for Pemberton Hale\'s records and ongoing fund administration purposes. We expect this will include the executed LPA amendment, the new and amended operating agreements, the LPAC consent, the separation agreements (to the extent appropriate), and the amended Form ADV.
>
> \(iv\) Both firms should endeavor to avoid duplicative work. Any questions regarding scope allocation or the appropriate assignment of a particular matter should be directed to Nicholas Stern at Calderwood & Harkness (nstern@calderwoodharkness.com; (212) 404-7150) or Victoria Langford at Pemberton Hale, as applicable.

--
>
> 7\. Any existing co-investment allocation policies or guidelines applicable to the Fund.
>
> 8\. The Fund\'s most recent annual report and quarterly report (the latter reflecting the September 30, 2023 valuation). We understand the Fund\'s current performance reflects a gross MOIC of approximately 1.42x, a net IRR of approximately 14.7%, unrealized value of approximately \$2.33 billion, and realized proceeds of approximately \$445 million. These reports will assist us in preparing the LPAC presentation memorandum and LP notification letters.
>
> 9\. The placement agent agreement between Ardent Capital GP III LLC and Lockwood Placement Partners LLC (Sarah Fontaine, principal contact), including all schedules and exhibits, and in particular any tail-fee provisions that may be relevant to the Restructuring or that could be triggered by changes in the GP\'s ownership structure.
>
> 10\. A current schedule of LPAC members. We understand the LPAC currently includes Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System, Crestwood Endowment Partners, Pinnacle Insurance Group, and Graystone Family Office LLC, though we would appreciate confirmation and identification of any additional members.
>
> 11\. Any prior amendments to the LPA, the GP operating agreement, or the ManCo operating agreement, whether formal or by way of letter agreement, waiver, or consent.

--

We very much appreciate Pemberton Hale\'s cooperation and look forward to a productive working relationship between our two firms throughout the Restructuring process. We recognize the depth of institutional knowledge that your team has accumulated as formation and ongoing fund counsel for Ardent Capital Partners III LP, and we expect that our coordination will contribute meaningfully to the quality and efficiency of the work product on both sides.

We anticipate that the Restructuring will be completed within the next several months, with a target of achieving LPAC consent and executing definitive documentation by the end of the first quarter of 2024. Calderwood & Harkness will keep Pemberton Hale informed of key milestones as the Restructuring progresses.

Please do not hesitate to contact me directly at (212) 404-7150 or nstern@calderwoodharkness.com with any questions regarding scope delineation, the document request set forth above, or the Restructuring generally. We look forward to working with you and your team.

November 18, 2025

Adriana Voss, Esq. Vice President & General Counsel Pellegrino Capital Group LLC 1440 Brickell Avenue, Suite 3200 Miami, FL 33131

> **Re:** Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP in Connection with Pellegrino Capital Group LLC Co-Investment alongside Ridgeline Equity Partners Fund IV, L.P. in Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P.
>
> **Matter No.:** 1027-00002

Dear Ms. Voss:

**[1. Introduction and Purpose]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Pellegrino Capital Group LLC (\"Pellegrino\" or \"PCG\"), a Delaware limited liability company, in connection with Pellegrino\'s proposed Twenty-Five Million Dollar (\$25,000,000) co-investment alongside Ridgeline Equity Partners Fund IV, L.P. (\"Ridgeline Fund IV\") in Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P. (the \"Co-Invest Vehicle\"), a Delaware limited partnership formed for the purpose of facilitating co-investment alongside Ridgeline Fund IV.

As we understand the transaction, the Co-Invest Vehicle will co-invest alongside Ridgeline Fund IV in the equity of Clarion Holdings Acquisition Corp. (\"AcquisitionCo\"), a Delaware corporation formed to acquire one hundred percent (100%) of the equity interests of Clarion Hospitality Holdings, Inc. (\"Clarion\"), an integrated hospitality asset management platform headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee. The acquisition of Clarion by AcquisitionCo (the \"Acquisition\") is expected to be structured as a leveraged buyout, with the equity capitalization of AcquisitionCo funded through commitments from Ridgeline Fund IV, the Co-Invest Vehicle, and any other co-investment vehicles or equity participants designated by the sponsor.

Pellegrino\'s \$25,000,000 commitment to the Co-Invest Vehicle represents approximately thirty-three and one-third percent (33.33%) of the Co-Invest Vehicle\'s aggregate Seventy-Five Million Dollar (\$75,000,000) in commitments, and approximately ten percent (10.0%) of the total Two Hundred Fifty Million Dollar (\$250,000,000) equity capitalization of AcquisitionCo. We understand that the balance of the equity capitalization will be comprised of commitments from Ridgeline Fund IV and, potentially, other co-investment participants alongside the Co-Invest Vehicle.

This letter agreement (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions governing Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement by Pellegrino, including the scope of legal services to be provided, attorney staffing, fees and billing arrangements, conflict of interest disclosures, confidentiality obligations, and other terms and conditions of the attorney-client relationship. We ask that you review this Engagement Letter carefully and confirm Pellegrino\'s agreement to these terms by executing and returning a copy as described in Section 13 below.

**[2. Client Identification]{.underline}**
--
In addition, Calderwood & Harkness will draft and negotiate a side letter agreement (the \"Side Letter\") between Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC (the \"Co-Invest GP\") and Pellegrino. The Side Letter is intended to contain investor-specific protections and additional rights for the benefit of Pellegrino, including the following:

> \(a\) most-favored-nation (\"MFN\") rights, entitling Pellegrino to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable term or right granted to any other limited partner of the Co-Invest Vehicle in a side letter or other agreement, subject to customary exclusions;
>
> \(b\) a right to a seat on the limited partner advisory committee (\"LPAC\") of the Co-Invest Vehicle, or, if no LPAC is formed for the Co-Invest Vehicle, a right to a seat on the LPAC of Ridgeline Fund IV, to the extent such rights are available;
>
> \(c\) enhanced reporting rights, including quarterly unaudited financial statements, annual audited financial statements, and ad hoc reporting on material events affecting the Co-Invest Vehicle or the Acquisition;
>
> \(d\) ESG reporting covenants, requiring the Sponsor or the Co-Invest GP to provide Pellegrino with periodic environmental, social, and governance reporting with respect to Clarion and the portfolio, consistent with Pellegrino\'s own ESG reporting framework and investor disclosure obligations;
>
> \(e\) future co-investment allocation rights, entitling Pellegrino to a right of first offer or similar priority allocation right with respect to future co-investment opportunities originated by the Sponsor or Ridgeline Equity Management LLC in connection with Ridgeline Fund IV or any successor fund; and
>
> \(f\) excuse and exclusion protections, permitting Pellegrino to be excused from participation in, or excluded from the costs of, any investment or activity that would cause Pellegrino to violate applicable law, regulation, or any provision of its organizational documents or constituent fund documentation.

Calderwood & Harkness will also review, negotiate, and complete a subscription agreement (the \"Subscription Agreement\") for Pellegrino\'s Twenty-Five Million Dollar (\$25,000,000) limited partnership interest in the Co-Invest Vehicle, ensuring that the representations, warranties, and covenants contained therein are accurate and appropriate in the context of Pellegrino\'s organizational and regulatory status.

Finally, Calderwood & Harkness will assist Pellegrino with the completion of the investor questionnaire customarily required in connection with subscriptions of this nature, including representations and certifications relating to tax status (including U.S. tax-exempt status, if applicable), the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (\"FATCA\") and the Common Reporting Standard (\"CRS\"), the Office of Foreign Assets Control (\"OFAC\") sanctions programs, and anti-money laundering (\"AML\") requirements.
--
Calderwood & Harkness will prepare or coordinate the following deliverables in connection with the closing of Pellegrino\'s investment in the Co-Invest Vehicle:

> \(a\) a comprehensive closing checklist identifying all deliverables required in connection with the closing, the party responsible for preparation or delivery of each item, the applicable deadline or target date, and the current status of each item;
>
> \(b\) a funds flow memorandum detailing the movement of Pellegrino\'s Twenty-Five Million Dollar (\$25,000,000) capital contribution from Pellegrino\'s designated bank account, through the escrow account maintained by Continental Fiduciary Services, Inc. (the \"Escrow Agent\") pursuant to the terms of the applicable escrow agreement, to the Co-Invest Vehicle\'s account, and onward to AcquisitionCo in connection with the consummation of the Acquisition;
>
> \(c\) a legal opinion letter addressed to the Co-Invest GP, in customary form and substance, regarding the due organization, valid existence, and good standing of Pellegrino; the authorization by all necessary action of Pellegrino\'s execution, delivery, and performance of the Co-Invest LPA, the Side Letter, and the Subscription Agreement; and the enforceability of Pellegrino\'s obligations under such documents against Pellegrino in accordance with their respective terms, in each case subject to customary assumptions, qualifications, and exceptions; and
>
> \(d\) an officer\'s certificate or secretary\'s certificate of Pellegrino, certifying as to the authority of the person or persons executing the transaction documents on behalf of Pellegrino, the incumbency of such person or persons, and the authenticity of the organizational documents of Pellegrino delivered in connection with the closing.
--
> \(a\) Calderwood & Harkness is **not** engaged to provide legal advice with respect to the underlying Acquisition of Clarion, including but not limited to the conduct of business, legal, financial, or operational due diligence on Clarion\'s business, assets, liabilities, contracts, regulatory compliance, intellectual property, or workforce matters. Pellegrino should satisfy itself, through its own due diligence or through the diligence conducted by the Sponsor, that the Acquisition and the underlying business of Clarion meet Pellegrino\'s investment criteria.
>
> \(b\) Calderwood & Harkness is **not** engaged to provide legal advice with respect to the credit facility or any other debt financing provided by Pinnacle National Bank, N.A. or any other lender in connection with the Acquisition, including the terms of any credit agreement, security agreement, guarantee, or intercreditor arrangement.
>
> \(c\) Calderwood & Harkness is **not** engaged to advise on the interests, rights, or obligations of any party other than Pellegrino, including the Sponsor, the Co-Invest GP, Ridgeline Fund IV, AcquisitionCo, Clarion, any seller, or any other co-investor in the Co-Invest Vehicle (including without limitation Brindoval Growth Capital Fund II, L.P., to the extent it is a participant).
>
> \(d\) Calderwood & Harkness is **not** engaged to provide tax advice as a substitute for the engagement of Whitfield Greer & Associates LLP. Any tax analysis provided by Calderwood & Harkness is supplemental in nature and is intended to inform Pellegrino\'s understanding of the tax aspects of the co-investment structure; such analysis should be reviewed in conjunction with, and does not supersede, the independent advice of Whitfield Greer & Associates LLP.
>
> \(e\) Calderwood & Harkness does **not** represent Pellegrino in connection with any regulatory filings, including but not limited to filings under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, or filings with any state regulatory authority, unless separately agreed in writing.
--
If the scope of our engagement needs to be expanded or modified at any point, we will discuss the matter with you and, if appropriate, confirm any revised scope in a supplemental engagement letter or amendment to this Engagement Letter.

**[4. Staffing]{.underline}**

The following attorneys have been assigned to this engagement and will be the primary members of the Calderwood & Harkness team working on this matter:

**Responsible Partner:** Nicholas Stern, Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Stern will have overall responsibility for the engagement, including client relationship management, strategic direction, and supervision of all work product produced by the engagement team. Mr. Stern will serve as the primary point of contact for Pellegrino on significant issues, negotiations, and escalation matters.

**Billing Partner:** Graham Sutherland, Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Sutherland will serve as the billing partner for purposes of rate approvals, billing administration, and invoice review. Mr. Sutherland will also be available to provide substantive legal advice as needed on particular issues within his areas of expertise.

**Lead Associate:** Owen Fischer, Associate, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Fischer will serve as the day-to-day lead on document review, drafting, markup, and negotiation of the Co-Invest LPA, Side Letter, Subscription Agreement, and related transaction documents. Mr. Fischer will also be responsible for coordinating with Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP on document exchanges and turn schedules.

**Working Associate:** Stephen Adler, Associate, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Adler will support Mr. Fischer in connection with legal research, preparation of the closing checklist, drafting of the funds flow memorandum and certificates, and coordination of closing mechanics.

Additional attorneys, paralegals, or other professional staff may be assigned to this engagement from time to time as the needs of the matter require. We will endeavor to staff this matter efficiently and to avoid unnecessary duplication of effort. Pellegrino will be notified of any material changes in staffing, including the substitution of any of the named attorneys listed above.

**[5. Fees and Billing]{.underline}**

**5.1 Hourly Rates**

This engagement will be billed on an hourly basis at Calderwood & Harkness\'s standard rates for the attorneys and professional staff assigned to the matter. The current rates for 2025 are as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Timekeeper Category**             **2025 Hourly Rate Range**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
--

  Paralegals                          \$350 -- \$450 per hour
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The specific rate for each timekeeper will fall within the applicable range based on the individual\'s seniority and experience level. We will provide Pellegrino with a schedule of the specific rates applicable to each attorney and paralegal assigned to this matter upon request.

Rates are subject to periodic adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each calendar year. Calderwood & Harkness will notify Pellegrino in advance of any rate changes. Any adjusted rates will apply to services rendered on or after the effective date of the adjustment.

**5.2 Fee Estimate**
--
**[6. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness has conducted a conflicts check in connection with this engagement in accordance with the Firm\'s standard conflict clearance procedures. Based on that review, the Firm is not aware of any conflict of interest that would prevent it from representing Pellegrino in this matter under the applicable Florida Rules of Professional Conduct.

Specifically, Calderwood & Harkness does not currently represent, and has not in the recent past represented, any of the following entities in connection with this transaction or any related matter: Ridgeline Equity Partners Fund IV, L.P.; Ridgeline Equity Management LLC; Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC; Clarion Hospitality Holdings, Inc.; Clarion Holdings Acquisition Corp.; Brindoval Growth Capital Fund II, L.P.; Pinnacle National Bank, N.A.; or any of their respective affiliates, general partners, managing members, or portfolio companies, insofar as such representation would relate to the subject matter of this engagement.

Pellegrino acknowledges and agrees that Calderwood & Harkness is a large, multi-office law firm with a diverse client base, and that the Firm may from time to time represent other clients whose interests may be adverse to Pellegrino in matters that are unrelated to this engagement. Nothing in this Engagement Letter shall be construed to preclude or restrict Calderwood & Harkness from accepting or continuing any such representation, provided that (i) the matter in question does not involve the same or a substantially related matter as this engagement, and (ii) such representation does not create a direct and impermissible conflict of interest with respect to the Firm\'s obligations to Pellegrino under this Engagement Letter and the applicable Rules of Professional Conduct.

In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of this engagement, Calderwood & Harkness will promptly notify Pellegrino of the conflict and discuss appropriate steps to address it. Such steps may include, depending on the nature and severity of the conflict, the implementation of an ethical wall or information barrier within the Firm, the obtaining of an informed written waiver from the affected parties, or, if the conflict cannot be adequately resolved, the withdrawal of Calderwood & Harkness from the representation in accordance with Section 9 of this Engagement Letter.
--
> \(b\) Aldridge Mayer Stevens LLP, counsel to the seller(s) of Clarion, to the extent that the exchange of information with seller\'s counsel is reasonably required in connection with the co-investment closing process;
>
> \(c\) Whitfield Greer & Associates LLP, Pellegrino\'s independent tax and accounting advisor, in connection with the tax analysis and coordination described in Section 3.2 above; and
>
> \(d\) Continental Fiduciary Services, Inc., the Escrow Agent, in connection with the preparation and execution of the funds flow memorandum and the mechanics of capital contribution funding.

This authorization is limited to disclosures that are reasonably necessary for the purposes described above and does not constitute a general waiver of Pellegrino\'s right to confidentiality. Calderwood & Harkness will use reasonable efforts to ensure that any such disclosures are made in a manner that preserves applicable privileges, including the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine, to the greatest extent practicable.

**[8. Document Retention]{.underline}**
--
**[12. Miscellaneous]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter constitutes the entire agreement between Calderwood & Harkness and Pellegrino with respect to the terms and conditions of the engagement described herein and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous discussions, representations, and agreements, whether written or oral, relating to the subject matter hereof.

No amendment, modification, or waiver of any provision of this Engagement Letter shall be effective unless set forth in a writing signed by both Calderwood & Harkness and Pellegrino. No failure or delay by either party in exercising any right or remedy hereunder shall constitute a waiver thereof.

This matter has been assigned the internal reference number **1027-00002** within Calderwood & Harkness\'s matter management system. Pellegrino is requested to reference this matter number on all correspondence and communications directed to the Firm in connection with this engagement, including payment remittances, to ensure proper application and recordkeeping.

The provisions of Sections 5 (Fees and Billing), 7 (Confidentiality), 8 (Document Retention), 10 (Governing Law), and 11 (Limitation of Liability) shall survive the termination or completion of this engagement.

**[13. Acceptance]{.underline}**

If the foregoing terms are acceptable to Pellegrino, we respectfully request that Adriana Voss, in her capacity as Vice President & General Counsel of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC, sign and date this Engagement Letter in the space provided below and return one fully executed copy to the undersigned at your earliest convenience. A countersigned copy may be returned via email (PDF) to nstern@calderwoodharkness.com or via hand delivery or overnight courier to our office address set forth above.

We are genuinely enthusiastic about the opportunity to work with Pellegrino Capital Group and the broader PCG team on this co-investment alongside Ridgeline Fund IV. We are confident that our Funds & Asset Management Practice Group is well positioned to provide Pellegrino with the high-quality legal counsel and responsive client service that this transaction requires, and we look forward to a successful collaboration.

Please do not hesitate to contact me or Owen Fischer if you have any questions regarding this Engagement Letter or if you wish to discuss any of its provisions.

> Very truly yours,
--
By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Name: Nicholas Stern

Title: Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group

Date: November 18, 2025

**ACKNOWLEDGMENT AND ACCEPTANCE**

The undersigned hereby acknowledges receipt of this Engagement Letter dated November 18, 2025, and confirms that Pellegrino Capital Group LLC agrees to the terms and conditions set forth herein.

ACKNOWLEDGED AND AGREED:

PELLEGRINO CAPITAL GROUP LLC

Without limiting the generality of Section 7.1, the General Partner shall have the power and authority, on behalf of and in the name of the Partnership, to, among other things:

\(a\) Make, hold, monitor, and dispose of the Investment, including the exercise of all rights of the Partnership as a holder of AcquisitionCo Equity, such as voting rights, consent rights, and information rights;

\(b\) Execute, deliver, and perform all contracts, agreements, instruments, and documents on behalf of the Partnership, including the execution of closing documents in connection with the Acquisition;

\(c\) Borrow money and incur indebtedness on behalf of the Partnership, grant security interests in Partnership assets, and guarantee obligations of AcquisitionCo or its subsidiaries, subject to the limitations set forth in Section 7.3;

\(d\) Open, maintain, and close bank accounts and other financial accounts in the name of the Partnership, and draw checks, drafts, and other orders for the payment of money;
--
\(l\) Institute, defend, settle, or compromise any litigation, arbitration, or other proceeding on behalf of the Partnership; and

\(m\) Take any and all other actions as the General Partner deems necessary, advisable, or incidental to carry out the purposes of the Partnership.

**Section 7.3 --- Actions Requiring LPAC Approval**

Notwithstanding the broad authority granted to the General Partner under Sections 7.1 and 7.2, the following actions shall require the prior written approval of a majority of the members of the LPAC (i.e., at least two (2) of three (3) LPAC members):

\(a\) Any borrowing by the Partnership in an aggregate principal amount in excess of One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000), other than short-term borrowings to bridge the funding of Capital Contributions pending receipt thereof from the Limited Partners;

\(b\) Any amendment to this Agreement that adversely affects the economic or governance rights of the Limited Partners, including any amendment to the Distribution waterfall, the Preferred Return, the Carried Interest Percentage, or the LPAC provisions;

\(c\) Any transaction or arrangement between the Partnership, on the one hand, and the General Partner, Ridgeline Management, or any Affiliate thereof, on the other hand (each, a \"conflict transaction\"), including any fee, compensation, or reimbursement arrangement not expressly contemplated by this Agreement;

\(d\) Any Distribution in kind (as set forth in Section 6.7);
--
\(a\) The Partnership shall invest in AcquisitionCo on terms and conditions no less favorable in all material respects than those applicable to Fund IV\'s investment in AcquisitionCo. The Investment shall be made on a pari passu basis with Fund IV, and the Partnership shall be entitled to the same class and type of AcquisitionCo Equity as Fund IV, with the same rights, preferences, privileges, and restrictions.

\(b\) Based on the equity contributions of the Partnership and Fund IV, the Partnership\'s ownership of AcquisitionCo shall be thirty percent (30%) (representing Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000) of Two Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$250,000,000) of total equity invested) and Fund IV\'s ownership shall be seventy percent (70%) (representing One Hundred Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$175,000,000) of Two Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$250,000,000) of total equity invested).

\(c\) Following the Closing, the management rollover equity of approximately Thirty Million Dollars (\$30,000,000) contributed by Theodore \"Ted\" J. Barrington and Lisa M. Kwon (each, members of Clarion\'s management team) shall dilute all existing equity holders of AcquisitionCo, including the Partnership and Fund IV, on a proportional basis.

\(d\) The Partnership shall participate in any disposition of all or any portion of the Investment on a pro rata basis with Fund IV, at the same price per unit and on the same terms and conditions.

**Section 7.5 --- Expenses**
--
**Section 7.7 --- Delegation**

The General Partner may delegate any of its powers, duties, and responsibilities hereunder to any officer, employee, agent, or Affiliate of the General Partner or Ridgeline Management; provided, however, that no such delegation shall relieve the General Partner of its obligations and liabilities under this Agreement or under the Act, and the General Partner shall remain fully responsible and liable for any act or omission of any delegate to the same extent as if such act or omission were the act or omission of the General Partner.

**Section 7.8 --- Standard of Care; Exculpation**

The General Partner shall manage the business and affairs of the Partnership in good faith and in a manner it reasonably believes to be in the best interests of the Partnership. No Covered Person shall be liable to the Partnership or to any Partner for any act or omission taken or suffered by such Covered Person in good faith and reasonably believed by such Covered Person to be in, or not opposed to, the best interests of the Partnership, provided that such act or omission does not constitute fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, or a material breach of this Agreement. The General Partner shall not be liable for any error of judgment or for any mistake of fact or law. No Covered Person shall be obligated to guarantee the return of any Partner\'s Capital Contributions or a profit for any Partner from the operations of the Partnership.

**Section 7.9 --- Indemnification**
--
\(c\) Each Limited Partner may elect to exercise its Tag-Along Right by delivering written notice to the General Partner within fifteen (15) Business Days of receipt of the Tag-Along Notice. Any Limited Partner that does not deliver a timely election notice shall be deemed to have waived its Tag-Along Right with respect to such Tag-Along Sale.

\(d\) Each Limited Partner exercising its Tag-Along Right may include in such Tag-Along Sale up to one hundred percent (100%) of its proportionate interest in the AcquisitionCo Equity (determined based on the Partnership\'s proportionate ownership of AcquisitionCo and such Limited Partner\'s Partnership Percentage).

\(e\) The closing of any Tag-Along Sale shall be conditioned upon the participation of all Limited Partners that have timely exercised their Tag-Along Rights.

**Section 8.6 --- Drag-Along Rights**

\(a\) If the General Partner determines, in its sole discretion, to sell one hundred percent (100%) of the AcquisitionCo Equity held by the Partnership and Fund IV to a third party (a \"**Drag-Along Sale**\"), the General Partner may require all Limited Partners to sell their proportionate interests in the AcquisitionCo Equity (indirectly, through the Partnership) on the same terms and conditions as Fund IV (the \"**Drag-Along Right**\").
--
\(c\) In any Drag-Along Sale, each Limited Partner shall receive its proportionate share of the sale proceeds in accordance with the Distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.2.

\(d\) In connection with any Drag-Along Sale, the representations and warranties required of the dragged Limited Partners shall be limited to (i) title to and ownership of their Partnership Interests, (ii) authority and power to enter into and perform the sale transaction, and (iii) the absence of encumbrances on their Partnership Interests. No Limited Partner shall be required to make any representations or warranties with respect to the business, assets, liabilities, operations, or financial condition of AcquisitionCo, Clarion, or any of their respective subsidiaries.

\(e\) Each Limited Partner hereby agrees to take all actions and execute all documents reasonably requested by the General Partner to consummate a Drag-Along Sale, including execution of purchase agreements, closing certificates, and related instruments.

**Section 8.7 --- Substitute Limited Partners**

A permitted transferee of a Partnership Interest shall be admitted to the Partnership as a substitute Limited Partner only upon satisfaction of all conditions set forth in Section 8.2 and execution and delivery of such documentation as the General Partner may reasonably require, including a joinder agreement substantially in the form of Exhibit A. Upon admission as a substitute Limited Partner, the transferee shall succeed to all of the rights and obligations of the transferring Limited Partner with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest, and the transferring Limited Partner shall be released from all obligations hereunder with respect to the transferred Partnership Interest (other than obligations that accrued prior to the effective date of such Transfer). The General Partner shall promptly update Schedule A to reflect any such substitution.

**[ARTICLE IX --- LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE (LPAC)]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Establishment and Composition**

The Partnership shall establish a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\") consisting of three (3) members. The members of the LPAC shall be appointed by the General Partner from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives; provided, however, that Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be entitled to appoint one (1) member of the LPAC for so long as Pellegrino Capital Group LLC holds a Partnership Interest in the Partnership. LPAC members shall serve in a non-fiduciary, advisory capacity, except where specific approval or consent rights are expressly conferred upon the LPAC by this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, LPAC members shall not owe any fiduciary duties to the Partnership or to any other Partner by virtue of their service on the LPAC.

**Section 9.2 --- LPAC Functions**

The LPAC shall have the following functions and responsibilities:

\(a\) Review and approve (or disapprove) conflict transactions between the Partnership and the General Partner or any of its Affiliates as contemplated by Section 7.3(c);

\(b\) Review and approve (or disapprove) all other matters requiring LPAC consent as set forth in Section 7.3;

\(c\) Consult with the General Partner regarding valuations of the Investment, including the methodology and inputs used for such valuations;

\(d\) Review and approve (or disapprove) any proposed Distributions in kind pursuant to Section 6.7;
--
\(e\) Consult with the General Partner regarding the management transition plan in connection with a Key Person Event pursuant to Section 10.1; and

\(f\) Perform such other advisory functions as the General Partner may request from time to time, including review of the Partnership\'s annual financial statements and consultation on material strategic matters relating to the Investment.

**Section 9.3 --- LPAC Meetings**

\(a\) The LPAC shall meet at least once per calendar year, or more frequently as the General Partner or any two (2) LPAC members may request. Meetings may be held in person at the offices of the General Partner, by video conference, or by telephonic conference, as determined by the General Partner in consultation with the LPAC members.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least ten (10) Business Days\' prior written notice of each meeting to all LPAC members, together with a written agenda and copies of any relevant materials to be discussed at such meeting.

\(c\) A quorum for any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members). Actions of the LPAC shall be taken by the affirmative vote or written consent of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members).

\(d\) Actions may be taken by the LPAC without a meeting by written consent signed by a majority of the LPAC members, which consent shall be effective as of the date of the last signature.

\(e\) The General Partner shall prepare and distribute to all LPAC members written minutes of each meeting within fifteen (15) Business Days following such meeting.

**Section 9.4 --- Indemnification of LPAC Members**

Each member of the LPAC shall be indemnified by the Partnership on the same basis as Covered Persons under Section 7.9 with respect to any Losses incurred by such member arising out of or in connection with such member\'s service on the LPAC. LPAC members acting in good faith in the performance of their duties as LPAC members shall have no personal liability to the Partnership, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner for any actions taken or omitted to be taken in their advisory capacity as LPAC members.

**Section 9.5 --- Removal and Replacement**

\(a\) The General Partner may remove any LPAC member for Cause upon written notice to such LPAC member and the Limited Partner that appointed or designated such member.

\(b\) Any Limited Partner that appointed or designated an LPAC member may, at any time, designate a replacement for such LPAC member by written notice to the General Partner, and such replacement shall become effective upon receipt of such notice by the General Partner.

\(c\) In the event of a vacancy on the LPAC (whether by removal, resignation, or otherwise), the General Partner shall appoint a replacement LPAC member from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives within thirty (30) days of such vacancy; provided, however, that any vacancy in the LPAC seat held by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be filled by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC.

**[ARTICLE X --- KEY PERSON; EXCUSE RIGHTS]{.underline}**

> Re: Legal Opinion --- Subscription by Pellegrino Capital Group LLC for a Limited Partnership Interest in Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P.

Ladies and Gentlemen:

We have acted as counsel to Pellegrino Capital Group LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (\"Pellegrino\" or the \"Subscriber\"), in connection with Pellegrino\'s subscription for a limited partnership interest in Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P., a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Partnership\" or the \"Co-Invest Vehicle\"). The Co-Invest Vehicle\'s general partner is Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the \"General Partner\"). This opinion letter is delivered pursuant to the requirements of the Subscription Agreement (as defined below) and the Partnership Agreement (as defined below) in connection with the closing of the transactions contemplated thereby occurring on January 30, 2026 (the \"Closing\"). In connection with the Closing, Pellegrino has committed to make capital contributions to the Partnership in an aggregate amount of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) (the \"Capital Commitment\"), subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the Transaction Documents (as defined below).

This opinion letter is being furnished to you in your capacity as General Partner of the Partnership and is delivered in satisfaction of the condition precedent set forth in the Subscription Agreement requiring delivery of an opinion of counsel to the Subscriber in connection with the Closing.

**[I. Documents Examined]{.underline}**

In connection with the opinions set forth herein, we have examined originals or copies (certified or otherwise identified to our satisfaction) of the following documents:

> 1\. Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P., dated as of January 30, 2026, by and among the General Partner and the limited partners party thereto, as the same may be amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time (the \"Partnership Agreement\" or the \"LPA\");
>
> 2\. Side Letter Agreement, dated as of January 30, 2026, by and between Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC and Pellegrino Capital Group LLC (the \"Side Letter\");
>
> 3\. Subscription Agreement, dated as of January 30, 2026, executed by Pellegrino Capital Group LLC in connection with its subscription for a limited partnership interest in the Partnership (the \"Subscription Agreement,\" and together with the Partnership Agreement and the Side Letter, collectively, the \"Transaction Documents\");
>
> 4\. Certificate of Formation of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC, as filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on July 12, 2019, together with all amendments thereto as of the date hereof (collectively, the \"Certificate of Formation\");
>
> 5\. Limited Liability Company Agreement (Operating Agreement) of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC, dated as of July 15, 2019, as amended by that certain First Amendment to the Limited Liability Company Agreement, dated as of March 1, 2021, and that certain Second Amendment to the Limited Liability Company Agreement, dated as of September 15, 2023 (as so amended, the \"Operating Agreement\");
>
> 6\. Certificate of Good Standing of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC, issued by the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, dated January 28, 2026 (the \"Good Standing Certificate\");
>
> 7\. Certificate of Authorization and Resolutions of the Managing Member of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC, dated January 30, 2026, adopted by Marco A. Pellegrino, in his capacity as Founder and Managing Member, authorizing the execution, delivery, and performance of the Transaction Documents and the consummation of the transactions contemplated thereby (the \"Authorizing Resolutions\");
>
> 8\. Officer\'s Certificate and Secretary\'s Certificate of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC, dated January 30, 2026, certifying as to the incumbency of certain officers and authorized signatories, the authenticity and current effectiveness of the organizational documents of Pellegrino, and the adoption of the Authorizing Resolutions (the \"Officer\'s Certificate\"); and
>
> 9\. Such other documents, records, agreements, instruments, certificates, and statements of governmental officials and officers and representatives of Pellegrino as we have deemed necessary or appropriate as a basis for the opinions expressed herein.

The documents referenced in items (1) through (3) above are collectively referred to herein as the \"Transaction Documents.\" The documents referenced in items (1) through (9) above, together with any other documents, records, and materials reviewed by us in connection with the preparation of this opinion letter, are collectively referred to herein as the \"Reviewed Documents.\"
--
In rendering the opinions set forth herein, we have assumed, without independent investigation or verification, the following:

> \(a\) All signatures on all documents examined by us are genuine, and all documents submitted to us as originals are authentic and complete. All documents submitted to us as copies, whether certified or otherwise, conform to the authentic originals of such documents, and all such originals are authentic and complete.
>
> \(b\) Each party to the Transaction Documents (other than Pellegrino) has the requisite organizational power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform its respective obligations under such documents, and each such document has been duly authorized by all necessary organizational action on the part of each such party (other than Pellegrino), has been duly executed and delivered by each such party (other than Pellegrino), and constitutes the legal, valid, and binding obligation of each such party (other than Pellegrino), enforceable against such party in accordance with its terms.
>
> \(c\) The Transaction Documents accurately reflect the complete agreement of the parties thereto with respect to the subject matter thereof, and there are no oral or written agreements, understandings, or arrangements between or among the parties that would modify, amend, or supplement the terms of the Transaction Documents or that would otherwise be relevant to the opinions expressed herein.
>
> \(d\) All natural persons who have executed any of the Reviewed Documents or any other documents, instruments, or certificates in connection with the transactions contemplated by the Transaction Documents have sufficient legal capacity to do so.
>
> \(e\) The Good Standing Certificate referred to in Section I above remains accurate and complete as of the date hereof, and no event has occurred since the date of the Good Standing Certificate that would adversely affect the good standing of Pellegrino under the laws of the State of Delaware.
>
> \(f\) All factual representations and warranties made by Pellegrino in the Transaction Documents, the Investor Questionnaire completed by Pellegrino in connection with its subscription for a limited partnership interest in the Partnership, and the Officer\'s Certificate are true, correct, and complete in all material respects as of the date hereof and as of the date of each such document.
>
> \(g\) No provision of any agreement, instrument, order, judgment, decree, or other document or arrangement binding on Pellegrino (other than those agreements and instruments specifically identified in Section I above and reviewed by us in connection with the preparation of this opinion letter) conflicts with, or would be violated or breached by, the execution, delivery, or performance by Pellegrino of the Transaction Documents or the consummation by Pellegrino of the transactions contemplated thereby.
>
> \(h\) The laws of the State of Delaware as applied to the formation, organization, existence, and operation of Pellegrino have been, and will continue to be, complied with in all material respects.
>
> \(i\) Pellegrino has paid all franchise taxes and filing fees required to be paid to the State of Delaware in order to maintain its good standing as a limited liability company under the laws of the State of Delaware.
--
Pellegrino Capital Group LLC is a limited liability company duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware. Pellegrino was formed under the Delaware Limited Liability Company Act, 6 Del. C. § 18-101 *et seq.*, by the filing of its Certificate of Formation with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware. As reflected in the organizational documents of Pellegrino examined by us, Pellegrino\'s federal employer identification number is 84-3291047. Based upon our review of the Good Standing Certificate, Pellegrino is in good standing as a limited liability company under the laws of the State of Delaware as of the date of such certificate, and, based upon the assumptions set forth in Section II above, we have no reason to believe that Pellegrino\'s good standing status has changed since the date of such certificate.

**Opinion 2 --- Power and Authority**

Pellegrino has full limited liability company power and authority under its Certificate of Formation and Operating Agreement to: (a) execute and deliver each of the Transaction Documents, including the Partnership Agreement, the Side Letter, and the Subscription Agreement; (b) perform its obligations under each of the Transaction Documents, including, without limitation, its obligation to contribute capital to the Partnership in an aggregate amount equal to the Capital Commitment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), subject to and in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth in the Partnership Agreement and the Subscription Agreement; and (c) carry on its business as presently conducted to the extent relevant to the consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Transaction Documents. The Operating Agreement of Pellegrino vests in Marco A. Pellegrino, in his capacity as Founder and Managing Member, the requisite authority to authorize and approve the execution, delivery, and performance of agreements and instruments on behalf of Pellegrino, including the Transaction Documents, and to bind Pellegrino in connection therewith. As reflected in the Authorizing Resolutions, Marco A. Pellegrino has duly exercised such authority with respect to the Transaction Documents and the transactions contemplated thereby.

**Opinion 3 --- Due Authorization, Execution, and Delivery**

The execution, delivery, and performance by Pellegrino of each of the Transaction Documents have been duly authorized by all necessary limited liability company action on the part of Pellegrino. The Authorizing Resolutions were duly adopted by Marco A. Pellegrino, in his capacity as Founder and Managing Member of Pellegrino, in accordance with the Operating Agreement. Based upon our review of the Operating Agreement, no vote, consent, or approval of any other member of Pellegrino or any other person is required under the Operating Agreement or the Certificate of Formation for the authorization, execution, delivery, and performance of the Transaction Documents or the consummation of the transactions contemplated thereby. Each of the Transaction Documents has been duly executed and delivered by or on behalf of Pellegrino by a duly authorized signatory of Pellegrino acting within the scope of such signatory\'s authority.

**Opinion 4 --- Enforceability**

Each of the Transaction Documents constitutes the legal, valid, and binding obligation of Pellegrino, enforceable against Pellegrino in accordance with its respective terms, except as such enforceability may be limited by the Enforceability Exceptions (as defined in Section V below).

**Opinion 5 --- No Violation / No Conflict**

The execution, delivery, and performance by Pellegrino of the Transaction Documents and the consummation by Pellegrino of the transactions contemplated thereby do not and will not:

> \(a\) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of, or constitute a default under, or result in the termination of, or accelerate the performance required by, or result in the creation of any lien or encumbrance upon any property or assets of Pellegrino pursuant to, the Certificate of Formation or the Operating Agreement of Pellegrino;
>
> \(b\) violate any applicable law, statute, rule, regulation, order, judgment, or decree of the State of Delaware applicable to Pellegrino or any of its properties or assets, in each case limited to those laws of the State of Delaware as to which we have rendered opinions herein; or
--
> 2\. **Equitable Principles Exception.** The effect of general principles of equity (regardless of whether such enforceability is considered in a proceeding in equity or at law), including, without limitation, principles relating to the implied covenants of good faith and fair dealing, unconscionability, reasonableness, materiality, the availability of specific performance, injunctive relief, and other equitable remedies (which are subject to the discretion of the court before which any proceeding therefor may be brought), and the exercise of judicial discretion in accordance with general equitable principles.
>
> 3\. **Public Policy Limitation.** The extent to which certain provisions of the Transaction Documents may be rendered unenforceable as contrary to public policy as determined by a court of competent jurisdiction, including, without limitation, provisions purporting to waive or limit statutory rights or constitutional protections that are not subject to waiver by agreement of the parties.
>
> 4\. **Indemnification and Contribution Limitation.** The enforceability of provisions of the Transaction Documents relating to indemnification, contribution, or exculpation may be limited by applicable law or public policy considerations, including, without limitation, limitations imposed by applicable securities laws (including, where applicable, judicial interpretations of Section 17 of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended), and the general principle that indemnification and exculpation provisions may not be enforceable to the extent they purport to indemnify or exculpate a party for its own fraud, willful misconduct, bad faith, or gross negligence.
>
> 5\. **Waiver Limitations.** Provisions of the Transaction Documents relating to waivers of rights or defenses, including, without limitation, waivers of the right to trial by jury, waivers of rights to receive notices otherwise required by law, waivers of statutes of limitations, and waivers of rights to interpose counterclaims or raise defenses, may not be enforceable in all circumstances, and the enforcement of such provisions is subject to the discretion of the court before which any such matter may be presented.
>
> 6\. **Choice of Law and Forum Selection.** While the Transaction Documents designate the laws of the State of Delaware as the governing law thereof, no assurance can be given that a court in any particular jurisdiction would honor such designation in all respects, particularly if the application of Delaware law would be contrary to a fundamental policy of a jurisdiction that has a materially greater interest in the determination of a particular issue. Similarly, any consent-to-jurisdiction or forum-selection provisions contained in the Transaction Documents may not be enforceable in all circumstances and are subject to the discretion of the court before which any such matter is presented, including considerations of convenience, fairness, and public policy.
--

Where our opinions or statements herein are qualified by the phrase \"known to us,\" \"to our knowledge,\" or words of similar import, such knowledge is limited to the actual, current knowledge (as distinguished from constructive or imputed knowledge) of Nicholas Stern, Owen Fischer, and Stephen Adler, the attorneys at this firm who have had primary and substantive involvement in the representation of Pellegrino in connection with the transactions contemplated by the Transaction Documents, and does not include knowledge of any other attorney at Calderwood & Harkness LLP or any of its affiliated offices. We trust the foregoing is satisfactory for your purposes. Should you have any questions regarding this opinion letter or any of the matters addressed herein, please do not hesitate to contact the undersigned.
