>
> • *FOIA/public records carve-outs* --- The side letter includes provisions designed to protect Fund confidential information from disclosure under state freedom of information and public records laws to which CPERS is subject as a governmental entity, while acknowledging CPERS\'s statutory obligation to comply with valid requests.
>
> • *Enhanced quarterly reporting* --- CPERS has negotiated enhanced quarterly reporting deliverables, including sector-level attribution data and disaggregated performance metrics by investment stage, beyond the standard quarterly reporting package provided to all limited partners under the LPA.
>
> • *Co-investment rights* --- CPERS has negotiated the right to co-invest alongside the Fund in portfolio company transactions on a no-management-fee, no-carried-interest basis, subject to the GP\'s allocation discretion and the co-investment allocation policy described in the LPA.

**Northstar Endowment Partners LLC (NEP):**

> • *Advisory committee seat* --- NEP has been granted a seat on the Fund\'s limited partner advisory committee (\"LPAC\"), an Excluded Provision under the MFN framework (see Section III.B below).
>
> • *Key-person event notification* --- NEP has negotiated a provision requiring the GP to provide written notice to NEP within five (5) business days of the occurrence of a key-person event involving either Rajesh Mehta or Claire Dubois, in addition to the standard key-person event notification provisions set forth in the LPA.
>
> • *Transfer rights* --- NEP has the right to transfer all or a portion of its limited partnership interest to affiliated endowment vehicles of Veltrano University without GP consent, provided that the transferee executes a joinder to the LPA and meets applicable anti-money laundering and know-your-customer requirements.
>
> • *ERISA representation waiver* --- The GP has agreed to waive certain representations regarding the Fund\'s compliance with the \"plan assets\" regulations under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (\"ERISA\"), acknowledging NEP\'s representations that its assets do not constitute plan assets subject to ERISA.
>
> • *Co-investment rights* --- NEP has co-investment rights on terms substantially similar to those granted to CPERS, though the NEP side letter does not explicitly state \"no management fee, no carried interest\" with respect to co-investment vehicles and instead provides for co-investment on \"terms to be determined by the GP at the time of allocation.\"

**Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP (Brindoval):**

> • *Competitive investment opt-out* --- Brindoval has the right to opt out of any Fund investment in a portfolio company that competes directly with certain SaaS businesses owned or controlled by the Raines family (the principals of Brindoval), as identified on a schedule annexed to the Brindoval side letter.
>
> • *Fee netting against carried interest* --- Brindoval has negotiated a provision under which management fees paid by Brindoval during the investment period will be netted against carried interest distributions otherwise allocable to the GP with respect to Brindoval\'s limited partnership interest, effectively treating management fees as an advance against carry.
>
> • *Information rights* --- Brindoval has negotiated information rights aligned with the Institutional Limited Partners Association (\"ILPA\") Reporting Best Practices, including access to standardized reporting templates, fee and expense disclosures, and ESG reporting metrics.
>
> • *Co-investment rights* --- Brindoval has co-investment rights, though the specific economic terms of such co-investments are not specified in the side letter and are subject to the GP\'s standard co-investment terms at the time of allocation.

**MFN Eligibility of Non-Fee Provisions.** It is important to note that CPERS\'s co-investment rights --- specifically, the right to co-invest on a no-management-fee, no-carried-interest basis --- constitute an MFN-eligible provision that, if elected by subsequent limited partners, would compound the economic impact on the GP beyond the management fee reductions analyzed below. A subsequent LP that elects CPERS\'s no-fee/no-carry co-investment terms could effectively reduce the GP\'s economics on co-investment transactions to zero with respect to that LP\'s co-investment allocation. The analysis in Section IV of this memorandum focuses on management fee exposure from MFN elections, but we flag the co-investment fee/carry waiver as an additional source of economic risk warranting further analysis.

**[III. MFN Framework --- Eligibility and Excluded Provisions]{.underline}**

**[A. MFN Eligibility]{.underline}**

Under the MFN provisions set forth in the LPA and reflected in each anchor side letter, the right to make MFN elections is available to limited partners that have committed at least \$25,000,000 to the Fund (the \"MFN Threshold\"). Limited partners whose commitments fall below the MFN Threshold are not eligible to participate in the MFN election process and will not receive the MFN Side Letter Compilation.

All three anchor limited partners meet the MFN Threshold. Brindoval, as the smallest anchor investor at \$40,000,000, exceeds the \$25,000,000 threshold by \$15,000,000. As a practical matter, the MFN Threshold is relevant only to subsequent limited partners, as the anchor investors\' side letter terms are already negotiated and finalized.

For purposes of the modeling in Section IV below, we have assumed that all subsequent limited partner commitments in the MFN-eligible pool exceed \$25,000,000. This assumption is reasonable given the Fund\'s target size of \$600,000,000 and the typical institutional check sizes for a venture fund of this scale. Based on preliminary indications from Greystone Capital Advisors LLC, the Fund\'s placement agent, the anticipated subsequent LP base is composed primarily of institutional investors --- including pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, foundations, insurance company general accounts, and large family offices --- whose commitment sizes are expected to range from \$25,000,000 to \$100,000,000. While there may be a small number of commitments below the MFN Threshold (e.g., from smaller family offices or fund-of-funds vehicles), these are expected to represent a de minimis portion of total subsequent LP capital and would not materially affect the modeling results.

It should be noted that the MFN Threshold applies to the aggregate commitment of a limited partner, not to the commitment of affiliated vehicles. The LPA does not currently aggregate commitments of affiliated investors for purposes of the MFN Threshold. Owen and Nicholas may wish to consider whether the LPA should be amended prior to First Close to include an aggregation provision, which could either expand or restrict the MFN-eligible pool depending on the composition of the subsequent LP base.

**[B. Excluded Provisions]{.underline}**

The MFN framework in the LPA identifies certain categories of side letter provisions that are excluded from MFN election (each, an \"Excluded Provision\"). Specifically, the following provisions cannot be elected by a subsequent LP through the MFN process:

> 1\. Provisions granted to satisfy specific legal, regulatory, or tax requirements of the limited partner to which such provisions were originally granted (e.g., FOIA and public records carve-outs for governmental plans such as CPERS; representations and acknowledgments regarding the inapplicability of ERISA to a particular LP\'s investment).
>
> 2\. Advisory committee seats, including the LPAC seat granted to NEP.
>
> 3\. Portfolio company board observer rights.
>
> 4\. Any other term or provision that the GP reasonably determines is specific to the legal, regulatory, or tax status of the limited partner that originally received such term or provision and is not applicable to the electing limited partner.

**Fee Concessions Are MFN-Eligible.** Critically, management fee concessions are *not* listed among the Excluded Provisions and are therefore MFN-eligible. This is the primary source of economic exposure analyzed in this memorandum. The LPA\'s silence on fee concessions as Excluded Provisions is consistent with the general market practice in Delaware fund formation, where MFN provisions are typically drafted to encompass fee terms unless a specific carve-out is negotiated.

**Co-Investment Fee/Carry Waivers Are MFN-Eligible.** Similarly, co-investment terms --- including the no-management-fee, no-carried-interest co-investment terms negotiated by CPERS --- are not listed as Excluded Provisions and are therefore MFN-eligible. As noted in Section II.C, this creates an additional vector of economic exposure beyond management fees.

**Excuse Rights and Opt-Out Provisions.** The treatment of excuse rights and competitive opt-out provisions under the MFN framework requires case-by-case analysis. CPERS\'s excuse rights (tobacco/firearms) are directly linked to CPERS\'s publicly adopted investment policy restrictions as a governmental plan and are likely excludable under Category 1 or Category 4 of the Excluded Provisions framework. By contrast, Brindoval\'s competitive investment opt-out --- which is tied to the Raines family\'s private business interests rather than to any legal or regulatory requirement applicable to Brindoval --- presents a less clear case for exclusion. If a subsequent LP sought to elect Brindoval\'s competitive opt-out right, the GP would need to evaluate whether the provision is \"specific to the legal, regulatory, or tax status\" of Brindoval within the meaning of Category 4. In our view, the competitive opt-out is more accurately characterized as a commercial accommodation than a regulatory necessity, and the GP\'s ability to exclude it from MFN election is uncertain.
--
**[C. Timing]{.underline}**

The MFN election process is governed by the following timeline:

> • **Final Close:** July 15, 2026 (the deadline for the admission of additional limited partners to the Fund).
>
> • **MFN Side Letter Compilation:** The GP is required to prepare and deliver to each MFN-eligible limited partner a redacted compilation of all side letter provisions granted to any limited partner, excluding (a) the identity of the limited partner to which each provision was originally granted and (b) Excluded Provisions. The Compilation must be delivered within fifteen (15) business days after the Final Close.
>
> • **MFN Election Period:** Each MFN-eligible limited partner has thirty (30) calendar days following delivery of the Compilation to submit its MFN election notice to the GP, identifying the specific provisions it elects to adopt.

The practical implication of this timeline is significant for budget planning purposes. Assuming the Final Close occurs on July 15, 2026, the Compilation would be delivered on or about August 5, 2026 (fifteen business days later), and the MFN election period would close on or about September 4, 2026. The GP will therefore not have full visibility into the extent of MFN fee elections --- and thus the Fund\'s actual management fee revenue for the first year of the investment period --- until nearly eight months after the targeted First Close and approximately two months after the Final Close. During this period, the GP should budget conservatively, assuming a worst-case fee scenario consistent with Scenario 1 in Section IV.B below.

Additionally, we note that the LPA does not specify a deadline by which the GP must acknowledge or implement MFN elections. As a matter of best practice, we recommend that the GP confirm receipt of each MFN election notice within five (5) business days and implement elected provisions (including adjusted fee calculations) within thirty (30) days of the close of the MFN election period, with appropriate retroactive adjustments to fees charged from the date of such LP\'s admission to the Fund. The fee administrator, Meridian Fund Services LLC, should be apprised of this timeline and should prepare to process retroactive fee adjustments as necessary.

**[IV. Scenario Analysis --- Economic Impact of MFN Fee Elections]{.underline}**

**[A. Modeling Assumptions]{.underline}**

The following assumptions apply across all three scenarios modeled in this Section IV:

> • **Target fund size:** \$600,000,000.
>
> • **Anchor LP commitments:** \$165,000,000 (as set forth in Section II.A).
>
> • **Subsequent LP commitments needed to reach target:** \$435,000,000 (\$600,000,000 minus \$165,000,000).
>
> • **Standard management fee:** 2.00% per annum on committed capital during the investment period (January 15, 2026 through January 15, 2031).
>
> • **Fund size assumption:** All modeling assumes the Fund reaches its \$600,000,000 target. Sensitivity to different raise amounts is addressed in Section IV.F.
>
> • **Post-investment-period fee:** The management fee during the post-investment period reverts to 2.00% per annum calculated on invested capital (rather than committed capital) for all limited partners. The anchor side letters do not differentiate the post-investment-period fee, and all anchor LPs revert to the standard post-investment-period fee structure set forth in the LPA. Accordingly, post-investment-period fees are not modeled in this analysis.
>
> • **Brindoval fee netting provision:** For purposes of this analysis, the Brindoval fee netting provision (which nets management fees paid by Brindoval against carried interest distributions otherwise allocable to the GP with respect to Brindoval\'s limited partnership interest) is excluded from fee-rate modeling. The netting provision affects the timing and offset of fee payments against carry distributions, but does not alter the stated management fee rate applicable to Brindoval\'s commitment. It therefore does not change the management fee rate that appears in the MFN Side Letter Compilation or the rate available for MFN election. However, if a subsequent LP elects Brindoval\'s netting provision through the MFN process, the netting would apply to that LP\'s fees and carry as well, creating additional economic complexity that is beyond the scope of this analysis.
>
> • **MFN eligibility:** Each scenario assumes that all subsequent LP commitments exceed the \$25,000,000 MFN Threshold, such that all subsequent LP capital is MFN-eligible. As discussed in Section III.A, this assumption is reasonable given the Fund\'s institutional investor base and anticipated commitment sizes.

**[B. Scenario 1 --- Aggressive Election: 50% of Subsequent LPs Elect CPERS Rate (1.75%)]{.underline}**

Scenario 1 models the most severe plausible fee erosion from MFN elections. Under this scenario, 50% of subsequent LP capital elects into the 1.75% management fee rate granted to CPERS, while the remaining 50% of subsequent LP capital remains at the standard 2.00% rate.
--
> • Five-year investment period cumulative reduction vs. standard baseline: \$806,250 × 5 = **\$4,031,250**
>
> • Five-year investment period incremental cumulative reduction beyond anchor discounts: \$543,750 × 5 = **\$2,718,750**

This scenario represents the upper bound of plausible fee erosion. It assumes a high rate of MFN election (50% of subsequent LP capital) and that all electing LPs choose the deepest available discount (the 1.75% CPERS rate). While a 50% election rate may seem aggressive, it is not unprecedented in the current fundraising environment, particularly for venture funds with strong track records that attract sophisticated institutional investors with experienced fund formation counsel. The fact that all three anchor LPs are represented by well-known fund formation practices --- Whitfield & Gage, Hollander McKee & Stone, and Prescott & Langley --- suggests that subsequent LPs and their counsel will be similarly attentive to MFN opportunities.

A key factor in whether Scenario 1 materializes is whether the 1.75% CPERS rate can be characterized as an Excluded Provision (see Section V.A.1 below). If the CPERS fee reduction is successfully excluded from MFN election, the deepest available rate becomes the 1.85% Northstar rate, and Scenario 1 (in its current form) becomes impossible.

**PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT** This memorandum is protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. It is intended solely for the use of the attorneys and personnel of Calderwood & Harkness LLP and should not be disclosed to any third party without the prior written consent of the undersigned.

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** **FUNDS & ASSET MANAGEMENT GROUP** **INTERNAL STRATEGY MEMORANDUM**

October 6, 2025

**TO:** Nicholas Stern, Responsible Partner, Funds & Asset Management

**FROM:** Owen Fischer, Lead Associate, Funds & Asset Management

**RE:** Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP --- Side Letter Negotiation Strategy and Most Favored Nation Election Framework

**CC:** Graham Sutherland (Billing Partner); Stephen Adler (Working Associate)

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**[I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY]{.underline}**

The purpose of this memorandum is to analyze the structuring of the most favored nation (\"MFN\") election framework and to develop a comprehensive, LP-by-LP negotiation strategy for the three anchor investor side letters in connection with Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership managed by its general partner, Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC (the \"GP\"). This memorandum is prepared to inform internal strategy discussions and to guide the drafting and negotiation of the side letter agreements anticipated to be delivered to counterparty counsel on or about October 20, 2025.

The Fund is targeting an aggregate capital raise of \$600,000,000 (with a hard cap of \$750,000,000) and will focus on early-stage and growth-stage venture capital investments in the enterprise software and software-as-a-service (\"SaaS\") sectors. The GP\'s principals, Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois, have established a strong track record through Pinnacle Venture Fund I LP (2021 vintage, \$350 million), which has generated a net internal rate of return (\"IRR\") of 24.3% and a net total value to paid-in multiple (\"TVPI\") of 1.58x as of June 30, 2025. The successor fund is well-positioned in the market, and the GP has attracted significant interest from institutional limited partners seeking exposure to the enterprise software sector.

Three anchor limited partners have made preliminary commitments representing aggregate capital commitments of \$165,000,000, or approximately 27.5% of the target fund size:

> • **Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System (\"CPERS\"):** \$75,000,000 commitment (12.5% of target);
>
> • **Northstar Endowment Partners LLC (\"NEP\"):** \$50,000,000 commitment (8.33% of target); and
>
> • **Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP (\"Brindoval\"):** \$40,000,000 commitment (6.67% of target).

Each of these anchor investors will execute a separate side letter agreement that supplements the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (the \"LPA\"), which is expected to be dated as of the First Close on January 15, 2026. The side letters will grant various economic, governance, informational, and operational accommodations tailored to the legal status, investment policy requirements, and negotiating priorities of each anchor LP.

The key timeline milestones are as follows: initial drafts of the three anchor side letters are targeted for distribution to counterparty counsel by October 20, 2025; the negotiation period is expected to extend through December 20, 2025 (with two to three rounds of mark-ups anticipated per side letter); the First Close is targeted for January 15, 2026; and the Final Close deadline is July 15, 2026. The MFN Side Letter Compilation will be delivered to all MFN-eligible limited partners within fifteen (15) business days following the Final Close.

Our central recommendation is to structure the MFN framework with robust \"Excluded Provisions\" carve-outs designed to limit the GP\'s economic and operational exposure from subsequent LP elections, while providing sufficient MFN coverage to satisfy the institutional expectations of sophisticated anchor investors. Specifically, we recommend defining five categories of Excluded Provisions (governmental plan regulatory requirements, ERISA representations, advisory committee seats, portfolio company board observer rights, and a catch-all for LP-specific legal/regulatory/tax provisions) while permitting MFN elections for economic terms (management fee reductions, co-investment terms, fee netting) and information/notification rights.

This memorandum addresses the following topics in detail: (a) the structural design of the MFN framework, including eligibility thresholds, election procedures, and operative mechanics; (b) the categorization and rationale for Excluded Provisions; (c) LP-specific negotiation considerations, including anticipated positions of counterparty counsel; and (d) recommended provision-by-provision treatment, presented both in narrative analysis and in a summary classification table.

**[II. BACKGROUND --- FUND OVERVIEW AND ECONOMICS]{.underline}**

**[A. Fund Structure and Terms]{.underline}**

The Fund is organized as Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, a Delaware limited partnership. The Certificate of Limited Partnership was filed with the Delaware Secretary of State on August 12, 2025 (File No. 7924813). The Fund\'s general partner is Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company controlled by its Co-Founders and Managing Partners, Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois. The GP is a registered investment adviser with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended (SEC File No. 801-XXXXX --- to be confirmed with the GP prior to finalizing the side letter drafts).

The Fund will rely on the exemption from registration under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended, pursuant to either Section 3(c)(1) (limiting the Fund to no more than 100 beneficial owners) or Section 3(c)(7) (limiting the Fund to \"qualified purchasers\" as defined in Section 2(a)(51) of the Investment Company Act). The determination of which exemption will be relied upon will depend on the composition and number of investors admitted through the Final Close. Given the target fund size and the anticipated investor base, we expect the Fund to rely primarily on Section 3(c)(7).

The Fund\'s registered agent in Delaware is Capitol Registered Agents Inc., located at 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801. The Fund\'s principal office and headquarters are located at 2400 Sand Hill Road, Suite 320, Menlo Park, California 94025.

The Fund\'s investment strategy is focused on early-stage and growth-stage venture capital investments in the enterprise software and SaaS sectors. This represents a continuation and expansion of the investment strategy successfully employed in the predecessor fund. Pinnacle Venture Fund I LP (the \"Predecessor Fund\") is a 2021-vintage fund with total commitments of \$350,000,000. As of June 30, 2025, the Predecessor Fund has generated a net IRR of 24.3% and a net TVPI of 1.58x, positioning it in the upper quartile for venture capital funds of its vintage. The strong performance of the Predecessor Fund is a significant driver of LP interest in the current fundraise and provides meaningful leverage in side letter negotiations.

**[B. Fund Economics]{.underline}**

The principal economic terms of the Fund, as set forth in the LPA, are summarized below:

**Target Fund Size and Hard Cap.** The Fund\'s target aggregate capital commitments are \$600,000,000. The LPA provides for a hard cap of \$750,000,000, above which no additional commitments may be accepted without the consent of a majority-in-interest of the existing limited partners. The \$150,000,000 buffer between the target and the hard cap provides meaningful flexibility for the GP to accommodate additional investor interest, particularly from institutional investors who may increase their commitments following the First Close.

**Management Fee.** The management fee is 2.0% per annum on committed capital during the five-year investment period (January 15, 2026 through January 15, 2031). Following the expiration of the investment period, the management fee transitions to 2.0% per annum calculated on invested capital (i.the legal, regulatory, or tax status of the LP to whom it was originally granted and would be inapplicable or meaningless if adopted by the electing LP. For example, a provision granting a fee reduction that is expressly conditioned on the LP\'s status as a tax-exempt organization may not be applicable to a taxable LP. The GP\'s determination of applicability must be made in good faith and on a reasonable basis. We anticipate that this discretion will be a point of negotiation with counterparty counsel, and we should be prepared to provide examples of circumstances in which the GP\'s discretion would appropriately be exercised.

**Preservation of LP confidentiality.** There is no requirement for the GP to notify the limited partner whose term was elected into by another LP. The confidentiality of each LP\'s identity and the specific terms of its side letter are preserved throughout the MFN process. The MFN Side Letter Compilation itself is delivered on a confidential basis and is subject to the confidentiality provisions of the LPA.

**Prospective effect.** MFN elections do not create retroactive economic adjustments. Elected provisions apply prospectively from the effective date of the election (i.e., the date of the GP\'s receipt of the MFN Election Form). For management fee provisions, this means that an elected fee reduction will apply to management fee calculations for periods following the election date, and the GP will not be required to refund or credit management fees previously collected at the standard rate.

**[IV. EXCLUDED PROVISIONS --- CATEGORIES AND RATIONALE]{.underline}**

**[A. Overview]{.underline}**

\"Excluded Provisions\" are categories of side letter terms that are carved out from the MFN election process. No limited partner may elect into an Excluded Provision through the MFN framework, regardless of the LP\'s commitment size or MFN eligibility. Excluded Provisions are omitted entirely from the MFN Side Letter Compilation and are not disclosed to MFN-eligible LPs.

The definition of Excluded Provisions is one of the most critical structural decisions in the MFN framework. If the category is defined too narrowly, the GP faces significant economic and operational exposure as subsequent LPs elect into the most favorable terms granted to any investor. If the category is defined too broadly, institutional LPs (and their counsel) will resist the MFN clause as illusory --- providing the form of MFN protection without substantive content. The appropriate balance depends on the specific terms being negotiated, the characteristics of the LP base, and market practice for comparable venture capital funds.

We recommend defining five categories of Excluded Provisions, each of which is supported by a clear policy rationale and is consistent with market practice for institutional venture capital funds. These categories are discussed in detail below.

**[B. Category 1: Provisions Required by Specific Legal or Regulatory Requirements of a Governmental Plan LP]{.underline}**

The first category of Excluded Provisions covers any provision that is included in a side letter to satisfy the specific legal or regulatory requirements of a limited partner that is a governmental pension plan, governmental retirement system, or sovereign entity. This category is designed to capture provisions that are legally mandated for governmental investors and that have no economic value, relevance, or applicability to non-governmental limited partners.

The primary beneficiary of this exclusion is Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System, which is a Washington State governmental pension plan that is tax-exempt under Internal Revenue Code Section 115. As a governmental entity, CPERS is subject to Washington State public records laws (the Washington Public Records Act, RCW 42.56), sunshine law requirements, and state-law mandated investment restrictions that do not apply to private institutional investors, endowments, or family offices. The side letter provisions granted to CPERS to address these requirements --- including FOIA/public records protections, notice and consultation rights before disclosure of Fund information in response to public records requests, and redaction procedures for proprietary Fund information --- are driven entirely by CPERS\'s governmental status and are not economic accommodations subject to competitive equalization through MFN elections.

The rationale for this exclusion is straightforward: non-governmental LPs (including NEP and Brindoval) have no exposure to public records laws and no basis to elect into protections that address governmental disclosure obligations. Including these provisions in the MFN Side Letter Compilation would serve no purpose and would add unnecessary length and complexity to the compilation document. We expect no significant pushback from counterparty counsel on this category.

**[C. Category 2: ERISA Representations and Waivers]{.underline}**

The second category of Excluded Provisions covers representations that a limited partner is not subject to the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), or waivers of ERISA-related representations that may be included in the LPA.

The side letters described herein supplement and, to the extent of any conflict between the provisions of a side letter and the corresponding provisions of the partnership agreement, modify solely as between the General Partner and the applicable limited partner, the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, dated as of the First Close (the \"LPA\"). In all cases, the side letters are intended to be read in conjunction with the LPA, and any capitalized terms used in the side letters and not otherwise defined therein have the meanings assigned to them in the LPA.

Three anchor limited partners are party to individually negotiated side letters at the First Close:

> 1\. **Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System (\"CPERS\")** --- Capital commitment of \$75,000,000, representing approximately 12.5% of the Fund\'s \$600,000,000 target fund size. CPERS is a governmental pension plan organized under the laws of the State of Washington.
>
> 2\. **Northstar Endowment Partners LLC (\"Northstar\" or \"NEP\")** --- Capital commitment of \$50,000,000, representing approximately 8.33% of the Fund\'s \$600,000,000 target fund size. > 3\. **Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP (\"Brindoval\")** --- Capital commitment of \$40,000,000, representing approximately 6.67% of the Fund\'s \$600,000,000 target fund size. > Attention: Rajesh Mehta, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
>
> Claire Dubois, Co-Founder & Managing Partner

**Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- Side Letter Agreements and Most Favored Nation Election Framework for Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP**

Dear Mr. Mehta and Ms. Dubois:

**[1. Purpose and Confirmation of Engagement]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the \"GP\"), in its capacity as the general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Fund\"), in connection with the negotiation, preparation, and documentation of side letter agreements with certain anchor limited partners of the Fund and the structuring and documentation of the most favored nation (\"MFN\") election framework applicable to qualifying limited partners of the Fund, each as more fully described in Section 2 below.

The Fund was organized pursuant to a Certificate of Limited Partnership filed with the Office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on August 12, 2025, under File No. 7924813. The rights, obligations, and governance terms of the Fund and its limited partners will be set forth in the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of the Fund, to be dated as of the date of the Fund\'s initial closing (the \"First Close\") (as may be further amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"LPA\"). The side letters to be prepared in connection with this engagement will supplement and, solely as between the GP and the applicable limited partner, modify certain terms of the LPA in the manner described herein.

This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions of our engagement, including the scope of the Firm\'s representation, the engagement team, our fee arrangements, and other matters relevant to the attorney-client relationship between Calderwood & Harkness and the GP. We ask that you review this Engagement Letter carefully and confirm your agreement to its terms by countersigning a copy of this letter as provided in Section 13 below.

**[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

The scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement in connection with the Fund\'s side letter program and MFN election framework shall encompass the following:

**(a) Anchor Limited Partner Side Letter Agreements**

Calderwood & Harkness will draft, negotiate, and finalize individual side letter agreements (each, a \"Side Letter\") with the following three anchor limited partners of the Fund (collectively, the \"Anchor LPs\"):

> \(i\) **Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System** (\"Cascadia PERS\"), a governmental pension plan organized under the laws of the State of Washington. Cascadia PERS has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000), representing approximately 12.5% of the Fund\'s target fund size of Six Hundred Million Dollars (\$600,000,000) (the \"Target Fund Size\").
>
> \(ii\) **Northstar Endowment Partners LLC** (\"Northstar\"), a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of Delaware, serving as the dedicated investment vehicle for the endowment of Veltrano University. Northstar has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000), representing approximately 8.33% of the Target Fund Size.
>
> \(iii\) **Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP** (\"Brindoval\"), a limited partnership organized under the laws of the State of Delaware. Brindoval has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Forty Million Dollars (\$40,000,000), representing approximately 6.67% of the Target Fund Size.

The aggregate capital commitments of the Anchor LPs total One Hundred Sixty-Five Million Dollars (\$165,000,000), representing approximately 27.5% of the Target Fund Size. Given the significance of these commitments to the Fund\'s initial closing and overall capital formation, the Firm understands that the timely completion of Side Letter negotiations with each of the Anchor LPs is a priority for the GP.

**(b) Side Letter Terms and Provisions**

Each Side Letter will be structured to supplement and, solely as between the GP and the applicable Anchor LP, modify certain terms and conditions of the LPA. The specific provisions to be addressed in each Side Letter will vary based on the nature, regulatory status, and specific requirements of the applicable Anchor LP, but are expected to include, as applicable, the following categories of terms:

> \(i\) **Management fee concessions**, including reduced management fee rates, management fee offsets, and fee calculation methodologies applicable during the investment period and the post-investment period;
>
> \(ii\) **Co-investment rights**, including rights to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund, allocation priority, notification procedures, and minimum co-investment allocation amounts;
>
> \(iii\) **Excuse and opt-out rights**, including the right of certain limited partners to be excused from, or to opt out of, specific Fund investments on the basis of legal, regulatory, tax, or policy considerations applicable to such limited partner;
>
> \(iv\) **Reporting enhancements**, including supplemental reporting obligations of the GP, enhanced transparency regarding portfolio company performance, ESG-related reporting, and diversity and inclusion metrics;
>
> \(v\) **FOIA and public records protections**, particularly relevant to Cascadia PERS, including provisions addressing the treatment of Fund information in the event of a public records request, prior notice and consultation obligations of the limited partner, and the GP\'s right to seek protective relief;
>
> \(vi\) **Advisory committee seats**, including the right of certain Anchor LPs to designate a representative to serve on the Fund\'s advisory committee, as well as related governance provisions;
>
> \(vii\) **Key-person event notifications**, including enhanced notification rights in the event of a key-person event under the LPA, consultation rights, and accelerated information delivery timelines;
>
> \(viii\) **Transfer rights**, including any enhanced or modified transfer, assignment, or secondary sale rights negotiated with an Anchor LP, subject to the transfer restrictions and consent provisions of the LPA;
>
> \(ix\) **Fee netting provisions**, addressing the application and allocation of transaction fees, monitoring fees, break-up fees, and other fees received by the GP or its affiliates in connection with Fund investments;
>
> \(x\) **Information rights**, including the right to receive additional information from the GP regarding the Fund\'s investments, operations, or financial condition, beyond the standard reporting obligations set forth in the LPA; and
>
> \(xi\) **Other customary terms**, including provisions relating to indemnification, representations and warranties, sovereign immunity (if applicable), governing law modifications, and such other terms as may be customary for side letters in institutional venture capital fund formations.

The Firm will work closely with the GP to tailor each Side Letter to the specific requirements and negotiation objectives of each Anchor LP, while maintaining consistency across the side letter package and managing the GP\'s exposure under the MFN framework.

**(c) Most Favored Nation Election Framework**

Calderwood & Harkness will structure and document a comprehensive most favored nation election framework (the \"MFN Framework\") applicable to qualifying limited partners of the Fund. The MFN Framework will include the following components:

> \(i\) **MFN Eligibility Threshold.** The Firm will advise on and document the MFN eligibility threshold, which the GP has preliminarily determined shall be set at capital commitments of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) or greater. Limited partners whose capital commitments equal or exceed this threshold (each, an \"Eligible LP\") will be entitled to elect certain rights and benefits granted in Side Letters to other limited partners of the Fund, subject to the exclusions described below.
>
> \(ii\) **MFN Election Procedures Letter and Election Form.** The Firm will draft a template MFN election procedures letter (the \"MFN Procedures Letter\") to be delivered by the GP to each Eligible LP, together with a standardized MFN election form (the \"MFN Election Form\") to be completed and returned by any Eligible LP wishing to make an MFN election. The MFN Procedures Letter will set forth the procedures, timing, and conditions applicable to MFN elections, including the process for the GP\'s review and confirmation of elected provisions.
>
> \(iii\) **Excluded Provisions.** The Firm will define and categorize certain provisions that will not be available for election under the MFN Framework (collectively, \"Excluded Provisions\"). Excluded Provisions are expected to include, without limitation: (A) provisions granted to a limited partner in order to satisfy specific legal, regulatory, or tax requirements applicable to such limited partner by reason of its status, jurisdiction, or governing law; (B) advisory committee seats and related governance rights; (C) portfolio company board observer rights; and (D) any other terms that the GP reasonably determines are specific to the legal, regulatory, or organizational status of a particular limited partner and are not appropriate for general election by other limited partners.
>
> \(iv\) **Redacted MFN Side Letter Compilation.** The Firm will prepare a redacted compilation of the Side Letters entered into by the Fund (the \"MFN Side Letter Compilation\"), from which the identities of the limited partners party thereto and all Excluded Provisions shall be redacted. The MFN Side Letter Compilation will be delivered by the GP to each Eligible LP within fifteen (15) business days following the final closing of the Fund (the \"Final Close\"), which is currently targeted to occur on or before July 15, 2026.
>
> \(v\) **MFN Election Period.** Following delivery of the MFN Side Letter Compilation, each Eligible LP shall have a period of thirty (30) calendar days (the \"MFN Election Period\") in which to review the MFN Side Letter Compilation and submit a completed MFN Election Form to the GP indicating which provisions, if any, such Eligible LP elects to receive. The Firm will advise the GP on the review, confirmation, and administration of MFN elections following the close of the MFN Election Period.

**(d) Coordination with Counterparty Counsel**
--
> \(ii\) **Hollander McKee & Stone LLP** (Boston, Massachusetts), with David Tannenbaum as lead partner, serving as counsel to Northstar Endowment Partners LLC; and
>
> \(iii\) **Prescott & Langley LLP** (Chicago, Illinois), with Angela Ferris as lead partner, serving as counsel to Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP.

The Firm will coordinate the distribution of initial Side Letter drafts to each counterparty counsel, manage the negotiation process, track open issues, and seek to resolve negotiation points in a manner consistent with the GP\'s objectives and the Fund\'s overall commercial terms. The Firm will also facilitate, as appropriate, the scheduling and conduct of negotiation calls between the parties and their respective counsel.

**(e) Internal Analyses and Negotiation Support**

In support of the Side Letter negotiations and the MFN Framework, Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the following internal analyses and work product for the GP\'s use:
--
These materials will be prepared for the GP\'s internal use and will be subject to the attorney-client privilege and work product protections, as applicable.

**(f) Closing Checklist --- First Close Deliverables**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a closing checklist identifying all deliverables and conditions related to Side Letter execution that must be completed in connection with the First Close, including the execution and delivery of each Anchor LP Side Letter, the GP\'s execution of any related certificates, confirmations, or ancillary documents, and the distribution of any required notices or disclosures to the Anchor LPs or other limited partners of the Fund.

**[3. Matters Outside the Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

The GP and the Firm acknowledge and agree that the following matters are expressly outside the scope of this engagement and are not included in the services to be provided by Calderwood & Harkness hereunder:

> \(a\) The drafting, negotiation, or review of the LPA itself, or any amendments or restatements thereto;
>
> \(b\) The preparation, drafting, or review of the Fund\'s private placement memorandum, confidential offering memorandum, subscription agreements, investor questionnaires, or other offering or subscription documents;
>
> \(c\) Any filings with, or submissions to, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") or any state securities regulator, including Form D filings, Form ADV amendments, or blue sky filings;
>
> \(d\) Tax structuring, tax planning, or the rendering of any tax opinion or tax advice in connection with the Fund, the GP, or any limited partner, including any analysis under Subchapter K of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, or any state or local tax regime;
>
> \(e\) Analysis of compliance with the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), or the plan asset regulations thereunder, except to the extent of any ERISA-related representations, warranties, or acknowledgments that may be included in the Side Letters as a matter of standard drafting practice;
>
> \(f\) Any representation of, or advice to, the GP or the Fund in connection with the Fund\'s placement agent arrangements with Greystone Capital Advisors LLC, including the negotiation, review, or interpretation of any placement agent agreement; and
>
> \(g\) Any litigation, arbitration, mediation, or other dispute resolution proceeding, whether arising out of or related to the Side Letters, the LPA, the Fund, or otherwise.

In the event that the GP wishes to expand the scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s representation to include any of the foregoing matters or any other matter not described in Section 2 above, such expansion of scope shall be confirmed in a separate engagement letter or in a written amendment to this Engagement Letter, setting forth the additional scope, engagement team, fee arrangements, and other applicable terms.

**[4. Engagement Team]{.underline}**
--

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Team Member**     **Role**              **Practice Group**         **Primary Responsibilities**
  ------------------- --------------------- -------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Nicholas Stern      Responsible Partner   Funds & Asset Management   Primary point of contact for strategic matters and client relationship management; overall supervision of the engagement; participation in key negotiation sessions with counterparty counsel

  Graham Sutherland   Billing Partner       Funds & Asset Management   Billing administration and fee monitoring; periodic review of engagement progress and work product

  Owen Fischer        Lead Associate        Funds & Asset Management   Day-to-day management of the engagement; principal drafter of all Side Letters, MFN Framework documents, and internal analyses; primary liaison with counterparty counsel; coordination of negotiation schedules and issue resolution

  Stephen Adler       Working Associate     Funds & Asset Management   Supporting drafting and research; preparation of the MFN exposure analysis, redline comparison charts, and negotiation issues tracker; assistance with closing checklist preparation
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The GP\'s primary day-to-day contact for the engagement will be Owen Fischer. For strategic and client relationship matters, the GP may contact Nicholas Stern directly. The Firm may, from time to time, assign additional attorneys or professional staff to the engagement as circumstances warrant, and will inform the GP of any material changes to the composition of the engagement team.

--

  Stephen Adler           Associate               \$750
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The foregoing billing rates are the Firm\'s standard rates in effect as of January 1, 2025. Billing rates are subject to annual adjustment, which typically takes effect on January 1 of each calendar year. The Firm will notify the GP in advance of any changes to the billing rates applicable to this engagement. In the event that senior associates are assigned to the engagement in a supporting capacity, the applicable senior associate rate set forth above will apply.

**(b) Fee Estimate**

Based on the scope of services described in Section 2 above, and on the Firm\'s experience with comparable side letter programs for venture capital and private equity fund formations, Calderwood & Harkness estimates that total professional fees for the engagement will be in the range of **\$185,000 to \$225,000**. This estimate is based on an anticipated total of approximately **170 to 210 hours** of attorney time across the engagement team, and assumes a negotiation process involving a customary number of drafting rounds and negotiation sessions with each of the three Anchor LPs.

The foregoing estimate is provided solely for the GP\'s budgeting and planning purposes and **does not constitute a cap on fees or a fixed fee arrangement**. Actual fees may be higher or lower than the estimate depending on a number of factors, including the complexity and duration of negotiations with each Anchor LP, the number and scope of negotiation rounds, the extent of LP-specific requirements or unusual provisions, and the responsiveness of counterparty counsel. The Firm will provide the GP with monthly updates on accrued fees relative to the estimate and will promptly notify the GP if the Firm believes that fees are likely to materially exceed the estimated range.

**(c) Disbursements and Expenses**
--

  MFN Election Period                                               30 calendar days following delivery of the MFN Side Letter Compilation
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Calderwood & Harkness will use commercially reasonable efforts to meet the foregoing timeline and milestones; however, the Firm notes that the actual schedule will depend on a number of factors outside the Firm\'s control, including the responsiveness of counterparty counsel and the Anchor LPs, the complexity and scope of LP-specific negotiation requests, and any changes to the GP\'s fundraising timeline or closing schedule. The Firm will keep the GP regularly informed of progress against the timeline and will promptly communicate any anticipated delays or scheduling issues.

**[7. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by the GP and the Fund in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s professional obligations under the California Rules of Professional Conduct and applicable law. The Firm will not disclose confidential information to any third party except as authorized by the GP, as required by law or court order, or as necessary to carry out the Firm\'s responsibilities under this engagement (including, for the avoidance of doubt, communications with counterparty counsel in the course of Side Letter negotiations, as directed by the GP).

The Firm acknowledges the particularly sensitive nature of LP-specific terms and the MFN Framework structure, and will implement appropriate internal controls to safeguard such information, including limiting access to engagement files and work product to members of the engagement team and such other Firm personnel as are reasonably necessary to support the engagement.

**[8. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**
--
In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of this engagement, Calderwood & Harkness will promptly notify the GP and discuss appropriate steps to address the conflict, which may include, depending on the nature and severity of the conflict, obtaining an informed written waiver from the affected parties, implementing an ethical screen within the Firm, or, if necessary, withdrawing from the engagement in whole or in part. The Firm will endeavor to minimize any disruption to the engagement in the event a conflict issue arises.

**[9. Client Identity and Authority]{.underline}**

The client in this engagement is **Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC**, in its capacity as the general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP. For the avoidance of doubt, Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and this Engagement Letter does not create an attorney-client relationship with:

> \(a\) any individual limited partner of the Fund, including any of the Anchor LPs;
>
> \(b\) the Fund itself as a separate legal entity, except to the extent that the interests of the Fund are aligned with, and directed by, the GP in the GP\'s capacity as the general partner and manager of the Fund; or
>
> \(c\) any individual managing partner, officer, member, or employee of the GP in his or her personal capacity, including Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois.

All instructions, authorizations, and direction regarding this engagement shall be received by the Firm from Rajesh Mehta and/or Claire Dubois, acting on behalf of the GP. The Firm shall be entitled to rely upon any instruction or authorization communicated by either Mr. Mehta or Ms. Dubois as being duly authorized by the GP, absent written notice to the contrary.
--
Upon the conclusion of the engagement, or at any time thereafter upon written request from the GP, the Firm will return any original documents provided by the GP to the Firm in connection with the engagement. Copies of engagement files and work product may be retained by the Firm in accordance with its retention policies and applicable professional obligations.

**[11. Governing Law]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter and the terms of the engagement described herein shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to the conflicts of law principles thereof. The selection of Delaware law as the governing law for this Engagement Letter is consistent with the governing law provisions of the Side Letters, the LPA, and the Fund\'s organizational documents, and is intended to provide uniformity across the documentation of the Fund\'s formation and investor arrangements.

**[12. Termination]{.underline}**

Either the GP or Calderwood & Harkness may terminate this engagement at any time upon written notice to the other party. Termination of the engagement shall not relieve the GP of its obligation to pay all professional fees and disbursements incurred by the Firm through the effective date of termination, including any amounts reflected on invoices rendered prior to or after the date of termination for services performed through such date.
--
Upon any termination of the engagement, Calderwood & Harkness will take such steps as are reasonably necessary to protect the GP\'s interests during the transition period, including cooperating with successor counsel, delivering work product and files to the GP or its designee, and providing reasonable assistance in connection with the orderly transition of the matter. The Firm\'s obligations under Sections 7 (Confidentiality) and 10 (Document Retention) shall survive termination of the engagement.

**[13. Acceptance and Counterparts]{.underline}**

We respectfully request that the GP confirm its agreement to the terms and conditions of this Engagement Letter by having an authorized representative of the GP countersign a copy of this letter in the space provided below and return the executed copy to Calderwood & Harkness at the address set forth above, or by electronic transmission to Nicholas Stern at nstern@calderwoodharkness.com.

This Engagement Letter may be executed in one or more counterparts, including by means of electronic signature (including Brightwater Software or similar platforms), each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which, taken together, shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of this Engagement Letter by electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf) or by other electronic transmission shall be effective as delivery of an original executed counterpart.

We look forward to working with you and the entire Pinnacle team on this important engagement. We are confident that Calderwood & Harkness\'s experience in fund formation and institutional side letter programs will be of significant value to the GP and the Fund as you advance toward your First Close and beyond. Please do not hesitate to contact Nicholas Stern or Owen Fischer with any questions regarding this Engagement Letter or the scope of our representation.

Very truly yours,

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**

101:**Description:** Execution copy of the Side Letter (the \"CPERS Side Letter\") between Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, in its capacity as general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, and Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System, dated as of the First Close (January 15, 2026). The CPERS Side Letter sets forth certain rights, obligations, and modifications to the LPA that are applicable solely as between the General Partner and CPERS.
102-
103-**Key Provisions Covered:**
104-
105-> \(a\) **Management Fee Reduction.** Reduction of the management fee payable by CPERS to 1.75% per annum on committed capital during the Investment Period (representing a 25 basis point discount from the standard 2.00% management fee set forth in Section 6.1 of the LPA). Following the expiration of the Investment Period, CPERS will pay the management fee at the standard rate of 2.00% per annum on invested capital, consistent with the LPA.
106->
107-> \(b\) **Excuse Rights.** Right of CPERS to be excused from participating in any Fund investment in a portfolio company that derives more than 15% of its revenues from the manufacture, distribution, or sale of tobacco products or firearms and related accessories, in each case as determined in good faith by the General Partner. The General Partner shall provide CPERS with reasonable prior written notice of any proposed investment that it believes may trigger this excuse right and shall afford CPERS a period of not less than ten (10) business days to exercise such right.
--
111-> \(d\) **FOIA / Public Records Protection Carve-Outs.** Acknowledgment by the General Partner that CPERS is a governmental plan subject to the Washington Public Records Act (RCW 42.56) and related public disclosure requirements. Provisions establishing (i) the General Partner\'s obligation to label confidential or proprietary information as such, (ii) CPERS\'s obligation to notify the General Partner promptly (and in any event within five (5) business days) of any public records request that could require disclosure of Fund-related information, and (iii) the General Partner\'s right to seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy prior to any such disclosure.
112->
113-> \(e\) **Co-Investment Rights.** Right to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund, with no management fee or carried interest charged on co-invested capital. Co-investment allocations shall be offered to CPERS on a pro rata basis relative to its commitment to the Fund, subject to the General Partner\'s discretion regarding allocation among all co-investment-eligible limited partners.
114->
115-> \(f\) **Most Favored Nation Election Right.** Right to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner in the Fund (subject to certain Excluded Provisions as described in Section IX of this Checklist), in accordance with the MFN election procedures established in the side letters and the procedures letter to be delivered following the Final Close.
116->
117:> \(g\) **Tax-Exempt Status Representations.** Representations by CPERS regarding its status as a tax-exempt entity under Section 115 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.
