=== documents/matters/1001-00002/Engagement & Administration/engagement-letter.docx ===

**[1. Purpose and Engagement]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter confirms that Calderwood & Harkness has been engaged by the ManCo to serve as legal counsel in connection with a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$2.8 billion in total commitments. The ManCo is a Delaware limited liability company and a registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") under CRD #298417. The Fund\'s sole general partner is Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company.

The engagement encompasses the formation of new holding entities, the negotiation of separation arrangements with departing principals, the realignment of carried interest and management fee economics among continuing and next-generation principals, the solicitation of necessary limited partner consents, compliance with existing side-letter obligations, and related tax structuring. The scope of the representation, the personnel assigned to the engagement, the fee arrangement, and other terms and conditions governing this engagement are set forth in the sections that follow.

--

\(e\) Preparing and filing Certificates of Formation with the Delaware Secretary of State for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, together with any ancillary filings or registrations required in connection with the formation and qualification of such entities.

\(f\) Preparing Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund (the \"LPA\") to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner, including any required modifications to the definitions, representations, and governance provisions of the LPA necessitated by the interposition of GP Intermediate and HoldCo above the General Partner.

**2.2 Economics Realignment**

--

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on all limited partner notification, consent, and compliance matters arising from the restructuring, including:

\(a\) Preparing materials for notification to, and solicitation of consent from, the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, including a detailed memorandum describing the restructuring and its implications for the Fund and its limited partners.

\(b\) Analyzing compliance with the Fund\'s fourteen (14) existing side letters, with particular attention to key-person provisions under Section 5.2 of the LPA and any expanded or supplemental key-person provisions contained in certain side letters, to determine whether the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask or the structural changes contemplated by the restructuring trigger key-person events, consent requirements, or notification obligations under any such side letter.

\(c\) Preparing LP notification letters to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund, describing the restructuring, the changes to the General Partner structure, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, and any other information required to be disclosed under the LPA or the applicable side letters.

\(d\) Advising on the preparation and filing of an amended SEC Form ADV (Parts 1 and 2) to reflect the restructuring, and advising on any other regulatory filings or notifications required in connection with the restructuring, including any applicable state regulatory filings.

--

**[10. Acceptance and Counterparts]{.underline}**

We respectfully request that the Client confirm its acceptance of the terms and conditions of this engagement by having each of the undersigned representatives execute and return the enclosed copy of this Engagement Letter to Calderwood & Harkness at the address set forth above, or by transmitting an executed copy by electronic mail to Nicholas Stern at nstern@calderwoodharkness.com or Graham Sutherland at gsutherland@calderwoodharkness.com.

This Engagement Letter may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart by electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf) or by other electronic transmission shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart.

=== documents/matters/1001-00002/Engagement & Administration/matter-closing-memo.docx ===

**Date:** March 15, 2024

**Re:** Matter Closing Memorandum --- Ardent Capital Partners III LP --- Management Company Restructuring & Economics Realignment

**Status:** CLOSED --- COMPLETED

This memorandum is protected by the attorney-client privilege and constitutes attorney work product. It has been prepared solely for internal firm purposes in connection with the closing of the above-referenced matter. It should not be disclosed to any person or entity outside of Calderwood & Harkness LLP without the prior written approval of the Responsible Partner. Any inadvertent disclosure does not constitute a waiver of any applicable privilege or protection.

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**[1. Executive Summary]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") was engaged on October 9, 2023 by Ardent Capital Management LLC (\"ManCo\" or the \"Client\") to advise on a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$2.8 billion in aggregate capital commitments from forty-seven (47) limited partners. The engagement arose in the context of the planned retirement of one senior partner (David Kellner) and the voluntary departure of another partner (Joanna Trask), necessitating a thorough reorganization of the ownership, governance, and economic arrangements among the continuing and next-generation principals of the Ardent Capital platform.

The engagement encompassed four principal workstreams, which were subsequently expanded to six coordinated workstreams over the course of the representation:

--
>
> \(3\) **Departing Principal Separations** --- Negotiation and execution of separation and release agreements, carry retention and clawback side letters, and (in the case of David Kellner) a senior advisor agreement, with counterparty counsel Whitford & Chase LLP;
>
> \(4\) **LP Consent, Notification & Side-Letter Compliance** --- Solicitation and receipt of LPAC consent pursuant to LPA Section 9.4, preparation and distribution of LP notification letters to all 47 limited partners, and comprehensive review and analysis of all 14 side letters for compliance with restructuring-triggered obligations, including key-person analysis;
>
> \(5\) **Regulatory Filings** --- Preparation and filing of an amended SEC Form ADV for ManCo reflecting the new ownership structure, updated control persons, and revised organizational chart; and
>
> \(6\) **Coordination with Other Advisors** --- Delineation of responsibilities with Pemberton Hale LLP (ongoing fund formation and operations counsel), coordination with Heathrow Whitman & Co. (auditor and tax advisor) on tax reporting implications, and interaction with Broadleaf Consulting Group (valuation advisor) as needed for performance data.

All workstreams were completed and all restructuring documents were duly executed as of February 28, 2024. The new holding company entities --- Ardent Capital Holdings LLC and Ardent GP Intermediate LLC --- were formed with the Delaware Secretary of State on March 1, 2024. LP notification letters were sent to all 47 limited partners on March 5, 2024. The SEC Form ADV amendment for ManCo was filed on March 10, 2024. With all deliverables completed and all post-execution administrative steps finalized, the matter is hereby closed as of March 15, 2024.

The engagement team consisted of the following Calderwood & Harkness attorneys:

--

The Client in this engagement is **Ardent Capital Management LLC** (the \"ManCo\"), a Delaware limited liability company organized and existing under the Delaware Limited Liability Company Act (6 Del. C. § 18-101 *et seq.*). ManCo is registered as an investment adviser with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended, and maintains CRD No. 298417. ManCo\'s Employer Identification Number is 84-3291070.

ManCo\'s principal office is located at 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor, New York, New York 10022. ManCo serves as the investment adviser and manager of Ardent Capital Partners III LP, providing investment management, portfolio monitoring, and related advisory services to the Fund in accordance with the terms of the Fund\'s governing documents and ManCo\'s advisory agreement with the Fund.

Prior to the restructuring, ManCo was owned directly by five individual members (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao). Following the restructuring, ManCo\'s sole member is Ardent Capital Holdings LLC, as described below.

--

The following entities are related to ManCo and are material to the restructuring:

**Ardent Capital Partners III LP** (the \"Fund\"). The Fund is a Delaware limited partnership, EIN 84-3291057, formed for the purpose of making private equity investments primarily in middle-market and upper-middle-market companies across a range of sectors. The Fund held its final closing on April 15, 2019, at which time aggregate capital commitments totaled approximately \$2.8 billion from 47 limited partners. The Fund\'s limited partner base includes public pension funds, endowments, insurance companies, family offices, fund-of-funds vehicles, and sovereign wealth entities. As of September 30, 2023, the Fund maintained 11 active portfolio company investments. The Fund\'s term expires on December 31, 2029, subject to two one-year extension options exercisable at the discretion of the general partner. The investment period under the Fund\'s LPA commenced on June 30, 2019 and is scheduled to expire on June 30, 2025.

**Ardent Capital GP III LLC** (the \"GP\"). The GP is a Delaware limited liability company, EIN 84-3291063, which serves as the sole general partner of the Fund. The GP maintains a 1.5% general partner commitment to the Fund, representing \$42,000,000 in aggregate committed capital. The GP\'s registered agent is Prestige Registered Agents LLC, located at 850 New Burton Road, Suite 201, Dover, Delaware 19904. Prior to the restructuring, the GP was owned directly by five individual members (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao). Following the restructuring, the GP\'s sole member is Ardent GP Intermediate LLC.

--

**Heathrow Whitman & Co.** --- Auditor and tax advisor to the Fund and related entities. The engagement partner at Heathrow Whitman is Paul Devereux, CPA, located at 1345 Avenue of the Americas, 18th Floor, New York, New York 10105. Heathrow Whitman was consulted regarding the tax reporting implications of the restructuring, including Schedule K-1 changes, the carry reallocation mechanics, the treatment of departing principal interests, and the timing of entity-level tax filings. Coordination with Heathrow Whitman was primarily conducted by Sylvia Hartwell.

**Broadleaf Consulting Group** --- Valuation advisor to the Fund. The lead contact at Broadleaf is Martin Schreiber, located at 125 High Street, Suite 2800, Boston, Massachusetts 02110. Broadleaf\'s involvement in this engagement was limited; the firm\'s most recent quarterly valuation as of September 30, 2023 was referenced in the LPAC Presentation Memorandum and in the determination of accrued carried interest amounts.

**Lockwood Placement Partners LLC** --- Placement agent retained in connection with the fundraising for Fund III. The lead contact is Sarah Fontaine, located at 399 Park Avenue, Suite 3100, New York, New York 10022. Certain tail-fee obligations owed by ManCo to Lockwood remain in effect in accordance with the terms of the placement agent agreement. No action was required from Calderwood & Harkness with respect to the Lockwood arrangement, and the tail-fee obligations were unaffected by the restructuring.

--

**Second Amended and Restated LLC Agreement --- Ardent Capital Management LLC.** This agreement amends and restates the prior LLC Agreement of ManCo to reflect: (i) the admission of HoldCo as the sole member of ManCo (replacing the five individual principals); (ii) revised management fee profit distribution provisions to accommodate the pass-through of profit distributions to HoldCo for further allocation among the HoldCo members; (iii) updated key-personnel provisions reflecting the restructured ownership; and (iv) updated regulatory compliance provisions, including provisions addressing ManCo\'s obligations as an SEC-registered investment adviser. The agreement became effective February 28, 2024.

**Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership --- Ardent Capital Partners III LP.** This amendment to the Fund\'s LPA was prepared to reflect the restructuring at the Fund level. The amendment: (i) amends certain defined terms to reflect the new holding company structure and the departure of Kellner and Trask; (ii) updates the GP commitment provisions to address the assumption of the departing principals\' unfunded commitment obligations (\$3,402,000 in aggregate); and (iii) makes conforming changes to Sections 5.2 (Key Person provisions), 8.3 (GP Removal and Replacement), and 9.4 (Amendments and Consents). The amendment was executed as of February 28, 2024, following receipt of LPAC consent on February 14, 2024, as required under LPA Section 9.4.

**Member Consent Resolutions --- Ardent Capital GP III LLC.** Written resolutions dated February 28, 2024, evidencing the unanimous written consent of all five then-current members of the GP (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao) to: (i) approve the restructuring transactions and the formation of the holding company structure; (ii) authorize the withdrawal of Kellner and Trask as members of the GP; (iii) authorize the admission of GP Intermediate as the sole member of the GP; and (iv) authorize the execution and delivery of all restructuring documents by the GP.

--

*Note: Minor rounding adjustments were applied to Aldridge\'s assumed amount to ensure the total matched precisely.*

The GP commitment reallocation was documented in the Second Amended and Restated LLC Agreement of the GP, the Amendment No. 1 to the Fund\'s LPA, and the HoldCo LLC Agreement.

**3.3 Workstream III --- Departing Principal Separations**

--

**3.4 Workstream IV --- LP Consent, Notification & Side-Letter Compliance**

**3.4.1 LPAC Consent.** The Fund\'s LPA requires that certain amendments and structural changes receive the prior consent of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") pursuant to LPA Section 9.4. The LPAC for Fund III consists of four members, each representing a significant limited partner:

> • **Thomas Engström** --- Chief Investment Officer, Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System. Commitment: \$225,000,000.
>
--
>
> • **Catherine Whitfield** --- Managing Director, Graystone Family Office LLC. Commitment: \$50,000,000.

Calderwood & Harkness prepared and sent an LPAC notification and consent solicitation letter to each LPAC member on February 5, 2024. The letter was accompanied by a comprehensive **LPAC Presentation Memorandum** that summarized: (i) the rationale for the restructuring, including the planned departures of Kellner and Trask; (ii) the new entity structure, including organizational charts depicting the pre- and post-restructuring structures; (iii) the economics realignment, including updated carry and management fee profit share allocations; (iv) the key terms of the departing principal separation agreements; and (v) a confirmation that the restructuring does not constitute a Key Person Event under LPA Section 5.2, as neither Kellner nor Trask is a designated Key Person (only Aldridge and Narayanan hold that designation).

A virtual LPAC meeting was convened on February 14, 2024, during which the LPAC members had the opportunity to ask questions and discuss the restructuring with the remaining principals and Calderwood & Harkness. Following the meeting, LPAC consent was obtained in the form of a written consent executed by all four LPAC members, constituting the approval required under LPA Section 9.4 for the execution of Amendment No. 1 to the LPA.

**3.4.2 LP Notification.** Following the execution of all restructuring documents on February 28, 2024, the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate on March 1, 2024, and the filing of the SEC Form ADV amendment on March 10, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness prepared and sent LP notification letters to all 47 limited partners of the Fund on March 5, 2024. The notification letters informed the limited partners of:

--
>
> • The departures of David Kellner (retirement, effective March 31, 2024) and Joanna Trask (voluntary departure, effective April 15, 2024);
>
> • The receipt of LPAC consent on February 14, 2024;
>
> • The execution of Amendment No. 1 to the LPA; and
>
> • Confirmation that there is no change to: the Fund\'s investment strategy; management fee rates (1.75% on committed capital during the investment period, transitioning to 1.50% on invested capital post-investment period); or the Fund\'s term (December 31, 2029, with two one-year extension options).

--

> • **Most Favored Nation (MFN) Provisions (11 side letters):** Eleven of the 14 side letters contained MFN provisions entitling the relevant LP to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms subsequently granted to another LP. The restructuring did not implicate any MFN provisions, as no new side letter terms were granted to any LP in connection with the restructuring. No issues were identified.
>
> • **Expanded Key-Person Provisions (6 side letters):** Six side letters contained expanded key-person provisions that named David Kellner as a \"Contributing Person\" (a broader designation than the LPA\'s \"Key Person\" definition, which includes only Aldridge and Narayanan). Under these expanded provisions, Kellner\'s retirement triggers a notification obligation requiring ManCo to provide written notice to the affected LPs within fifteen (15) business days. Additionally, three of those six side letters (Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System, Pinnacle Insurance Group, and one additional LP) grant the affected LP the right to request a suspension of the investment period for up to ninety (90) days pending LPAC review. All required notifications were issued in connection with the LP notification process, and no LP elected to exercise the investment period suspension right.
>
> • **Fee discount/Rebate Provisions (8 side letters):** Eight side letters contained management fee discount or rebate provisions. The restructuring had no impact on these provisions, as management fee rates and the underlying fee structure were not altered.
>
--
>
> • **Updated Organizational Chart:** A revised organizational chart depicting the new holding company structure (HoldCo → ManCo; HoldCo → GP Intermediate → GP → Fund) was included in the filing.
>
> • **Updated Schedule D:** The private fund reporting section (Schedule D) for Ardent Capital Partners III LP was updated to reflect the restructured general partner and management company arrangements.

A **Summary of Changes Memorandum** was prepared by Stephen Adler documenting each material change reflected in the Form ADV amendment, the rationale for the change, and the specific sections of the Form ADV affected. This memorandum is preserved in the matter file for reference.

--

**3.6.1 Pemberton Hale LLP.** At the outset of the engagement, Nicholas Stern sent a letter (approximately October 2023) to Victoria Langford at Pemberton Hale LLP delineating the respective scopes of responsibility between the two firms. Under this arrangement:

> • **Calderwood & Harkness** was responsible for all restructuring-specific matters, including: the design and implementation of the holding company structure; all restructuring documentation (entity formation, governing document amendments, carry and economics agreements); all departing principal separation negotiations and documentation; LPAC consent solicitation and LP notifications relating to the restructuring; side-letter compliance analysis; and regulatory filings triggered by the restructuring.
>
> • **Pemberton Hale LLP** continued in its role as fund counsel for routine fund operations, including: portfolio company transactions; ongoing LP communications unrelated to the restructuring; compliance monitoring; and other day-to-day fund operation matters.

--

**3.6.2 Heathrow Whitman & Co.** Sylvia Hartwell sent an email (approximately February 2024) to Paul Devereux, the engagement partner at Heathrow Whitman & Co., outlining the tax reporting implications of the restructuring for all five entities in the Ardent Capital structure:

> • Ardent Capital Partners III LP (Fund) --- EIN 84-3291057
>
> • Ardent Capital GP III LLC (GP) --- EIN 84-3291063
>
--

**[5. Key Fund Performance Data (As of September 30, 2023)]{.underline}**

The following Fund performance data, as of September 30, 2023 (the most recent quarterly valuation date at the time of the restructuring), was referenced in the LPAC Presentation Memorandum and was relevant to the calculation of accrued carried interest and the economics of the departing principal separations:

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Metric**                                 **Amount**
--
  Accrued Carried Interest (Undistributed)   \$87,600,000
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

These figures were provided by Broadleaf Consulting Group (valuation advisor) and confirmed by Heathrow Whitman & Co. (auditor) in the ordinary course of the Fund\'s quarterly reporting process. Calderwood & Harkness did not independently verify these figures but relied upon them for purposes of the engagement and the preparation of the restructuring documents and LPAC materials.

The accrued carried interest of \$87,600,000 formed the basis for calculating the departing principals\' retained carry entitlements: Kellner at \$13,140,000 (100% of 15% of \$87,600,000) and Trask at \$6,307,200 (60% of 12% of \$87,600,000).

--

The identity and role of the GP remain unchanged; Ardent Capital GP III LLC continues to serve as the sole general partner of the Fund. The sole material change in Schedule D is the disclosure of the updated ownership chain above the GP, reflecting the interposition of GP Intermediate and HoldCo. No changes have been made to the Fund\'s strategy description, auditor, legal domicile, or other identifying information. No new private funds are being reported. The ManCo does not advise or sub-advise any additional funds beyond Ardent Capital Partners III LP.

**[III. Changes to Part 2A --- Firm Brochure]{.underline}**

--

> • Ardent Capital Management LLC is a Delaware limited liability company and is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company formed on March 1, 2024. Prior to February 28, 2024, the ManCo was directly owned by its individual principals.

The Fund pursues a strategy of making control investments in middle-market industrial and business-services companies in North America, targeting companies with enterprise values between \$200 million and \$750 million.
>
> • The Fund has total commitments of \$2.8 billion from 47 limited partners, of which approximately \$1.96 billion (approximately 70%) has been called as of the date of this filing. The Fund currently holds 11 active portfolio companies at various stages of value creation.
>
--

No substantive changes have been made to Item 6. The carried interest arrangement continues as described in Item 5 above: 20% of net profits, subject to an 8% preferred return (compounded annually) and a full catch-up provision. The carried interest is a performance-based fee within the meaning of the Advisers Act.

The only update to Item 6 relates to the internal allocation of carried interest among the principals. Following the Restructuring, the carried interest allocation percentages have been realigned to reflect the revised ownership structure within HoldCo and the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask. This internal reallocation is disclosed in Item 6 to the extent it reflects that the aggregate carried interest charged to the Fund remains unchanged --- no additional performance-based fee has been imposed on the Fund as a result of the Restructuring.

**D. Item 10: Other Financial Industry Activities and Affiliations**

Item 10 has been substantially revised to reflect the updated organizational structure. The prior disclosure described a flat ownership structure in which five individual principals directly held membership interests in both the ManCo and the GP. The updated disclosure describes the multi-tiered holding company structure established through the Restructuring.

The revised organizational chart disclosed in Item 10 is as follows:

> 1\. **IARD Filing.** The Form ADV amendment was filed via the IARD system on March 10, 2024. The filing is classified as an other-than-annual amendment, prompted by the change in control persons and organizational structure resulting from the Restructuring. The filing was made within the timeframe required by SEC rules, which generally require prompt amendment of Form ADV when information previously reported becomes materially inaccurate.
>
> 2\. **LPAC Consent.** Consent of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") of the Fund to the Restructuring was obtained on February 14, 2024, pursuant to Section 9.4 of the Fund\'s Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership, dated as of June 15, 2019 (the \"LPA\"). Section 9.4 of the LPA requires LPAC consent for any change in the control or ownership of the general partner or the investment adviser of the Fund. The LPAC consent was obtained by written action in lieu of meeting, with all five LPAC members voting in favor.
>
> 3\. **Execution of Restructuring Documents.** All documents effecting the Restructuring were executed on February 28, 2024, including: (i) the Certificate of Formation of HoldCo; (ii) the Operating Agreement of HoldCo; (iii) the Certificate of Formation of GP Intermediate; (iv) the Operating Agreement of GP Intermediate; (v) the Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of the ManCo; (vi) the Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of the GP; (vii) the Assignment and Assumption Agreements transferring the individual principals\' membership interests in the ManCo and the GP to HoldCo and GP Intermediate, respectively; (viii) the Kellner Retirement and Consulting Agreement; and (ix) the Trask Separation Agreement.
>
--
>
> 3\. **Form PF.** The ManCo\'s Form PF filing obligations are unaffected by the Restructuring. The ManCo is classified as a \"smaller private fund adviser\" for Form PF purposes (managing less than \$5 billion in private fund assets) and files Form PF on an annual basis. The most recent Form PF was filed for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022. The next filing, for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, is due within 120 days of fiscal year-end (i.e., by April 29, 2024). The organizational changes resulting from the Restructuring will be reflected in that filing as appropriate.
>
> 4\. **Placement Agent Disclosure.** Lockwood Placement Partners LLC (Sarah Fontaine, Managing Director) served as the exclusive placement agent for Fund III. The placement agent agreement with Lockwood remains in full force and effect, and any tail-fee obligations arising thereunder continue to be disclosed in Item 14 of Part 2A (Client Referrals and Other Compensation). The Restructuring does not affect the terms of the placement agent agreement or the ManCo\'s disclosure obligations with respect thereto. No amendment to Item 14 is required.
>
> 5\. **Side Letter Compliance.** The ManCo has reviewed the nine (9) side letters entered into with limited partners of the Fund and confirmed that the Restructuring does not trigger any additional obligations, consent requirements, or notification provisions beyond those already addressed through the LPAC consent process and the LP notification letters described in Section VI above. Certain side letters contain \"key person\" provisions naming Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan (and, in some cases, David Kellner); the departure of Mr. Kellner may implicate key person provisions in certain side letters, but this analysis is being conducted separately and is not within the scope of the Form ADV amendment.

**[I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") was engaged on June 11, 2024 by Driftwood Capital Management LLC (\"DCM\"), in its capacity as General Partner of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (\"DARF\" or the \"Fund\"), to advise on the legal implications of, and governance response to, a key-person event triggered by the sudden medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore, the Fund\'s founder, Chief Investment Officer, and sole designated Key Person under Section 8.04 of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership, dated as of March 15, 2017 (the \"A&R LPA\"). The engagement arose under circumstances requiring immediate attention: Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024, and the contractual Key Person Event was deemed triggered on June 10, 2024 upon expiration of the seven-consecutive-calendar-day threshold set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA, thereby suspending the Fund\'s Investment Period and initiating a 90-calendar-day Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024.

The scope of the engagement, as set forth in the engagement letter dated June 11, 2024, encompassed the following principal workstreams: (i) comprehensive analysis of Section 8.04 key-person clause mechanics and the contractual consequences flowing from the triggering event; (ii) preparation and review of the limited partner notification required under Section 8.04(c); (iii) development and recommendation of a successor governance framework, including the designation of successor Key Persons and the establishment of an Investment Committee; (iv) drafting and negotiation of the First Amendment to the A&R LPA (the \"First Amendment\") to implement the successor governance framework; and (v) solicitation and tabulation of limited partner consents as required under the A&R LPA for approval of the successor Key Persons and the related amendments.

All engagement objectives were achieved within the contractual Cure Period and in compliance with all applicable provisions of the A&R LPA, Delaware law, and Cayman Islands regulatory requirements. Thirty-eight (38) of the Fund\'s forty-seven (47) limited partners delivered written consents representing \$2,412.8 million of LP capital commitments, or approximately 86.2% of voting LP commitments --- well in excess of the 66⅔% supermajority threshold required under Section 8.04(c). The First Amendment to the A&R LPA became effective on August 26, 2024, designating Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons, establishing a three-member Investment Committee, transitioning Marcus J. Whitmore to a Senior Advisor role without governance authority, and implementing a revised carried interest allocation among the principals of DCM. The Cure Period deadline of September 8, 2024 was thereby mooted by the successful completion of the successor governance process thirteen (13) calendar days in advance.

The engagement is closed as of September 2, 2024. The matter status is: **closed_completed**. No outstanding legal issues, open work items, or continuing obligations of the Firm remain as of the date of this memorandum.

**[IV. BACKGROUND: THE KEY-PERSON EVENT]{.underline}**

--

Marcus J. Whitmore is the founder, Chief Investment Officer, and controlling Managing Member (90% membership interest) of Driftwood Capital Management LLC. Whitmore established DCM and the Fund in 2017 following a distinguished career spanning twenty-eight (28) years in multi-strategy institutional investing. Prior to founding DCM, Whitmore served as Managing Director and Head of Multi-Strategy Investing at Veltrano Asset Partners LLC from 2004 to 2016, where he oversaw a multi-billion-dollar allocation across equity long/short, event-driven, and credit strategies within the financial services sector. Before joining Veltrano, Whitmore served as a Portfolio Manager at Fieldstone Capital Advisors LP from 1996 to 2004, where he managed equity long/short portfolios focused on the banking and specialty finance sectors.

Whitmore was the sole designated \"Key Person\" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA. His designation as the sole Key Person reflected his central role in the Fund\'s investment process, including his direct management of the largest strategy books, his sole authority over portfolio construction and risk limits at the fund level, and his personal relationships with many of the Fund\'s largest institutional investors. Whitmore\'s capital commitment to the Fund was \$57.4 million, representing 2.0% of the Fund\'s assets under management as of May 31, 2024. His carried interest entitlement, prior to the amendment described herein, was 18% of the General Partner\'s 20% incentive allocation --- equivalent to 3.6% of the Fund\'s net new profits above the high-water mark.

**B. Incapacitation Event**

On June 3, 2024, Marcus J. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke at his residence in New York City. Whitmore was transported to Lenox Hill Medical Center in New York, where he was admitted for emergency treatment and subsequently commenced an intensive neurorehabilitation program. According to information conveyed to DCM by Whitmore\'s immediate family and treating physicians, the attending neurological team projected a minimum recovery period of twelve (12) to eighteen (18) months, with an uncertain prognosis regarding Whitmore\'s ability to return to full-time professional activity. As of the date of this memorandum, Whitmore remains in a rehabilitation setting and has not resumed any professional duties with respect to DCM or the Fund.

The severity and sudden onset of Whitmore\'s medical condition meant that no advance notice was given to DCM, the limited partners, or any service provider prior to the incapacitation. DCM\'s Deputy CIO, Elaine R. Sato, assumed day-to-day operational and investment management responsibilities for the Fund on an interim basis effective June 3, 2024, subject to the contractual constraints described below.

**C. Key-Person Event Trigger Analysis**

Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA provides, in relevant part, as follows:

> A \"Key Person Event\" shall be deemed to have occurred if a Key Person designated pursuant to Section 8.04(a) is \"unable to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Partnership for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days,\" absent the prior written notice of such Key Person delivered to the General Partner and each member of the Investor Advisory Committee setting forth the anticipated duration and reason for such absence.

No prior written notice was delivered by Whitmore, as his incapacitation was sudden and unexpected. The incapacitation commenced on June 3, 2024. The seven-consecutive-calendar-day period prescribed by Section 8.04(b) elapsed at 11:59 p.m. (Eastern Time) on June 9, 2024, and accordingly the Key Person Event was deemed triggered as of the close of business on June 10, 2024 (the first business day following the expiration of the seven-day period). The C&H engagement team confirmed this trigger date through a detailed analysis of the A&R LPA\'s definitions and day-count conventions, as set forth in the Key-Person Event Analysis Memorandum delivered to DCM on June 13, 2024.

**D. Contractual Consequences (Section 8.04(c))**

Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA imposed the following immediate and automatic consequences:

> \(i\) **Suspension of the Investment Period.** The Fund\'s Investment Period was immediately suspended. During the suspension, DCM was prohibited from making any new investments on behalf of the Fund. For purposes of this provision, a \"new investment\" was defined as any acquisition of a position not held in the Fund\'s portfolio as of the date of the Key Person Event.
>
--
>
> \(iv\) **Commencement of the 90-Day Cure Period.** A Cure Period of ninety (90) calendar days commenced on June 10, 2024, expiring on September 8, 2024. During the Cure Period, the General Partner was afforded the opportunity to propose one or more Successor Key Persons, subject to approval by limited partners holding not less than 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments (excluding the GP co-investment).
>
> \(v\) **Failure to Cure.** If no Successor Key Person was approved by the requisite supermajority of limited partners within the Cure Period, the A&R LPA provided that limited partners holding a majority-in-interest could elect either (a) to extend the Cure Period by up to ninety (90) additional calendar days, or (b) to commence an orderly wind-down of the Fund.

**E. LP Consent Voting Mechanics**

--
>
> • Required Consent Threshold (66⅔%): \$1,865,500,000

The foregoing calculation was confirmed in the Key-Person Event Analysis Memorandum and was consistent with the methodology specified in Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA for the computation of LP voting percentages.

**[V. DETAILED MATTER TIMELINE]{.underline}**

**A. Phase 1: Initial Response (June 10--17, 2024)**

**June 10, 2024 --- Key Person Event Deemed Triggered.** As described in Section IV.C above, the Key Person Event under Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA was deemed triggered as of June 10, 2024, upon expiration of the seven-consecutive-calendar-day period during which Whitmore was unable to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Fund. The Investment Period was automatically suspended, and the 90-calendar-day Cure Period commenced running.

**June 11, 2024 --- Engagement Opened.** Calderwood & Harkness LLP was formally engaged by DCM on June 11, 2024. The engagement letter was executed by Elaine R. Sato on behalf of DCM and by Graham Sutherland on behalf of C&H. Matter No. 1024-00002 was assigned. The engagement team was assembled immediately, and an initial conference call was held with Ms. Sato and DCM\'s General Counsel to receive a factual briefing on the circumstances of Whitmore\'s incapacitation and to discuss preliminary legal considerations.

**June 11--13, 2024 --- Legal Analysis and Internal Memorandum.** The C&H engagement team undertook a comprehensive analysis of the key-person clause mechanics under Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, the contractual consequences of the Key Person Event, and the applicable provisions of Delaware law governing limited partnerships. This analysis included a review of the entire A&R LPA, with particular focus on the definitions of \"Key Person,\" \"Key Person Event,\" \"Investment Period,\" \"Cure Period,\" and \"Successor Key Person,\" as well as the voting and consent provisions set forth in Article XIV. The team also analyzed the interplay between the key-person provisions and the Fund\'s investment management agreement and related side letters with certain institutional limited partners. The Key-Person Event Analysis Memorandum was prepared and delivered to DCM on June 13, 2024. The memorandum confirmed the trigger date, outlined the contractual consequences, identified the applicable deadlines, and set forth a recommended course of action for the Cure Period.

**June 14, 2024 --- LP Notification Letter.** The LP Notification Letter was finalized, reviewed, and approved by C&H. The letter was signed by Elaine R. Sato in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer of DCM and distributed to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund via email (with contemporaneous hard copy via overnight courier). The notification disclosed the following: (i) the occurrence of the Key Person Event; (ii) the nature of the triggering circumstance (medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore); (iii) the automatic suspension of the Investment Period; (iv) the follow-on investment cap of \$28.7 million; (v) the commencement of the 90-day Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024; and (vi) DCM\'s intention to propose Successor Key Persons during the Cure Period. The LP Notification Letter was sent three (3) business days in advance of the contractual deadline of June 17, 2024, ensuring full compliance with the timing requirements of Section 8.04(c).

**B. Phase 2: Successor Governance Framework Development (June 17--July 15, 2024)**

Following the delivery of the LP Notification Letter, the C&H engagement team commenced the development of a comprehensive successor governance framework. This workstream involved extensive consultation with Elaine R. Sato and other senior members of DCM\'s investment team, a review of industry best practices for key-person succession in institutional hedge fund structures, and an analysis of the expectations and concerns likely to be raised by the Fund\'s institutional limited partner base and the Investor Advisory Committee.

**Successor Governance Framework Memorandum.** C&H prepared and delivered to DCM a detailed Successor Governance Framework Memorandum setting forth the Firm\'s analysis and recommendations. The principal recommendations were as follows:

> \(a\) **Designation of Joint Successor Key Persons.** C&H recommended the designation of Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons under an amended Section 8.04. The recommendation was based on the complementary expertise and track records of the two individuals, their existing roles within DCM\'s investment process, and the need to demonstrate to the LP base that the Fund\'s multi-strategy mandate could be sustained without reliance on a single individual. The joint designation structure was also designed to address anticipated LP concerns regarding concentration of authority in a sole Key Person --- the very structure that had created the vulnerability exposed by Whitmore\'s incapacitation.
>
> \(b\) **Establishment of a Three-Member Investment Committee.** C&H recommended the creation of a formal Investment Committee under a new Section 8.05 of the A&R LPA. The Investment Committee was to be composed of three members: Sato (as Chair), Huang, and one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee. The inclusion of an IAC-designated independent member was intended to enhance governance credibility and LP confidence, and to provide an institutional check on investment decision-making in the absence of Whitmore.
>
> \(c\) **Revised Key-Person Clause Mechanics.** C&H recommended a revision to the key-person clause to reflect the joint designation structure. Specifically, the loss of one Successor Key Person would trigger a 180-day Replacement Period --- during which the remaining Successor Key Person and the Investment Committee could continue to manage the Fund --- rather than an automatic Investment Period suspension. Only the loss of both Successor Key Persons would trigger the automatic Investment Period suspension and standard cure mechanics previously applicable under Section 8.04. This tiered approach was designed to provide operational continuity while preserving meaningful LP protections.
>
> \(d\) **Reduced Follow-Onnder the laws of the State of Delaware, with its principal office located at 680 Lexington Avenue, 31st Floor, New York, NY 10022, and its Delaware registered agent at Capitol Registered Agents, Inc., 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, DE 19801. DCM serves as the sole general partner of the Partnership and, in such capacity, is responsible for the management, operation, and investment activities of the Partnership as set forth in the A&R LPA.

As of the date hereof, the Partnership has forty-seven (47) Limited Partners who have been admitted to the Partnership in accordance with the terms and conditions of the A&R LPA and the relevant subscription agreements. The General Partner confirms that no additional Limited Partners have been admitted, and no existing Limited Partners have withdrawn or been removed, since the date of the Key Person Event (as defined below).

**B. The Key Person Event.**

Pursuant to Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA, Marcus J. Whitmore, Founder, Chief Investment Officer, and Managing Member (holding 90% of the membership interests) of DCM, was designated as the sole \"Key Person\" of the Partnership. Section 8.04(a) provides, in relevant part, that the term \"Key Person\" shall mean \"Marcus J. Whitmore, individually, for so long as he serves as the Chief Investment Officer of the General Partner and devotes substantially all of his professional time to the investment activities and affairs of the Partnership.\"

On June 3, 2024, Mr. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke, resulting in his hospitalization and rendering him unable to devote substantially all of his professional time to the investment activities and affairs of the Partnership. Mr. Whitmore\'s medical condition, as confirmed by attending physicians at NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital / Weill Cornell Medical Center and communicated to the General Partner, has been such that he has been and remains unable to perform his duties as Chief Investment Officer or to participate in any material respect in the management, operation, or investment activities of the Partnership.

Pursuant to Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA, a \"Key Person Event\" is deemed to have occurred if the Key Person \"is unable to devote substantially all of his professional time to the affairs of the Partnership for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days, whether by reason of death, permanent disability, incapacitation, resignation, removal, or any other cause.\" The seven (7) consecutive calendar day period commenced on June 3, 2024 and expired on June 10, 2024. Accordingly, the Key Person Event was deemed triggered on June 10, 2024 (i.e., seven consecutive calendar days following June 3, 2024) (the \"Key Person Event Date\").

Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA provides that: (i) the Investment Period of the Partnership shall be automatically suspended; (ii) the General Partner shall not make any new portfolio investments on behalf of the Partnership, provided that the General Partner may make follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions in an aggregate amount not exceeding \$28.7 million (representing 1.0% of the Partnership\'s assets under management as of the most recent quarterly valuation); and (iii) a 90-calendar-day cure period (the \"Cure Period\") shall commence on the Key Person Event Date, during which the General Partner may propose one or more Successor Key Persons for approval by the Limited Partners. The Cure Period commenced on June 10, 2024 and was set to expire on September 8, 2024.

**C. LP Notification.**

Pursuant to Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, the General Partner was required to notify all Limited Partners in writing within five (5) business days of the occurrence of the Key Person Event. The Key Person Event occurred on June 10, 2024; accordingly, the notification deadline was June 17, 2024 (the fifth business day following June 10, 2024, accounting for the weekend of June 15--16, 2024).

The General Partner delivered written notice of the Key Person Event (the \"Key Person Event Notice\") to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners of the Partnership on June 14, 2024, which date was within the required five (5) business day notification period. The Key Person Event Notice was delivered by electronic mail transmission to the notice addresses on file for each Limited Partner, with a copy delivered by international courier (Granite Harbor Enterprises) to each Limited Partner\'s physical notice address, in each case as set forth in the records of the Partnership and in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 16.01 of the A&R LPA. The Key Person Event Notice described: (i) the nature of the Key Person Event; (ii) the suspension of the Investment Period; (iii) the restrictions on new portfolio investments; (iv) the commencement and expiration of the Cure Period; and (v) the General Partner\'s intention to propose one or more Successor Key Persons during the Cure Period.

**D. The Successor Proposal and the First Amendment.**

Following extensive consultations with the members of the Investor Advisory Committee (as described in Recital G below), the General Partner proposed Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons for the Partnership. Ms. Sato currently serves as Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (holding 10% of the membership interests) of DCM. She has been with DCM since its formation in 2015 and has been a senior member of the investment team throughout the life of the Partnership. Mr. Huang currently serves as Head of Credit Strategies of DCM. He joined DCM in 2017 and has served in roles of progressively increasing responsibility within the investment team, most recently overseeing all credit-related investment strategies of the Partnership.

On July 15, 2024, the General Partner circulated the following documents to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners of the Partnership, in each case by electronic mail transmission and international courier delivery in accordance with Section 16.01 of the A&R LPA:

> \(i\) a Successor Key Person Proposal letter, dated July 15, 2024, setting forth the qualifications, experience, and proposed roles of Ms. Sato and Mr. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons, together with biographical information and investment track records for each proposed Successor Key Person (the \"Successor Proposal\");
>
> \(ii\) a draft First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (the \"First Amendment\"), together with a blackline comparison to the A&R LPA showing all proposed amendments; and
>
> \(iii\) a Form of Written Consent of Limited Partners (the \"Form of Written Consent\"), to be executed and returned by each consenting Limited Partner on or before the LP Consent Deadline (as defined in Recital F below).

The First Amendment, among other things, provides for the following changes to the A&R LPA:

> \(a\) *Redefinition of \"Key Person.\"* Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA is amended to redefine \"Key Person\" to mean Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang, jointly, for so long as each of them serves in her or his respective capacity with the General Partner and devotes substantially all of her or his professional time to the investment activities and affairs of the Partnership.
>
> \(b\) *Replacement Period for Loss of One Successor Key Person.* Sections 8.04(b) and 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA are amended to provide that, in the event of the departure, death, permanent disability, incapacitation, or other loss of one (but not both) of the Successor Key Persons, a 180-calendar-day Replacement Period (rather than an automatic suspension of the Investment Period) shall be triggered, during which the remaining Successor Key Person and the General Partner shall identify and propose a replacement to the Limited Partners for approval. In the event of the departure, death, permanent disability, incapacitation, or other loss of both Successor Key Persons, a Key Person Event shall be deemed to have occurred, with consequences as previously provided in Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA.
>
> \(c\) *Establishment of Investment Committee.* A new Section 8.05 is added to the A&R LPA, establishing a three-member Investment Committee of the Partnership. The Investment Committee shall consist of: (1) Elaine R. Sato, who shall serve as Chair of the Investment Committee; (2) Jonathan K. Huang; and (3) one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee of the Partnership pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA. All new portfolio investments by the Partnership in excess of \$5.0 million shall require the approval of at least two (2) of the three (3) members of the Investment Committee. The Investment Committee shall meet no less frequently than bi-weekly during the first twelve (12) months following the Amendment Effective Date.
>
> \(d\) *Reduction of Follow-On Investment Cap.* The follow-on investment cap applicable during any future Key Person Event is reduced from \$28.7 million (representing 1.0% of the Partnership\'s assets under management) to \$14.35 million (representing 0.5% of the Partnership\'s assets under management), reflecting a more conservative posture during periods of leadership transition.
>
> \(e\) *Designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor.* Marcus J. Whitmore is designated as \"Senior Advisor\" to the Partnership and to the General Partner, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date. In such capacity, Mr. Whitmore shall have no governance authority, no voting rights with respect to any matter requiring the action or consent of the General Partner, and no authority to bind the Partnership or the General Partner. Mr. Whitmore\'s role as Senior Advisor shall be limited to providing non-binding advisory input on investment matters, to the extent his health permits, and shall be subject to the terms and conditions of a separate Senior Advisor Agreement between Mr. Whitmore and DCM.
>
> \(f\) *Amendment to Schedule A (Carried Interest Allocation).* Schedule A to the A&R LPA is amended to reflect the following revised allocations of the General Partner\'s 20% incentive allocation (i.e., the \"Carried Interest\"):
>
> • Marcus J. Whitmore: 9% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (reduced from 18%);
>
--

**E. Consent Requirement.**

Pursuant to Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, any amendment to the A&R LPA requires the written consent of the General Partner and of Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment). Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA further provides that the approval of Successor Key Persons and any related amendments to the A&R LPA shall be subject to the same consent threshold set forth in Section 14.01.

As of the Certification Date, the aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments for purposes of the consent vote (the \"Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments\") are calculated as follows:

--
>
> **Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments: \$2,798.25 million**

The capital commitments of Mr. Whitmore and Ms. Sato are excluded from the Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments because they were committed through the General Partner\'s co-investment vehicle and are therefore excluded pursuant to Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, which provides that \"for purposes of any vote or consent of the Limited Partners, the capital commitments of the General Partner and any Affiliate of the General Partner that are invested through the General Partner\'s co-investment shall be excluded from the denominator.\"

The required consent threshold is therefore:

**F. Consent Deadline.**

The General Partner established August 23, 2024 as the deadline by which all Forms of Written Consent were required to be received by the General Partner (the \"LP Consent Deadline\"). The LP Consent Deadline of August 23, 2024 represents forty (40) calendar days from the July 15, 2024 circulation date of the Successor Proposal, the First Amendment, and the Form of Written Consent. The forty-day consent period was determined by the General Partner to be reasonable and consistent with the time periods customarily afforded to Limited Partners in similar circumstances, and was within the Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024. The General Partner also delivered reminder notices to all Limited Partners who had not yet returned executed Forms of Written Consent on August 5, 2024 and August 12, 2024, respectively.

**G. IAC Review.**

The Investor Advisory Committee (the \"IAC\") of the Partnership, established pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA, consists of five (5) members, each of whom is a representative of a Limited Partner of the Partnership. As of the date hereof, the members of the IAC are as follows:

> 1\. Diana Cortland, Representative of Northvale Public Employees\' Retirement System --- IAC Chair;
>
> 2\. Richard Oshima, Representative of Sycamore Endowment Partners LP;
>
--
>
> 5\. Nadia Al-Rashid, Representative of Atlas Sovereign Wealth Advisory LLC.

The IAC reviewed the Successor Proposal, the First Amendment, and related materials at a meeting held on July 29, 2024, at the offices of Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, 51 West 52nd Street, 40th Floor, New York, NY 10019. The meeting was attended by all five IAC members (Ms. Cortland, Mr. Oshima, Ms. Mercer, Mr. Ashworth, and Ms. Al-Rashid) and by legal counsel to the IAC, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP (Helen M. Calloway, Partner, and David Pineda, Senior Associate). Also in attendance at the invitation of the IAC were Ms. Sato and Mr. Huang, who presented their qualifications, investment philosophy, and proposed governance structure, and responded to questions from the IAC members and their legal counsel. The IAC meeting lasted approximately three hours and forty-five minutes. Following the presentation and discussion, the IAC unanimously confirmed that it did not object to the Successor Proposal or the First Amendment, and that the IAC would recommend to the Limited Partners that they approve the same. The IAC\'s recommendation was communicated to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners by separate letter from Ms. Cortland, as IAC Chair, dated August 1, 2024.

**Section 2. Certification of Amendment Effectiveness.**

**2.1 Effectiveness of the First Amendment.** Having determined, as set forth in Section 1 above, that the requisite Limited Partner consent has been obtained in accordance with Sections 14.01 and 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, and having further confirmed that all other conditions precedent to the effectiveness of the First Amendment have been satisfied (including, without limitation, the execution and delivery of the First Amendment by the General Partner on behalf of the Partnership), the General Partner hereby certifies that the First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. is effective as of August 26, 2024 (the \"Amendment Effective Date\"). The A&R LPA, as modified by the First Amendment, shall hereinafter be referred to as the \"LPA\" or the \"Partnership Agreement,\" and all references in any agreement, instrument, document, or certificate to the \"A&R LPA\" or the \"Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement\" shall be deemed to refer to the A&R LPA as amended by the First Amendment, unless the context otherwise requires.

**2.2 Summary of Key Amendments Now in Effect.** As of the Amendment Effective Date, the following material amendments to the A&R LPA, as effected by the First Amendment, are now in full force and effect:

> \(a\) *Section 8.04(a) --- Redefinition of \"Key Person.\"* The term \"Key Person\" is redefined to mean Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang, jointly, for so long as each of them serves in her or his respective capacity with the General Partner and devotes substantially all of her or his professional time to the investment activities and affairs of the Partnership.
>

Loss of both Successor Key Persons triggers a Key Person Event with consequences as previously provided in Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA.
>
> \(c\) *New Section 8.05 --- Investment Committee.* A three-member Investment Committee is established, consisting of Elaine R. Sato (Chair), Jonathan K. Huang, and one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA. All new portfolio investments in excess of \$5.0 million require approval of at least two (2) of the three (3) members of the Investment Committee.
>
> \(d\) *Follow-On Investment Cap.* The follow-on investment cap applicable during any future Key Person Event is reduced from \$28.7 million (1.0% of assets under management) to \$14.35 million (0.5% of assets under management).
>
> \(e\) *Designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor.* Marcus J. Whitmore is designated as Senior Advisor to the Partnership and to the General Partner, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date, with no governance authority, no voting rights, and no authority to bind the Partnership or the General Partner.
>
> \(f\) *Schedule A --- Carried Interest Allocation.* The revised allocations of the General Partner\'s 20% incentive allocation are as follows:
>
--
>
> \(g\) *Whitmore Carried Interest Vesting.* Fifty percent (50%) of Mr. Whitmore\'s carried interest allocation vested immediately as of the Key Person Event Date (June 10, 2024). The remaining fifty percent (50%) vests ratably on a monthly basis over thirty-six (36) months commencing on June 10, 2024, subject to continued compliance by Mr. Whitmore with the non-competition and non-solicitation covenants set forth in the Operating Agreement of DCM and the Senior Advisor Agreement.

**2.3 Cure Period.** The 90-calendar-day Cure Period under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA commenced on the Key Person Event Date of June 10, 2024 and was set to expire on September 8, 2024. The effectiveness of the First Amendment on the Amendment Effective Date of August 26, 2024 --- which date is thirteen (13) calendar days prior to the expiration of the Cure Period --- constitutes a cure of the Key Person Event within the Cure Period, in accordance with Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA. Accordingly, the September 8, 2024 Cure Period expiration date is rendered moot.

Furthermore, the suspension of the Investment Period that took effect automatically upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event on June 10, 2024, pursuant to Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, is hereby terminated as of the Amendment Effective Date of August 26, 2024. **1.1 Description of the Engagement**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H,\" \"we,\" \"our,\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm our engagement by Briarwood Family Office LLC (\"BFO\" or the \"Client\"), a Delaware limited liability company, to serve as legal counsel in connection with the negotiation and documentation of a side letter (the \"Side Letter\") to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership dated December 20, 2023 (the \"LPA\") of Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. (\"Fund IV\"), a Delaware limited partnership, in connection with a proposed capital commitment of Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000) by BFO as a limited partner of Fund IV.

Fund IV is managed by Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC (the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company and the sole general partner of Fund IV. The General Partner is a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"MPCA\"), a Delaware limited liability company registered as an investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended, with its principal office located at 200 Clarendon Street, 42nd Floor, Boston, MA 02116. We understand that the placement agent for Fund IV is Pinnacle Capital Markets LLC (\"Pinnacle\"), a FINRA-registered broker-dealer, and that the fund administrator is Granite Ledger Fund Services LLC (\"Granite Ledger\").

--

The scope of our engagement includes the following services:

> \(a\) **Review and Analysis of Governing Documents.** Review and analysis of the Fund IV LPA (dated December 20, 2023) and the Fund IV Private Placement Memorandum (dated December 15, 2023) (the \"PPM\"), including identification of key terms, risk factors, fee structures, governance provisions, withdrawal and redemption mechanics, and provisions that may be subject to negotiation, modification, or supplementation via side letter.
